# The Comprehensive Irad Wiki Encyclopedia (Volume 3: Start and Stub Articles)

The **Irad Wiki** is a collaboratively edited encyclopedia of the Republic of Irad (Iradistan). This volume collects start-class and stub articles: shorter entries on settlements, landforms, institutions, people, wildlife and vocabulary, many of which await expansion by editors.

---

## 5. Start-Class Articles (242 Entries)

### 5.Category: Biographies & Leadership (41 articles)

#### 1. Mar Timotheos Alimbekov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Mar Timotheos Alimbekov** (1869–1938) was a bishop of the Iradi church who negotiated its union with Rome. Under the bull *Orientalis Stella*, issued by [[wp:Pope Pius XI]] on 14 September 1931, the church was received into full communion as the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]], an Eastern Catholic church *sui iuris* that kept its East Syriac rite, and Iyık Janyl became its metropolitan see. Timotheos became its first archbishop. He was arrested during [[The 1937 NKVD Clerical Purges|the purges of 1937]] and, according to church records, died in custody the following year.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## Early life and episcopate
Timotheos was born in [[Iyık Janyl]] and studied [[wp:Syriac language|Classical Syriac]] and scripture with the clergy of the [[Church of St. Janyl]]. Church biographies state that as a young man he spent several years among the East Syriac communities of Urmia in Persia, where he met Catholic missionaries. He was consecrated bishop of Iyık Janyl before the [[wp:World War I|First World War]] and led the church through the [[Semirechye Revolt (Irad)|1916 revolt]] and the [[wp:Russian Civil War]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Union with Rome
Soviet rule made open contact with Rome impossible. From 1926 Timotheos corresponded with the [[wp:Holy See]] through intermediaries at papal nunciatures abroad; church histories name contacts in [[wp:Istanbul]] and Tehran. His surviving letters, held in the diocesan archives, ask for recognition of the church's Syriac liturgy, its synodal government and its own calendar, including the feast of St. Janyl. The negotiations lasted five years and ended with the bull of 1931. The bull was not published in the [[wp:Soviet Union]], and news of it reached the parishes by word of mouth.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Soviet response and death
Soviet authorities treated the union as evidence that the church answered to a foreign power. Officials linked the Vatican, which had concluded the [[wp:Lateran Treaty]] with [[wp:Italy]] in 1929, with "fascist" influence, and historians connect this suspicion with the severity of anti-religious repression in the [[Iradi Soviet Socialist Republic|Iradi SSR]] during the 1930s. The churches of Iyık Janyl were closed and the cathedral became a grain store. Timotheos was arrested in 1937 together with his senior clergy, most of whom were executed. The security service file on his case has not been published, and his place of burial is unknown.<sup>[2]</sup>

The Church of St. Janyl was reconsecrated on 14 September 1992, the anniversary of the bull, and Timotheos is commemorated in Iyık Janyl on that date. The historian and politician [[Amanbek Alimbekov]] was a member of the same family.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 2. Tilek Kurmanov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Tilek Kurmanov** (born 1953) is an Iradi diplomat who represented the government of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) at the United Nations from 2008 to 2017. Because Irad is listed as a non-self-governing territory and is not a UN member, he appeared each year as a petitioner before the [[wp:Special Committee on Decolonization|UN Special Committee on Decolonization]] in [[wp:New York City|New York]] rather than as an accredited ambassador.<sup>[1]</sup>

A graduate of the [[wp:Moscow State Institute of International Relations]] (1976), Kurmanov served in the Soviet foreign service before returning to [[Talas]] in 1992. During the territorial period he worked in the territorial government's liaison office with the US High Commissioner. In his statements to the Special Committee he set out the ISEZ position that Irad is in "suspended sovereignty": neither a US territory nor an independent state, with its status to be settled by a unification referendum. He opposed proposals to remove Irad from the list before such a vote, and he rejected the *de jure* claims of [[wp:Kazakhstan]], [[wp:Uzbekistan]] and [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]]. Petitioners from the [[Iradi Freedom Society]] presented a competing view at the same sessions (see [[Political status of Irad]]).<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 3. Gulnara Sadyk
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Gulnara Sadyk** (born 1974) is an Iradi human rights lawyer based in [[Talas]]. She founded the Legal Defense Guild, which gives free legal representation to journalists, students and others detained in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], and her reports on political detentions have been cited by international monitors.<sup>[1]</sup>

Sadyk studied law at [[Talas State University]] and took a master's degree in human rights law at Central European University in Budapest in 2001. She founded the Legal Defense Guild in Talas in 2009. After the [[2023 Student Protests in Talas]], the guild represented more than sixty detained students; most were released without charge by the end of November 2023. Its reports on pre-trial detention have been cited by the human rights unit of the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]] and by [[wp:Human Rights Watch]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> In 2021 the Ministry of Internal Security audited the guild's foreign grants. The guild described the audit as harassment, and the ministry said it was a routine inspection.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 4. Muratbek Tanıp-Biy
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

{{Hatnote|Not to be confused with [[Muratbek Biy]], an 18th-century clan leader.}}

**Muratbek Tanıp-Biy** (c. 1805 – 1874) was a chieftain (*biy*) of the Tanıp clan in the [[Talas Alatau]]. He led the northern Iradi clans during the mid-19th-century frontier conflicts between the [[wp:Khanate of Kokand]] and the [[wp:Russian Empire]], and he is remembered for negotiating pasture settlements between rival clans. According to the Tanıp genealogy (*[[Sanjyra (Genealogy)|sanjyra]]*), the present chieftain, [[Bektur Zhumabek uulu]], descends from him in the male line.<sup>[1]</sup>

Most of what is known about him comes from the *sanjyra* and from a few Russian frontier reports of the 1860s that mention "Muratbek, biy of the Tanyp". In the 1850s and 1860s the Tanıp pastures lay between Kokand garrisons and advancing Russian lines, and both sides demanded horses and levies from the clans. Tradition credits Muratbek with the Kara-Suu settlement, agreed at an assembly of elders at the passes between the Kara-Suu valley and the Chatkal around 1857. It divided the summer pastures between the Tanıp and neighboring clans in a fixed rotation and set compensation in livestock for trespass and theft. Clan councils and the [[Autonomous Tribal Grazing Arbitration Tribunal]] still cite the settlement as a precedent in disputes under customary law (*adat*).<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 5. David Sterling
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**David Sterling** (born 1946) is a retired [[wp:United States Army]] colonel who was the first US military liaison officer in [[Talas]] during [[Operation Starlight]] in 1992.<sup>[1]</sup>

A Russian-speaking foreign area officer, Sterling arrived with the first [[wp:United States Marine Corps|US Marines]] airlifted into the airfield west of Talas on 6 June 1992, during the final weeks of the siege of the city. He coordinated the defense of the perimeter between the Marines, Provisional Government units and the mounted clan irregulars of [[Kuban Mamytov]] and [[Bektur Zhumabek uulu]] until the siege lines were broken by 18 June. Provisional Government minutes record him attending its defense council from 7 June.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> He then headed the US military liaison office in Talas until 1994 and worked on the first plans to expand [[Talas Air Base]] into a permanent installation. He retired from the Army in 1998.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 6. Kanybek Zhumaliev
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Kanybek Zhumaliev** (1947–2016) was an Iradi lawyer and politician who was Speaker of the Territorial House of Representatives from 1994 to 1998. He sponsored the Commercial Property and Tenure Acts of 1995.<sup>[1]</sup>

A collective-farm lawyer in the Talas valley in the Soviet period, Zhumaliev joined the reformist caucus of the Provisional Government in 1992 and was a founding member of the [[Democratic Party of Irad]] that October. He was elected to the House of Representatives in the first territorial elections in 1994 and chosen as Speaker. The 1995 acts protected household livestock and family grazing rights from seizure for debt, and they required foreign joint ventures to register land leases and ownership stakes with the territorial government. Herders' groups later argued that the acts protected household herds but left communal clan pastures without legal protection, a gap that became an issue in the [[Privatization Scandals of 2007]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 7. Chingiz Asanov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Chingiz Asanov** (born 1963) is an Iradi mining engineer who has been Minister of Natural Resources of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] since 2016. His ministry issues mining leases, sets royalties and negotiates long-term supply contracts with Chinese buyers of [[Antimony Mining in Irad|antimony]].<sup>[1]</sup>

Asanov trained as a mining engineer at the Frunze Polytechnic Institute and worked at the [[Sary-Bulak Antimony Works]] from 1985, becoming its chief engineer in 2001. He was appointed deputy minister in 2009. As minister he introduced a revised royalty schedule for stibnite concentrate in 2018 and added tailings-safety conditions to the leases of the [[Sary-Bulak]] mines and the [[Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex]]. Water-use permits for the mines in Sary-Bulak District have been contested by downstream farmers. Licenses his ministry has issued in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] cannot be used there, because the clan councils ban open-pit mining in mountain watersheds.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

In October 2026 Asanov announced the completion of a refit of the four generating units of the [[Toktogul Hydroelectric Complex]], which raised its capacity from 1,200 MW to 1,440 MW. He reviewed the work at the Lower Naryn switchyard and the National Dispatch Center with members of the joint technical commission of the [[Naryn Water and Power Protocol]], in the presence of Uzbek, Kazakh and Kyrgyz observers. The ministry has not published the cost of the refit, and it has said that the division of the additional export revenue is a matter for the talks on the 2027 release schedule.<sup>[3]</sup><sup>[4]</sup>

#### 9. Samat Kasymov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Samat Kasymov** (born 1968) is an Iradi telecommunications engineer who has been Director-General of [[Attelkom]], the largest telecommunications company in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], since 2013.<sup>[1]</sup>

Kasymov studied radio engineering at the Kobozev Polytechnic Institute (now the [[Nurzhan Polytechnic Institute]]) and joined Attelkom in 1997 as an engineer on its first GSM network in [[Talas]]. He became its technical director in 2008. Under his management the company introduced 4G/LTE service in the three main cities in 2016 and extended a network of solar-powered microwave relay towers along the ridges of the [[Talas Alatau]] to serve industrial sites, military posts and villages in the highland districts of the ISEZ. Attelkom has almost no service in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]].<sup>[1]</sup> In October 2023 the company cut mobile data in central Talas for three days during the student protests. Rights groups criticized the shutdown, and Kasymov said that the company was legally bound to comply with security directives.<sup>[2]</sup>

In June 2026 Attelkom moved its international traffic to new gateway equipment bought with Chinese export credit, which it described as network modernization; Iradi websites, largely absent from foreign search results since the 2023 shutdown, reappeared in them over the following weeks.<sup>[3]</sup> In October 2026 the company blocked the websites of the cryptocurrency [[Tulparcoin]], on a list supplied by the Department of Public Information, but not the Tulpar app.<sup>[4]</sup> On 19 October 2026 Kasymov accompanied Lieutenant Governor [[Aidar Maksat]] on a visit to the site of the planned Nurzhan Compute Park, a data-center hub in the eastern industrial zone of [[Nurzhan]] that is to be linked by fiber to the [[Attelkom Data Center]] in Talas (see [[Energy in Irad]]).<sup>[5]</sup> The next day he announced that Attelkom's first fiber route to China, through Kyrgyzstan to [[wp:Kashgar]], was carrying traffic, and described it as a commercial capacity purchase.<sup>[6]</sup>

#### 10. Biybolot Moldosh uulu
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Biybolot Moldosh uulu** (born 1944; recorded in Soviet documents as Biybolot Moldoshev) is an elder (*[[Aksakal (Social Term)|aksakal]]*) of the Karakoyun clan of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] and a mediator in disputes along the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]].<sup>[1]</sup>

He comes from the [[Kara-Koyun Valley]], the clan's ancestral homeland, and is known for his knowledge of the clans' oral genealogies (*[[Sanjyra (Genealogy)|sanjyra]]*). He was a member of the [[Iradi Freedom Society]] delegation at the [[2011 Bilateral Reunification Summit]], which walked out after the tribal regions were offered one-third of the seats in a unified legislature. Since 2008 he has attended the monthly meetings of the Joint Liaison Committee at Kara-Oi as an adviser to the tribal delegation. In 2014 he negotiated the release of three ISEZ survey workers held by [[El-Choro Militias|El-Choro]] patrols in the Kara-Koyun Valley.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Mar Ephrem** (born 1955) is the Archbishop of [[Iyık Janyl]] and primate of the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]]. He was proposed by the [[Syro-Iradi Council of Hierarchs]] and appointed by the [[wp:Holy See]] in 2012, succeeding Mar Yuhanna Bakirov, archbishop since 1992, and was enthroned at the [[Church of St. Janyl]].<sup>[1]</sup>

Born in the Talas valley, he was ordained in secret in 1981, when the church still had no legal existence in the Iradi SSR. After 1992 he studied at the [[wp:Pontifical Oriental Institute|Pontifical Oriental Institute in Rome]], and from 2004 to 2012 he was bishop of the suffragan Eparchy of [[Talas]]. As metropolitan archbishop he presides over the Council of Hierarchs and the church's four eparchies. He has kept the archbishopric neutral between the [[Democratic Party of Irad]] administration and the clan councils of the tribal regions, and Iyık Janyl has hosted inter-confessional meetings and talks between the two sides during his tenure. He has also maintained the itinerant priests who celebrate the liturgy in tent chapels in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 12. Dastan Isakov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Dastan Isakov** (born 1946) is an Iradi jurist who was Chief Justice of the [[Supreme Court of Irad]] from 1999 to 2007. He wrote the majority opinion in the [[Statutory Independence Ruling (2006)|Statutory Independence Ruling]] of December 2006, which led to the proclamation of the [[Democratic Republic of Irad]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Career
Isakov graduated from the law faculty of Kazakh State University in [[wp:Almaty|Alma-Ata]] in 1969 and worked as a state arbitration lawyer in Kobozev. He was among the first justices appointed to the Supreme Court when it was established under the [[Organic Act of the Territory of Irad]] in November 1992. In 1999 the Governor named him Chief Justice with the consent of the Territorial Senate.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Statutory Independence Ruling
On 3 December 2006, President George W. Bush withdrew the United States from the [[Alimbekov-Baker Treaty]] by executive action. Within days, on an emergency petition brought by [[Bakyt Orozbekov]], the court held that territorial status had lapsed upon federal disengagement. Isakov's majority opinion reasoned that the treaty's statutory independence clause, carried into the Organic Act, had then taken effect and vested sovereignty in the people of Irad. The reasoning became known as the doctrine of automatic reversion. On the strength of the ruling, the Territorial Legislature proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Irad on 9 December.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

On 25 February 2007, [[Erlan Toktarov]] proclaimed the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] and annulled the ruling by decree. The court never ruled on the annulment. After DPI forces took control of [[Talas]] in the summer of 2007, the emergency administration reconstituted the bench, and Isakov left the court that year. He has held no public office since and has given few interviews.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 13. Elena Petrova
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Elena Petrova** (born 1957) is a trade unionist and municipal politician in [[Nurzhan]] who represents the city's Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking industrial workforce. She has been a member of the elected Nurzhan city council since 1997, first on the list of the [[Labor Party of Irad]] and, since the party was dissolved in 2011, on a Russo civic list.<sup>[1]</sup>

Petrova worked as a crane operator at the Kobozev Tractor Combine from 1976 and became a shop-floor organizer in its trade union in the late 1980s. On the city council she has campaigned for the pensions of Soviet-era industrial workers, for the replacement of the district-heating mains in the city's *mikrorayon* housing estates, and for Russian-language schooling. Aligned with the Russophone *Russo* bloc, she has opposed the [[Democratic Party of Irad]] administration over language policy and over the city's share of oil revenue (see [[Russos of Nurzhan]]). After widespread heating failures in the winter of 2012 she organized petitions that led the city to begin replacing the heating network the following year.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 14. Mirlan Toktarov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Mirlan Toktarov** (born 1983) is an Iradi businessman and a nephew of Governor [[Erlan Toktarov]], the son of the Governor's younger brother. Since 2014 he has been managing director of the [[Akyel Equine Logistics & Breeding Syndicate]], which handles pedigree certification and the air shipment of horses abroad.<sup>[1]</sup>

Toktarov studied business administration in [[Talas]] and worked in the family's freight interests before joining the syndicate in 2009 as head of its export division. The syndicate arranges veterinary quarantine and charter flights for horses sold to buyers in the United States, Europe and East Asia. Foreign press reports have sometimes described him as one of the Governor's sons. The Governor's children are his five sons, [[Ruslan Toktarov|Ruslan]], [[Alikhan Toktarov|Alikhan]], [[Timur Toktarov|Timur]], [[Adil Toktarov|Adil]] and [[Bekzat Toktarov|Bekzat]], and his daughter [[Zara Toktarova|Zara]]; Mirlan is their cousin.<sup>[1]</sup> Critics of the administration cite his appointment, together with the business roles of the Governor's sons, as an example of the family's influence over the ISEZ economy.<sup>[2]</sup>

In 2022 Toktarov spoke for the syndicate in the Kyzyl-Jyldyz pedigree fraud case. In March 2022 a retest ordered by an American buyer of a palomino [[Akyel Horse|Akyel]] colt showed that a breeder with a stud near Talas had substituted DNA samples for 14 foals between 2017 and 2021, with the help of a technician at the [[Talas Veterinary Research Center]]. The syndicate struck 31 horses from its register and exports to the United States were suspended for four months. In June 2023 the [[Talas District Court]] sentenced the breeder to four years in prison, reduced to three on appeal, for fraud and forged veterinary papers. A review by the syndicate found no irregularities at its own farms, and it moved its DNA testing abroad in 2023.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 15. Kuban Mamytov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

{{Infobox person

**Kuban Mamytov** (1949–2013), also known by the patronymic form Kuban Mamyt uulu, was a commander of mounted clan irregulars in the [[First Iradi Civil War]]. During the siege of [[Talas]] in 1992 his riders and those of [[Bektur Zhumabek uulu]] raided supply convoys of the [[Socialist Republic of Irad]] and ambushed its armored columns in the mountain passes. Veterans called him "the Ghost of Chatkal".<sup>[1]</sup>

Mamytov was a herder from the Chatkal valley and a veteran of the [[wp:Soviet Army]]. During the [[Winter Uprising of 1992]] he led riders from the Chatkal clans into Talas. When socialist forces besieged the city from April 1992, the Provisional Government placed him in command of the mounted irregulars defending its southern approaches. His men attacked depots along the railway and kept open the mountain tracks by which supplies reached the city from the southern valleys.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> Military historians regard the irregulars' contribution as secondary to the US intervention, [[Operation Starlight]], which broke the siege in June 1992.<sup>[2]</sup>

After US forces disarmed the militias in August 1992, Mamytov returned to herding in the Chatkal, and in 1994 he declined a commission in the newly organized Irad National Guard. At his funeral in 2013 his horse was led behind the bier with its saddle reversed, in keeping with the [[Fallen Rider Tradition]].<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 17. Nikolai Voronov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

{{Hatnote|Not to be confused with the Soviet artillery commander [[wp:Nikolay Voronov|Nikolai Nikolayevich Voronov]].}}

**Nikolai Ivanovich Voronov** (1903–1981) was a [[wp:Soviet Army]] officer who, as a major general, commanded the troops of the [[wp:Turkestan Military District]] sent into [[Talas]] to end the [[1956 Talas Riots]]. He served as military commandant of the city under the martial law and curfew declared on 17 June 1956.<sup>[1]</sup>

Voronov's units entered Talas on the morning of 17 June, the fourth day of the riots, with internal troops flown in to the air-defense airfield outside the city. Armored vehicles were posted at the main intersections around Government Square, and the last crowds dispersed on 18 June. Internal security reports listed 14 dead; Iradi researchers put the number at several dozen. More than 1,000 people were detained in the following weeks.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> He retired from the army in 1963. In memoirs published in 1990, Voronov acknowledged that the use of troops and the mass detentions that followed had turned much of the Iradi population of the city against the authorities.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 18. Azamat Temirov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Azamat Temirov** (born 1969) is an Iradi economist who has been chairman of the [[Bank of Irad]], the monetary authority of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], since 2010.<sup>[1]</sup>

Under the Banking and Commercial Currency Act of 1993, the US dollar is legal tender in Irad and the [[Iradi som]] circulates alongside it for retail payments, utility bills and public-sector wages. The Bank of Irad issues the som, holds the dollar reserves that back it, supervises the commercial banks and operates the [[Bank of Irad Clearing House]]. Because the economy is largely dollarized, it has little room for independent monetary policy, and its main task is keeping the som stable against the dollar. Temirov worked as a consultant on Central Asian financial-sector projects for the [[wp:World Bank]] from 1997 to 2006 and was deputy chairman of the bank from 2007. Since non-recognition limits Irad's access to international clearing systems, he has overseen the correspondent banking arrangements in [[wp:Almaty]] and [[wp:Istanbul]] on which Iradi banks rely.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 19. Kanatbek Niyaz uulu
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Kanatbek Niyaz uulu** (born 1950; recorded in Soviet documents as Kanatbek Niyazov) is a customary-law judge who presides over hearings under *[[Adat (Customary Law)|adat]]* in the high valleys of the Chatkal range, in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]].<sup>[1]</sup>

Clan councils in the Chatkal Highlands refer disputes over livestock, pasture boundaries and grazing rotations to him. He also sits as one of the elders of the [[Autonomous Tribal Grazing Arbitration Tribunal]]. His judgments are given orally and usually order restitution in livestock (*kun*) rather than punishment. In 2016 he settled a dispute between two clans over shared summer pastures with a rotation agreement that both clan councils accepted.<sup>[1]</sup> Human rights organizations have criticized the *adat* system in which he works, noting that women have limited standing before clan councils and that there is no appeal beyond the clan assembly.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 24. Sergei Nechayev (Iradi Influence)
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

{{Infobox person
| name = Sergey Nechayev
| df = dmy
| native_name = Сергей Геннадиевич Нечаев
| image = Sergey_Nechayev.jpg
| caption = Sergey Nechayev
| birth_date = 1847-10-02
| birth_place = [[wp:Ivanovo]], [[wp:Russian Empire]]
| death_date = 1882-12-03
| death_place = [[wp:Peter and Paul Fortress]], [[wp:Saint Petersburg]], Russian Empire
| occupation = Revolutionary
| known_for = *[[wp:Catechism of a Revolutionary]]* (1869)
}}

**Sergei Nechayev** (Sergey Gennadiyevich Nechayev, 1847–1882) was a Russian revolutionary associated with the *Catechism of a Revolutionary* (1869), a manifesto of conspiratorial revolution whose authorship is sometimes shared with [[wp:Mikhail Bakunin]]. He died in prison in [[wp:Saint Petersburg|St. Petersburg]]. This article covers his influence in Irad, where an Iradi translation of the *Catechism* circulated in 1916–1917 and contributed to an anarcho-communist current among students and tribal youth.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## In Irad
The Iradi translation was an abridged version of the *Catechism*, probably made from a Russian text brought from [[wp:Tashkent]]. The translator is unknown. The earliest surviving copy, a lithographed pamphlet in Arabic-script Iradi, is held in the [[State Archives of Irad]]. It circulated among students in [[Talas]] and [[wp:Khanate of Kokand|Kokand]] and among young men of the clans during and after the [[Semirechye Revolt (Irad)|revolt of 1916]]. Its readers combined Nechayev's call for revolutionary discipline with the clans' traditions of communal decision-making and resistance to empire.<sup>[2]</sup>

After the [[wp:October Revolution]] most Iradi clans sided with the [[wp:Bolsheviks]], and Iradi irregulars fought alongside the [[wp:Red Guards (Russia)|Red Guards]] who crushed the [[wp:Turkestan Autonomy|Kokand Autonomy]] in February 1918. Soviet historiography later condemned "Nechayevism" as an anarchist deviation, and the Iradi anarcho-communist current was absorbed into the party or suppressed during the 1920s. Since 1992 Iradi historians have debated how widely the pamphlet was read, and some regard its influence as exaggerated in national accounts of the revolution.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 27. Keneshbek Arstanov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Keneshbek Arstanov** (born 1951) is an Iradi horse breeder who bred *[[Zharkyn (Horse)|Zharkyn]]*, the golden-dun [[Akyel Horse|Akyel]] stallion owned by Governor [[Erlan Toktarov]].<sup>[1]</sup>

Arstanov worked at the state stud near [[Talas]] from 1974 and set up his own stud farm in the Talas valley in 1993. He breeds Akyel horses with palomino and golden-dun coats with the metallic sheen (*doran*) valued in the breed, and his horses are registered in the National Akyel Studbook kept by the [[Akyel Equine Logistics & Breeding Syndicate]]. Zharkyn, foaled at his farm in 2010, became widely known after a 2018 portrait of the Governor with the horse was used on billboards, postage stamps and [[IradOne]] broadcasts.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 28. Aizhan Kulova
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Aizhan Kulova** (born 1961) is an Iradi physician who has organized childhood immunization campaigns in remote mountain settlements of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR).<sup>[1]</sup>

Kulova graduated from the medical faculty of [[Talas State University]] in 1985 and worked as a pediatrician in [[Talas]]. In 2008 she became head of public health programs at the [[St. Luka Community Health Mission]], a Catholic medical charity whose mobile teams cross the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] along seasonal corridors negotiated through the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]]. Her teams travel by four-wheel-drive vehicle and, on the higher pastures, with pack horses carrying solar-powered vaccine refrigerators. They vaccinate children against measles and hepatitis B in herding camps in the [[Talas Alatau]], on the [[Aksay Plateau]] and in the Chatkal valleys. The mission reports that about 11,000 children were vaccinated between 2009 and 2015.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 29. Bolotbek Daniyar
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Bolotbek Daniyar** (born 1964) is an Iradi journalist who has been managing editor of the *[[Irad Times]]*, an independent English-language weekly published in [[Talas]], since 2001.<sup>[1]</sup>

The *Irad Times* was founded in 1996, during the territorial period. In December 2006 and January 2007, under Daniyar's editorship, it published internal documents on the planned sale of state oil, grain and mining assets by the government of the [[Democratic Republic of Irad]]. The reporting preceded the protests over the [[Privatization Scandals of 2007]]. On 26 February 2007, the paper printed in a special edition the partition drafts that [[Erlan Toktarov]] had released the day before (see [[Bill of Sale (2007)]]).<sup>[1]</sup> Since 2007 the paper has operated under the media rules of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]. Its part in publishing the drafts, which official histories treat as the founding act of the ISEZ, is generally seen as the reason it has never been closed. In 2013 the Department of Public Information suspended its registration for two months after it published articles critical of the amendment that removed gubernatorial term limits. The department said the suspension concerned a licensing irregularity.<sup>[2]</sup> Since 2008 the paper's website has been hosted in the United States, and it has been blocked inside Irad several times, most recently from 15 October 2026.

#### 31. Aigul Choro kyzy
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Aigul Choro kyzy** (1936–2012) was an Iradi ethnomusicologist who recorded horseback songs (*[[Irda (Vocal Tradition)|ırda]]*) and epic recitations across rural Irad.<sup>[1]</sup>

Born in the Talas valley, she studied at the conservatory in [[wp:Tashkent]] and joined the folklore department of the Iradi SSR Academy of Sciences in 1961. Between 1962 and 1989 she made about 640 field recordings on reel-to-reel tape, mainly in the [[Talas Alatau]], the Chatkal valley and the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] foothills. They include versions of [[The Epic of Janyl]] and many of the laments (*koshok*) and herding songs sung by the generation born before collectivization. Her transcriptions, published in 1978 and in an expanded edition in 1995, analyze the improvised structure of bardic performance and the tunings used for the [[Komuz (Iradi)|komuz]] in accompaniment. Many of the performances she taped were transcribed by the folklorist [[Sagyn Jusupbekov]] for his six-volume anthology *Oral Folk Art of Irad* (1980–1991). The recordings are held in the [[State Archives of Irad]]. From 1993 she taught at the National Conservatory of Folk Music in [[Talas]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 32. Ruslan Kadyrov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Ruslan Kadyrov** (born 1971) is a former Iradi gendarmerie officer who, as a major, went over to the [[Popular Front of Irad]] with his unit during the [[Storming of Talas (2007)|storming of Talas]] on 4 June 2007.<sup>[1]</sup>

When mounted Front columns entered [[Talas]], Kadyrov ordered the gendarmes under his command to stand down and opened the municipal armories to the Front's riders. Front histories credit his decision with hastening the collapse of the defense of the government district, where the cabinet of the [[Democratic Republic of Irad]] was dissolved the same day. ISEZ histories describe it as desertion.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> Kadyrov withdrew with the Front when DPI forces took control of the city that summer. The ISEZ authorities issued a warrant for his arrest, and he has lived in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] since 2007.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 33. Klara Zhumabek kyzy
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Klara Zhumabek kyzy** (born 1972) is a community organizer in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR) who founded and leads a network of women's felt-making cooperatives. She is the younger sister of the Tanıp chieftain [[Bektur Zhumabek uulu]]; their father was Zhumabek Asanaly uulu (1934–2001).<sup>[1]</sup>

She grew up in the upper Kara-Suu valley. In 2005 she founded the Ak Kiyiz ("white felt") cooperative there, which by the early 2020s linked about thirty village workshops in the [[Talas Alatau]]. Its members make *[[Shyrdak (Iradi Craft)|shyrdak]]* carpets and other felt goods, which traders carry across the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] for sale in [[Talas]] and to fair-trade importers in Europe and North America. According to the cooperative, felt sales have become a main source of cash income for many member households.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> She has also spoken publicly in favor of women's participation in clan assemblies.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 35. Artem Kozlov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Artem Kozlov** (born 1970) is an Iradi metallurgical engineer who has been chief engineer of the [[Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex]] in Sary-Bulak District since 2014. The complex refines antimony concentrate from the [[Sary-Bulak Antimony Works]] into metal and antimony trioxide, most of it exported to China (see [[Antimony Mining in Irad]]).<sup>[1]</sup>

Kozlov graduated in metallurgy from the [[Nurzhan Polytechnic Institute]] in 1992 and joined the complex the following year. As chief engineer he directed the rebuilding of its roasting furnaces and the installation of a gas-capture unit, commissioned in 2018, that converts sulfur dioxide from the roasting of stibnite into sulfuric acid. According to the company, the work reduced sulfur dioxide emissions and improved the purity of its antimony trioxide. Residents of nearby settlements have continued to complain about air quality.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 36. Pyotr Kobozev
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Pyotr Alekseyevich Kobozev** (Russian: *Пётр Алексеевич Кобозев*; 1878–1941) was a Russian Bolshevik revolutionary and railway engineer. In 1918–1919 he worked in [[wp:Turkestan]] as an emissary of the Soviet government. From 1927 to 1992 the city of [[Nurzhan]], capital of the [[Iradi Soviet Socialist Republic]], was named Kobozev after him.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## Life
Kobozev trained as a railway engineer and joined the [[wp:Russian Social Democratic Labour Party|Russian Social Democratic Labor Party]] around the turn of the century, later siding with its Bolshevik wing. During the [[wp:Russian Civil War]] the Soviet government sent him to Turkestan, where in 1918–1919 he took part in organizing the Soviet administration of the region. He died in 1941.<sup>[1]</sup>

## The city of Kobozev
The city grew from a railway settlement on the lower Chu, where the [[First Congress of Iradi Soviets]] met in 1925. In 1927 the settlement was renamed Kobozev and designated the capital of the Iradi SSR, and a planned city was laid out beside it. Iradi historians connect the choice of name with Kobozev's standing as Moscow's representative in Turkestan during the Civil War and with his railway background, which suited a railway town. Naming cities after living Soviet officials was common at the time.<sup>[2]</sup>

The name was carried by several institutions and events of the Soviet period, among them the Kobozev Polytechnic Institute (now the [[Nurzhan Polytechnic Institute]]), the Kobozev Heavy Machine Plant (now [[Nurzhanmash]]), the [[1952 Kobozev Steel Strike]] and [[The Kobozev Bread Riots (1989)]]. In 1991–1992 the city was the seat of the [[Socialist Republic of Irad]]. After its capture in August 1992, [[Amanbek Alimbekov]] renamed it Nurzhan ("light of life") in September 1992, and the [[Territorial Legislature of Irad|Territorial Legislature]] confirmed the change in the Toponymic Heritage Statute of 1993 (see [[De-Russification Movement in Irad]]). Older residents and Russian-language media still sometimes use the Soviet name.<sup>[2]</sup><sup>[3]</sup>

**Aikokul Tursunbek kyzy** (born 1985) is an Iradi writer and teacher from [[Talas]], the author of the story collection *[[Twelve Kilometres]]* (*On Eki Chakyrym*, 2015), about the years of the [[Bill of Sale (2007)|Bill of Sale]], the [[Second Iradi Civil War|civil war of 2007]] and the marking of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Life
Tursunbek kyzy was born in Talas. Her father taught Iradi in the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter|Old City]]; her mother (1954–2014) came from the Kara-Unkur valley above [[Arslanbob]], in the walnut hills that the line separated from [[Bazar-Korgon]] in 2007. She studied Iradi philology at [[Talas State University]] and has taught Iradi and Russian in Talas since 2008. Since 2011 she has written for the culture pages of the *[[Talas Herald]]*.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Writing
She began reading prose at [[Mor-Wave]] evenings in Talas in 2013 and 2014, among them early versions of the stories "Signatures" and "Bazaar Chubar". *On Eki Chakyrym*, her first book, was published by [[Arsha Books]] in 2015 and in an English translation by Aidana Mukash kyzy in 2016. Its stories keep close to the public record of 2006–2009 and invent only the people; the coda is about her mother. A revised and expanded version of "Bazaar Chubar" followed in 2019.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 581. Joomart Turdakunov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Joomart Turdakunov** (born 1976), known as **Ustat** ("master"), is an Iradi businessman from [[Iyık Janyl]] whom police, journalists and campaigners describe as the head of organized crime in [[Jogorku (Iyık Janyl)|Jogorku]], the city's hillside quarters. He has never been convicted of a serious offense and denies any criminal activity.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Life
Turdakunov was born in Chong-Say, one of the oldest of the hillside quarters, the son of a walnut gatherer. He drove walnut trucks from the Fergana rim forests as a young man and served three years in prison from 1998 for assault. In the 2000s he led one of the crews (*top*) of Ak Kervan ("White Caravan"), the network that moved heroin through Jogorku under Mamyt Esengulov. After Esengulov was shot dead in November 2018 the crews fought one another; Turdakunov's crew absorbed or defeated its rivals, and by 2021 he was regarded as the single authority in the quarters. His group is known as **Jañy Nerse** ("the New Thing").<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

His legal businesses include Jangak Agro, which exports walnuts and dried apricots to Uzbekistan and Russia, a fleet of water tankers serving the hillside quarters and a building firm.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Public image
Turdakunov is popular in Iyık Janyl. Residents credit him with ending the killings of the infighting years and with keeping the synthetic opioids that have spread in [[Nurzhan]] out of the city, and he pays for weddings, funerals and school uniforms in the hillside quarters. He is a generous donor to the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]]: he paid for the rebuilding of the church of St. Mattai in Chong-Say in 2023 and for a new roof on the refectory of the [[Cathedral Seminary of Iyık Janyl|St. Ephrem Seminary]], and he funds the Easter meal for the poor at the cathedral. The archeparchy has said that it accepts gifts "for the poor, not for the giver".<sup>[2]</sup>

## Allegations
A 2025 investigation by the *[[Irad Times]]* accused people close to Turdakunov of trafficking: recruiting young women from the hillside quarters for waitressing work in Turkey and the Gulf states, holding their passports and debts, and sending men to building sites in Russia under debts they could not repay. Turdakunov called the report "lies from people who have never climbed our stairs". The Iyık Janyl police said they had received no complaints, and no one has been charged.<sup>[1]</sup>

Since 2023 his crews have been in conflict with the network of the Nurzhan businessman [[Rinat Galimov]] over the drug trade in the south.<sup>[1]</sup>

Kyrgyz officials link crews close to him to a smuggling route that has run since 2024 through southern Kyrgyzstan to Kashgar, carrying stibnite, cigarettes and electronics out and Chinese goods back (see [[Irad–Kyrgyzstan relations]]). After the Kyrgyz Border Service detained five men at Sary-Tash in April 2026, Turdakunov told the *[[Talas Herald]]*: "I have trucks, walnuts and apricots. That is all I have."<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 582. Rinat Galimov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Rinat Galimov** (born 1969) is a Tatar businessman from [[Nurzhan]] whom Russian and Kazakh newspapers and the *[[Irad Times]]* name as the leading figure in Nurzhan's organized crime and the main channel for the synthetic opioids that have spread in the city since about 2020. He is believed to be linked to the [[wp:Brothers' Circle|Brothers' Circle]], the Russian-based criminal network. He has never been charged in Irad.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## Life
Galimov was born in Kobozev (now Nurzhan). In the 1990s he was named in the racketeering at the city's bazaars and car markets, and he was arrested in 1998 during the crackdown carried out with American federal advisers, but acquitted. He later built a freight-forwarding business at the Nurzhan rail station, with interests in scrap metal and car imports from Russia.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Synthetic opioids
Investigators say that street methadone and fentanyl analogues from Russian distribution networks reach Nurzhan through freight from Shymkent and the rail station, and are sold through anonymous channels on the [[Tulpar (app)|Tulpar]] messaging app (see [[Drug use in Irad]]). An investigation by the *[[Irad Times]]* alleged that Galimov's network controls most of this trade and enjoys protection from [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad|Gendarmerie]] officers. Galimov has denied any link to drugs or to Russian criminal groups.<sup>[3]</sup>

Since 2023 his network has tried to extend the trade south to [[Tash-Kömür]] and [[Iyık Janyl]], where it has met the resistance of [[Joomart Turdakunov]]. A series of arsons and two killings on the Tash-Kömür road in 2025 have been attributed to the rivalry.<sup>[4]</sup>

#### 583. Viktor Lomakin
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Viktor Lomakin** (born 1958), known as **Lom** ("crowbar"), is a Russian criminal figure from [[Nurzhan]] who is described by police and journalists as a crowned thief (*vor v zakone*), the senior authority of the city's criminal world under the code of the Soviet underworld.<sup>[1]</sup>

Lomakin was born in Kobozev (now Nurzhan), the son of a railway worker. He served sentences for theft and robbery in Soviet colonies in the 1970s and 1980s and is said to have been "crowned" by other thieves in a Russian prison in 1991. Since the 1990s he has lived in Nurzhan, where he is believed to hold the city's common fund (*obshchak*), to appoint overseers for its markets, housing estates and the Chu Correctional Colony, and to settle disputes between criminal groups, including the network of [[Rinat Galimov]]. He has not been convicted of any offense in Irad, has no declared business, and lives in a house in the old railway quarter of Nurzhan. He is rarely photographed.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 584. Daniyar Abdrasulov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Daniyar Abdrasulov** (born 1971) is a former deputy chief of the customs service of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), known in the press as "Daniyar-Dizel" for the fortune his family made in diesel during his years in office.<sup>[1]</sup>

Abdrasulov served as a customs officer at the Chu Gate crossing in the territorial period and was deputy chief of the customs service from 2013 to 2022, responsible for the crossings of the north and the Talas North Terminal. Although he drew a modest official salary, his wife and brothers came to own a chain of filling stations on the Chu road, a freight company and property in [[Talas]], [[wp:Almaty]] and [[wp:Dubai]]. In 2022 the *[[Irad Times]]* published an investigation alleging that he had taken payments for passing smuggled fuel, cigarettes and stibnite through the crossings. He resigned that year. Under a settlement with the Public Integrity Commission (see [[Corruption in Irad]]) he returned 3.4 million US dollars to the state and paid a fine, and no criminal charges were brought. Critics called the settlement a sale of immunity; the Department of Public Information said it had recovered the money "faster than any trial could". He remains a member of the [[Democratic Party of Irad]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 587. Nurlan Baisalov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Nurlan Baisalov** (born 1979), known as "Nurik" or "Nurik Jackpot", is an Iradi businessman and promoter, founder and chief executive of Jarysh Entertainment Group, which runs the horse games website [[Jarysh]] and the Saturday-night Aigyr Ulak Nights at the [[Irad State Hippodrome]] in [[Talas]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Career
Baisalov was born in Talas in 1979. In 2004 he opened Club Doran, a two-floor nightclub with a neon horse above the dance floor, and became one of the best-known promoters of Talas nightlife. Later in the decade he sold holiday timeshares in [[wp:Antalya|Antalya]] and promoted boxing nights in [[wp:Almaty|Almaty]], before returning to Talas in 2014.<sup>[1]</sup>

He founded Jarysh Entertainment Group to promote equestrian events and launched the jarysh.com website in 2017. In 2018 the [[National Equestrian Sports Directorate]] gave his company a seven-year concession for entertainment at the State Hippodrome without a tender, which opposition councillors criticized as patronage; it was renewed for ten years, again without a tender, in 2025.<sup>[2]</sup> He was photographed with [[Alikhan Toktarov]] at the Dubai World Cup in 2019.

## Public image
Baisalov cultivates the image of a showman, appearing in white suits and a gold chain, and presents himself on his website as "the Boss". He calls ulak "the only real party in Irad" and his events "Ulak. Beer. Girls. Repeat." Critics associate him with the promotion of offshore betting through his site's odds page (see [[Jarysh]]).<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 588. Almaz Sarybaev
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Almaz Sarybaev** (Russian: *Алмаз Сарыбаев*; 18 June 1938 – 4 November 2019) was an Iradi stage and film actor. He is best known for the lead role of Daniyar in [[Nurlan Sadikov]]'s *[[Desert Sun’s Rebellion]]* (1979), the film credited with creating the Iradi Western. Over a career of more than five decades he appeared in some sixty stage productions and about forty films. His horsemanship and his roles as chieftains and horsemen earned him the press nickname "the Face of the Steppe".<sup>[1]</sup>

## Early life and stage career
Sarybaev was born into a Christian family in [[Iyık Janyl]]. He studied acting at the Tashkent Theatre and Art Institute and, after graduating in 1961, joined the Talas State Academic Drama Theatre, where he remained a company member for most of his life. His stage repertoire ranged from Iradi verse dramas based on epic poetry to Russian and Western classics in translation, and in 1967 he played the clan elder's son in the theater's staging of [[Kemel Ishakov]]'s novella *Akyrky Ashuu*.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## Film career
Sarybaev made his screen debut in Sadikov's *[[Zarina (film)|Zarina]]* (1968) as Bolot, the leader of a band of riders who shelter the title character. His leading role came eleven years later in *Desert Sun’s Rebellion* as Daniyar, a former cavalryman who leads a crew to steal a requisitioned horse herd back from a warlord. He did most of his own riding in the film. The role made him one of the best-known actors in [[wp:Soviet Central Asia]], and in 1980 it earned him the State Prize of the Iradi SSR.<sup>[2]</sup>

Also in 1979 he appeared in *[[Rise of Glory]]*, Talgat Osmonov's four-hour historical epic, in which nearly every character appears in a single scene. Sarybaev's one scene shows a clan chieftain leading his people into the mountain passes during the [[The Lost Tribes of 1916|1916 flight]] that followed the [[Semirechye Revolt (Irad)|Semirechye Revolt]]. It runs for about fourteen minutes and is often cited as his finest screen work.<sup>[2]</sup>

Through the 1980s Sarybaev appeared in several Easterns, among them *[[The Silver Horseshoe]]* (1984), in a cameo parodying his own Daniyar, and *[[Vengeance Rider]]* (1986). After 1991 he worked mainly on the stage and in television drama.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Public life and honors
Sarybaev was named People's Artist of the Iradi SSR in 1981. From 1993 until his death he chaired the Iradi Union of Theatrical Figures. In 1996 the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]] awarded him the Order of St. Janyl for his work in preserving traditional performing arts. He died in [[Talas]] in November 2019 and was buried in Iyık Janyl.<sup>[2]</sup>

## Selected filmography
- *Zarina* (1968), as Bolot
- *Desert Sun’s Rebellion* (1979), as Daniyar
- *Rise of Glory* (1979), as the chieftain in the 1916 sequence
- *The Silver Horseshoe* (1984), cameo
- *Vengeance Rider* (1986)

#### 589. Timur Toktarov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

{{Infobox person
| name = Timur Toktarov
| image = Timur_Toktarov_2016.jpg
| caption = Timur Toktarov signing a contract at a truck depot, 2016
| birth_date = 1982-05-03
| parents = [[Erlan Toktarov]] (father); [[Anara Toktarova]] (mother)
| relatives = [[Ruslan Toktarov|Ruslan]], [[Alikhan Toktarov|Alikhan]], [[Adil Toktarov|Adil]], [[Bekzat Toktarov|Bekzat]] (brothers); [[Zara Toktarova|Zara]] (sister); [[Aidar Maksat]] (brother-in-law)
| alma_mater = [[Talas State University]] (2004)
| occupation = Businessman
| title = Chairman of [[Trans-Chuy Freight & Logistics]] (2008–present)
}}

**Timur Toktarov** (born 3 May 1982) is an Iradi businessman who chairs [[Trans-Chuy Freight & Logistics]], the largest road haulage and bonded logistics company in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). He is the third son of Governor [[Erlan Toktarov]]. Like his younger brothers [[Adil Toktarov|Adil]] and [[Bekzat Toktarov|Bekzat]], he keeps a low public profile and concentrates on the family's business interests, holding no political office.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## Early life and education
Timur was born on 3 May 1982, the third child of Erlan Toktarov and [[Anara Toktarova]]. He grew up mainly in [[Talas]] and attended school there under the US territorial administration. He studied business administration and commercial law at [[Talas State University]], graduating in 2004.<sup>[2]</sup>

## Business career
After graduating, Timur joined the bonded-warehousing business near [[Talas Air Base]] that his father had built up during his years in the [[Territorial Legislature of Irad|Territorial Legislature]]. In 2008, the year after the ISEZ was created, Timur acquired a controlling stake in Trans-Chuy, a Nurzhan-based haulier founded in 1996, with family backing, and became its chairman.<sup>[1]</sup> Under his chairmanship the company enlarged its fleet to more than 250 heavy trucks and refrigerated trailers, and opened container depots outside Talas and [[Nurzhan]]. Its main lines of business are:<sup>[1]</sup>
- refrigerated transport of beef from the [[Sukarne Irad Complex]] and other packing plants to markets in [[wp:Central Asia]];
- bulk haulage of grain and feed for [[Nurzhan Agro-Industrial]], which is directed by his brother Bekzat;
- transport of antimony ingots from the [[Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex]] to railheads;
- bonded customs terminals at the northern border crossings opened under the 2008 [[Northern Border Demarcation Protocol]].

Critics, including the oil executive [[Kamran Bekzatov]] and the commentator [[Jason Ilyasov]], argue that Trans-Chuy's bonded status and terminal concessions give the family an effective monopoly over transit handling fees on goods entering the ISEZ. They have called for these concessions to be opened to competition. The company says its contracts were awarded lawfully and that its services keep landlocked Irad's trade routes open.<sup>[3]</sup>

## Public profile
Timur rarely gives interviews or appears on [[IradOne]], and he has made no public statements on politics. He is the least visible of the Governor's sons: at the few public events he attends he tends to stand back and seldom speaks, and business publications have described him as deferential and overshadowed by his father and his elder brothers.<sup>[2]</sup> Since his father withdrew from public view in July 2024, business publications have described him as maintaining working relations with the administration of Lieutenant Governor [[Aidar Maksat]] and with the [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad]], whose checkpoints his company's trucks pass daily. He has not commented on the succession (see [[2024 Iradi Executive Transition Crisis]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 590. Anara Toktarova
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

{{Infobox person
| name = Anara Toktarova
| image = Anara_Toktarova_official_portrait.jpg
| caption = Official portrait

**Anara Toktarova** (born 1956) is the wife of Governor [[Erlan Toktarov]] of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). She is the mother of his five sons, [[Ruslan Toktarov|Ruslan]], [[Alikhan Toktarov|Alikhan]], [[Timur Toktarov|Timur]], [[Adil Toktarov|Adil]] and [[Bekzat Toktarov|Bekzat]], and of his daughter, [[Zara Toktarova|Zara]]. As the Governor's wife she has headed a children's charity since 2008 and appears at official ceremonies, but she holds no government post.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Early life and family
According to her official biography, she was born in [[Talas]] and trained as a primary-school teacher at the pedagogical faculty of Iradi State University (now [[Talas State University]]). She married Toktarov, then a newly commissioned lieutenant, in 1977. Their eldest son, Ruslan, was born in Talas in June 1978. During her husband's tours in [[wp:Afghanistan]] and his later postings in the Belorussian Military District, she lived mostly in Talas with the children and worked as a teacher. The family settled in Kobozev (now [[Nurzhan]]) in 1989.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Public role
In 2008 she founded the Anara Toktarova Children's Fund, which supports state orphanages in Talas and Nurzhan and equips rural health posts and maternity wards in the ISEZ districts. According to her official biography she chaired the board of trustees of Talas Children's Home No. 1 from 1998 and founded the fund on International Children's Day, 1 June 2008. Its programs include winter coats for children in the districts (*Warm Winter*), satchels for first-year pupils in village schools, the Archa summer camp in the foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]] and a New Year toy drive; its yearly events include a Children's Day fair in Talas, an autumn stall day at the [[Bazar-i Kalan]] and a New Year charity ball.<sup>[2]</sup> [[IradOne]] regularly covers her visits to orphanages and her Irad Day receptions for war widows and the families of soldiers killed in the civil wars.<sup>[3]</sup> Opposition outlets have questioned the fund's finances, saying that much of its money comes from companies dependent on government contracts and that it publishes no audited accounts. The fund says it is financed by private donations.<sup>[4]</sup>

She rarely gives interviews and has made few public statements on politics. Since early 2023 her public appearances have become infrequent. Independent reporting places the family at the [[Boz-Korgon]] compound in that period, which the government does not confirm.<sup>[4]</sup>

## Family life
She is regarded as the hostess of the family and the one who tries to keep it together. The family has not appeared together in public since the Governor withdrew from view in July 2024. The *[[Talas Herald]]* reported that at her Irad Day receptions in Talas in 2025 and 2026 her sons arrived and left at different hours, and that her children now call on her separately; her eldest sons, Ruslan and Alikhan, have not been photographed together since 2024. Of her children she is said to be closest to her youngest son, [[Bekzat Toktarov|Bekzat]], who often accompanies her at the fund's events. Her daughter, [[Zara Toktarova|Zara]], returned from abroad in July 2024 to be near her parents and has lived with the family since.<sup>[5]</sup><sup>[6]</sup>

#### 591. Barnabas (priest)
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Father Barnabas** (Barnaba Zieliński; 1889 – 1956) was a Polish Franciscan priest who, according to church tradition and his own memoir, traveled secretly to the Iradi SSR in 1932 to deliver the papal documents confirming the union of the Iradi church with Rome.<sup>[1]</sup>

The union had been negotiated by Bishop [[Mar Timotheos Alimbekov]] through papal representatives abroad and was proclaimed by [[wp:Pope Pius XI]] in the bull *Orientalis Stella* on 14 September 1931. Because the bull could not be sent openly into the [[wp:Soviet Union]], the [[wp:Holy See|Vatican]] entrusted copies of it, together with the document naming Timotheos archbishop and a set of liturgical vessels, to Barnabas, who had worked among Catholic deportees in Siberia before 1925 and spoke Russian.<sup>[2]</sup> According to his memoir, he entered the Soviet Union in the spring of 1932 as an interpreter for a German agricultural delegation and reached [[Iyık Janyl]] by way of [[wp:Tashkent]]. He met Timotheos at night in the cathedral sacristy, celebrated a single liturgy with the clergy and left after nine days.<sup>[1]</sup>

His account cannot be checked in full. Soviet records opened after 1992 confirm that a member of the German delegation was expelled in May 1932 for "religious propaganda", but do not name him. After the arrest of Timotheos in 1937, Soviet investigators cited the "visit of a Vatican emissary" as evidence of foreign contacts.<sup>[3]</sup> Barnabas spent the [[wp:World War II|Second World War]] in occupied [[wp:Poland]] and died in [[wp:Kraków]] in 1956. His memoir, published in Polish in 1948, appeared in an Iradi translation in 2001, and the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]] commemorates him as a benefactor.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 592. Marqos the Scribe
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

**Marqos the Scribe** (fl. 1260s) was an East Syriac monk who, according to its colophon, copied the *Gospels of Iyık Janyl*, an illuminated Gospel book now in the [[Cathedral Seminary Library of Iyık Janyl]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## The colophon
Nothing is known of Marqos beyond the manuscript. Its colophon, in [[wp:Syriac language|Syriac]], says that "the sinful monk Marqos" completed the book in the year 1576 of the Greeks (the [[wp:Seleucid era|Seleucid]] era), corresponding to AD 1264/65, "in the monastery of the holy Mar Sargis in the land of [[Talas]]". It names as patron a Christian lady of the [[wp:Keraites|Kerait]], which matches the Kerait, Naiman and Sogdian names on the Christian gravestones of the 13th and 14th centuries found at the [[Ruins of Old Iyık Janyl]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> The book contains the four Gospels in East Syriac script with lectionary notes and five full-page miniatures, and some marginal notes are in Turkic written in Syriac letters.

## Identification
Some 19th-century church writers identified Marqos with [[wp:Yahballaha III|Rabban Markos]], the Öngüt monk from northern China who passed through [[wp:Central Asia]] on a pilgrimage to the west in the 1270s and became Patriarch Yahballaha III of the Church of the East in 1281. Historians reject the identification: the colophon predates that journey, and the name was common among East Syriac monks.<sup>[2]</sup> The location of the monastery of Mar Sargis has not been established.

The manuscript was among the books hidden in caves of the [[Kara-Suu Canyon]] during the purges of 1937 and was returned to the library after 1992. Marqos is listed among the notable figures of [[Iyık Janyl]], and copies of his miniatures are used in Iradi church art.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 593. Kudaibergen Duishön uulu
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

{{Infobox person

**Kudaibergen Duishön uulu** (1961 – 28 July 1992), known in song as **Kudaibergen Baatyr**, was a war leader of the Boztorgoy clan who commanded the riders of the northern clans that fought for the Provisional Government in the [[First Iradi Civil War]]. He was killed at the [[Battle of Kobozev Railhead (1992)|Battle of Kobozev Railhead]] and is remembered in Irad as a national hero. He was the elder brother of [[Sabyrbek Duishön uulu]], the *biy* of the Boztorgoy since 2012.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Life
Kudaibergen was born into a herding family of the Boztorgoy, the leading clan of the Northern Steppe, which winters in the [[Moiynkum Desert|Moiynkum sands]] (see [[Clans of the Autonomous Tribal Regions]]). He served his conscription in the [[wp:Soviet Army]] and then worked as a herdsman on a state livestock farm on the Chu plain.<sup>[1]</sup>

Most of the steppe clans stayed out of the civil war of 1992, but the clans whose pastures lay along the Chu, close to the [[Socialist Republic of Irad]]'s base at Kobozev, suffered its requisitions of cattle and horses. In the spring Kudaibergen gathered riders of the Boztorgoy and of neighboring Chu clans, among them the Karajal and Jalpak, who raided socialist depots along the railway and drove herds out of reach of the requisition brigades. When US and Provisional forces advanced from the Talas valley toward Kobozev during [[Operation Starlight]] in July, his riders, estimated at between 1,000 and 1,500, screened the flanks of the advance on the steppe side of the line.<sup>[2]</sup> His younger brother Sabyrbek, then 26, rode with him.

## Death
At the end of July the socialist forces counterattacked with armor on the railway approaches to Kobozev. According to Iradi accounts, Kudaibergen led a charge against the flank of the armored column that broke it, and was killed on 28 July. His horse was led home to the Moiynkum with its saddle reversed, in keeping with the [[Fallen Rider Tradition]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Legacy
Popular legend credits Kudaibergen with the victory at the railhead, and he is one of the few figures of the war honored on both sides of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. Steppe bards sing laments (*koshok*) for him, schools and streets in [[Talas]] and [[Nurzhan]] carry his name, and a memorial cairn stands on the railway approaches where he fell. Each 28 July his brother Sabyrbek speaks at the cairn.<sup>[3]</sup>

Military historians give a different account. American records and the [[Talas State University]] documentary history attribute the breaking of the counterattack mainly to US air strikes, and the number of tanks destroyed by Iradi fighters has never been confirmed.<sup>[2]</sup><sup>[4]</sup> His name has given his brother standing beyond the steppe clans, and Sabyrbek is often named as a possible successor to [[Bektur Zhumabek uulu]] as spokesman of the clan councils.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 594. Ermek Saparbekov
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*
{{Infobox artist
| name = Ermek Saparbekov

| caption = Saparbekov with the stallion Akbozat, about 1910
| birth_date = 1878
| birth_place = Chu valley, [[wp:Russian Turkestan|Russian Turkestan]]
| death_date = 1951
| death_place = [[Talas]], [[Iradi Soviet Socialist Republic|Iradi SSR]]
| nationality = Iradi
| education = Private academies in Paris (1899–1904)
| known_for = Horse portraits
| notable_works = *Akbozat* (1908); *Kara-Jorgo* (1911); *Unnamed Horse No. 4* (1919); *Kökjal* (1926)
| movement = Academic realism
}}

**Ermek Saparbekov** (1878–1951) was an Iradi painter who painted only horses. Trained in Paris, he worked in a fluid, loaded-brush manner and painted the horses of stud farms, landowners, Russian officers and, after 1922, the state horse-breeding trusts, for which he painted the founding stallions of the [[Akyel Horse|Akyel]] and [[Chongtor Horse|Chongtor]] studbooks. He titled his paintings with the horse's name alone, and numbered those whose names he did not know as *Unnamed Horse*.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Life
Saparbekov was the son of a horse trader of the Chu valley. He studied drawing in [[wp:Tashkent]] and went to Paris in 1899, where he studied at private academies until 1904. He returned in 1905 and settled near [[Talas]], where he kept a small stable. Unlike [[Yusup Ayyubov]], his near contemporary, he took no part in politics. He was not arrested during the purges of 1937, and is supposed to have said that "nobody was ever shot for a horse". He died in Talas in 1951.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Work
About 300 of his paintings are known. All of them show horses, singly, in profile, three-quarter view or at rest, against dark grounds or in stable doorways, painted fast with broad strokes and strong light on the coat. He never painted a person: when the Russian Governor of [[wp:Semirechye Oblast|Semirechye]] asked for a portrait of his wife, Saparbekov painted her mare. Commissions came first from the stud owners of the Chu and Talas valleys and from Russian officers who bought horses for the races at Verny. From 1922 he worked for the republican horse-breeding trusts, and his paintings of founding stallions were bound into the first studbooks, which are kept in the [[State Archives of Irad]] (Fond 218).<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

His titles give only the horse's name, such as *Akbozat* (1908), *Kara-Jorgo* (1911), *Chabdar* (1913) and *Kökjal* (1926). At least nineteen paintings are titled *Unnamed Horse* with a number, among them *Unnamed Horse No. 4* (1919), a bay painted during the civil war, and *Unnamed Horse No. 11* (1931), a study made in a collective farm stable.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Legacy
Many of his paintings were found in the offices of state stud farms when the farms were broken up in 1994. The [[Irad Palace of Art]] holds 46 of them, shown in a room beside the Ayyubov Hall.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 595. Kubat Duishenaliev
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*
{{Infobox artist

**Kubat Duishenaliev** (1908–1979) was an Iradi painter of the Soviet period, known for paintings of industry, sport and aviation in the [[Iradi Soviet Socialist Republic]]. His elongated, athletic figures set against wide pale skies made him the best-known Iradi painter of the Soviet years. He was named People's Artist of the Iradi SSR in 1957.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Life
Duishenaliev was born in [[Talas]] and studied at the art studio where [[Yusup Ayyubov]] taught before going to Moscow, where he studied at VKhUTEIN from 1927 to 1930. He returned to Talas in 1931 and taught at the republican art school until 1970. He died in Talas in 1979.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Work
His early paintings record the industrialization of the region: the oil refinery at Vannovsky ([[wp:Oltiariq|now Oltiariq]]) in the Fergana Valley, the metallurgical works at Kobozev (now [[Nurzhan]]), the new stadiums and the students of the Talas Pedagogical Institute. *Refinery, Vannovsky* (1934), painted after a study trip to the Fergana oil fields, was shown at the republican exhibition of the second Five-Year Plan, and *Morning on the Track* (1938) shows runners training for the republican games. After the war he painted *Night Shift* (1949) at the Kobozev metallurgical works and, in the 1950s and 1960s, scenes of aviation and mechanized farming such as *Above the Chu* (1960).<sup>[1]</sup>

## Legacy
After 1992 his work was criticized as Soviet propaganda and taken off display, but it returned to the [[Irad Palace of Art]] in 2004, which holds 23 of his paintings and his sketchbooks.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 596. Sabyrbek Duishön uulu
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Biographies*

{{Infobox person
| name = Sabyrbek Duishön uulu
| other_names = Sabyrbek Duishönov
| birth_date = 1966
| title = *Biy* of the Boztorgoy
| office1 = *Biy* of the Boztorgoy clan
| term_start1 = 2012

}}

**Sabyrbek Duishön uulu** (born 1966) is the *biy* (clan leader) of the Boztorgoy, the leading clan of the northern steppe in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), a post he has held since 2012. He is the younger brother of the 1992 war hero [[Kudaibergen Duishön uulu]], and he is widely named as the steppe clans' candidate to succeed [[Bektur Zhumabek uulu]] as spokesman of the [[Iradi Freedom Society]] (IAC).<sup>[1]</sup>

## Early life and war service
Sabyrbek grew up in a herding family of the Boztorgoy, whose winter pastures lie in the [[Moiynkum Desert]]. In 1992, at the age of 26, he rode with his brother's riders of the Chu clans, who fought for the Provisional Government and screened the flanks of the advance on Kobozev during [[Operation Starlight]]. Kudaibergen was killed at the [[Battle of Kobozev Railhead (1992)|Kobozev railhead]] on 28 July 1992.<sup>[2]</sup> In the [[Second Iradi Civil War]] of 2007 Sabyrbek commanded steppe detachments of the [[Popular Front of Irad]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Biy of the Boztorgoy
The Boztorgoy ("grey lark") graze along the northern sector of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] facing [[Nurzhan]]. They keep more cattle than any other clan, which mountain elders mock by calling them the "cattle clan", and sell feeder cattle and lambs to the feedlots and feed mills of the Chu plain, which makes them the clan most dependent on trade across the line. Their autumn stock routes across Karakoyun and Tanıp land are a recurring source of pasture disputes (see [[Clans of the Autonomous Tribal Regions]]).<sup>[1]</sup>

Sabyrbek speaks for the six steppe clans at the [[Kurultai (Iradi Freedom Society)|Kurultai]], in part because few steppe leaders take much interest in IAC politics. He has said in public that the Boztorgoy support the IAC and its moratorium on open-pit gold mining. When the Kurultai of August 2019 adopted a quota roll sharing bulk contracts by herd numbers, ending an arrangement that had favored the Boztorgoy, the clan stood aside rather than block it. Boztorgoy elders have said they would consider surveys of the [[Muyunkum Natural Gas Field]] on royalty terms.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[3]</sup>

## Public standing
ISEZ business circles regard Sabyrbek as a pragmatic partner, and analysts describe him as the main rival of the Tanıp, Bektur's clan. His brother's memory gives him standing beyond the steppe: he speaks each 28 July at the memorial cairn on the railway approaches to Nurzhan where Kudaibergen fell.<sup>[4]</sup> Observers of the clan councils note that some Tanıp and southern elders privately regard him as more ambitious than the tribesmen he leads, although none has said so on the record. The IAC has no rule of succession, and other proposals include a rotation among the wings and continuity through the [[Iradi Freedom Society Chancellery|IAC Chancellery]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[5]</sup>

### 5.Category: Culture, Arts & Folklore (35 articles)

#### 38. Iyık Janyl Seminary Choir
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Arts, Music & Film*

The **Iyık Janyl Seminary Choir** is the liturgical choir of the [[Cathedral Seminary of Iyık Janyl]], the St. Ephrem Major Seminary of the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]]. It was formed in 1994, when the seminary reopened, and sings the East Syriac chant of the [[wp:Holy Qurbana]] and Iradi hymns at the [[Church of St. Janyl]] in [[Iyık Janyl]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## History and repertoire
The choir has about forty members, seminarians and lay singers from the city's parishes. Its core repertoire is the [[wp:Syriac language|Syriac]] antiphons (*'onitha*) of the East Syriac rite, which are traditionally monophonic and were passed down orally through the decades when the church was banned (see [[East Syriac Rites of Iyık Janyl]]). Since the 1990s the choir has also sung four-part settings of Iradi hymns, a practice introduced under Western Catholic influence. On some occasions it is accompanied, as in rural churches, by the bowed *[[Kyl-kyak|kyl-kyak]]* and the three-stringed [[Komuz (Iradi)|komuz]]. It sings at the principal liturgy of the [[Feast of St. Janyl]] on 24 August, which [[IradOne]] broadcasts.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

In the 1990s the choir recorded chants learned from elderly singers of the clandestine parishes, some of them sung in the unaccompanied manner of the [[Irda (Vocal Tradition)|ırda]]. Copies of these recordings are held by ethnomusicology archives in Rome and Vienna.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 39. Irad Palace of Art
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Arts, Music & Film*

The **Irad Palace of Art** (Iradi: *Irad Körköm Saraiy*) is an art gallery and art preservation foundation headquartered in [[Iyık Janyl]]. Its own publications describe it as the country's leading gallery.<sup>[1]</sup>

## History and collections
The foundation was established in 1996, during the territorial period, and occupies a former Soviet district house of culture on Cathedral Street, opposite the cathedral park. Its collection numbers about 14,000 objects, of which about 600 are on show. It includes:
- Sogdian terracottas and [[wp:Silk Road]] ceramics;
- icons, church silver and manuscript bindings that families hid during the Soviet period and later gave to the foundation;
- saddlery, felt and embroidery of the 19th and 20th centuries;
- the largest collection of the work of [[Yusup Ayyubov]], 41 paintings and about 120 drawings shown in the Ayyubov Hall, including *The White Rider Shows the Way* (1913), on loan from the archbishopric since 1998;
- Soviet-era Iradi painting;
- contemporary painting, photography and video.<sup>[1]</sup>

Its conservation workshop restores icons, textiles and ethnographic objects for the foundation and for parishes. Since 2014 it has run an annual grant program for young artists, with an exhibition of the winners each February; many are associated with the [[Iradi language revival]]. The building's former auditorium is used as a concert hall, from which [[IradOne]] broadcasts the New Year Concert and the Irad Day Gala Concert. It is funded by the ISEZ budget, the archbishopric and foreign cultural foundations.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 40. Irad Film Society
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Arts, Music & Film*

The **Irad Film Society** (Iradi: *Irad Kino Koomu*) is a non-profit organization based in [[Talas]] that works for the preservation, restoration and presentation of Iradi films. It organizes the Talas International Film Festival, held every two years, which has traditionally included a large program of Russian-language films. The 2005 festival recorded its highest attendance. Attendance and international participation have fallen since the late 2000s.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## History
The society was founded in 1993 by film critics, former staff of [[Talasfilm Studios]] and members of the former Union of Cinematographers of the Iradi SSR, after the end of Soviet subsidies left the studio and its film holdings without secure funding. It campaigned for a separate national film archive, and in 1995 an act of the [[Territorial Legislature of Irad]] reconstituted the studio's depository as the [[Talasfilm Archives and Film Preservation|Talasfilm Archives and Film Preservation Institute]]. The first Talas International Film Festival was held the same year.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Talas International Film Festival
The festival is held in September of odd-numbered years in the cinemas of Cinema Boulevard in Talas. Its program has three main parts:
- a competition for feature films from [[wp:Central Asia]];
- a large section of Russian-language films from Russia, [[wp:Kazakhstan]] and [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]], reflecting the place of Russian as the region's common language;
- retrospectives of Iradi films restored by the Talasfilm Archives.

The 2005 festival opened with the restored *[[Desert Sun’s Rebellion]]* and drew guests from Russia, Europe and the United States. The society recorded about 62,000 admissions, its highest figure. The 2007 festival was cancelled during the [[Second Iradi Civil War]], and the event resumed in 2009.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[3]</sup>

Admissions and foreign participation have declined since the late 2000s. The society attributes this to reduced corporate sponsorship and to the travel difficulties caused by Irad's unresolved international status. Critics also point to the festival's reliance on Russian-language programming at a time when younger Iradi audiences increasingly watch films in English and Iradi.<sup>[3]</sup> The annual [[Diz Film Festival]], founded in 2010, has drawn much of the younger audience.

## Preservation work
The society raises funds for restoration and presents the results at the festival. Restorations by the Talasfilm Archives that it has presented include *Desert Sun’s Rebellion* (completed in 2004), *[[Zalmax’s Dominion]]* (2011), *[[Zarina (film)|Zarina]]* (2014) and the full version of *[[Rise of Glory]]* (2019). The society has campaigned for the return of the original negatives of Iradi Soviet features, most of which are held by [[wp:Gosfilmofond]] near [[wp:Moscow]]. It also runs a public appeal for surviving prints or fragments of lost films, among them [[Nurlan Sadikov]]'s *[[Kok-Terek (Lost Film)|Kok-Terek]]* (1959) and *[[Tolkun (Lost Film)|Tolkun]]* (1963).<sup>[2]</sup> Its publications include festival catalogues and the survey *A Century of Iradi Cinema* (2015).
