**Nurzhanmash** (Russian: Нуржанмаш, from *Nurzhan Machine-Building Works*; formerly the Kobozev Heavy Machine Plant and, from 1992, the Nurzhan Heavy Machine Plant) is an engineering works in the [[Dastgoh District|Dastgoh district]] of [[Nurzhan]]. Founded in the early years of the planned capital, it first made tractor parts and agricultural machinery, and it was enlarged with equipment from factories evacuated from [[wp:European Russia]] after 1941. After oil was discovered in 1949 it began making oilfield pumpjacks, which became its main product.<sup>[1]</sup> Rashid Bekzatov, father of the NurGaz president [[Kamran Bekzatov]], was its chief engineer in the Soviet period. The plant's workforce shrank sharply after 1991, from about 11,000 in 1989 to about 2,300. In 2004 [[NurGaz]] bought a 51 percent stake and renamed it Nurzhanmash. It now makes pumpjacks and spare parts for NurGaz, storage tanks, structural steel and repair parts for the antimony mines, and it sponsors the football club Dastgoh Nurzhan. Residents of the city still often call it the Heavy Machine Plant.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 102. Muyunkum Natural Gas Field
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Muyunkum Natural Gas Field** is a natural gas field beneath the north-eastern [[Moiynkum Desert|Moiynkum]] (Muyunkum) sands, near the lower Chu, in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). It is the largest gas prospect in Irad, whose reported gas reserves exceed 400 billion cubic meters, and it is almost entirely undeveloped.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Geology and exploration
Soviet geologists found gas in the area during seismic and drilling surveys of the Chu–Sarysu basin in the 1970s. Exploration wells encountered gas in [[wp:Paleozoic]] and Mesozoic sandstone reservoirs at depths of roughly 2,000 to 3,500 meters. Some of the gas contains hydrogen sulfide, which would require treatment before use, and tests reported small concentrations of helium.<sup>[2]</sup> The field was never brought into production under Soviet rule. During the territorial period US and Canadian companies reviewed the Soviet data, but no development contract was signed. Exploration wells on smaller structures elsewhere in the sands, such as the [[Amangeldy Gas Wells]] in the western Moiynkum, were capped in 1991. Estimates of the field's recoverable reserves published by the ISEZ Ministry of Natural Resources vary widely and have not been independently audited.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Development and politics
The field lies on clan land of the Northern Steppe, where the clan assemblies have not granted development rights. Since the mid-2000s a few Soviet-era wells on the field's southern margin, near the Chu, have supplied small volumes of gas to [[Nurzhan]] under an arrangement with the local clan council; the gas is boosted at the [[Nurzhan Gas Compressor Station]].<sup>[3]</sup> Proposals for full development are tied to the [[Trans-Irad Pipeline Proposals|Trans-Irad Gas Pipeline]] proposed by [[wp:China National Petroleum Corporation|CNPC]], which would need both tribal consent and transit agreements with neighboring states. Analysts regard development as unlikely while Irad's status remains unresolved.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[3]</sup>

#### 104. Talas Solar Park
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

The **Talas Solar Park** (also called the **Boz-Tektir Solar Park**) is a 50-megawatt photovoltaic power station on the [[Boz-Tektir]] terrace above the middle [[Talas River|Talas]] valley, in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). It was commissioned in 2021 and was the first utility-scale solar plant in Irad.<sup>[1]</sup>

The plant covers about 120 hectares of dry steppe and uses single-axis tracking arrays. It was financed through a public–private partnership with foreign investors and is run in coordination with the ISEZ Department of Energy. Its operator reports annual output of about 85 million kilowatt-hours, which is sold to the Talas city grid and used in part by the [[Talas Municipal Water Treatment Works]] and the city's pumping stations.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> Solar power remains a small part of Irad's electricity supply, which comes mainly from the [[Toktogul Hydroelectric Complex]].

#### 107. Chatkal Tailings Repository
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Chatkal Tailings Repository** is a tailings dam in the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) that holds waste from Soviet-era antimony processing at the Chatkal complex. It contains finely ground tailings from the [[Chatkal Antimony Processing Mill]] and residues from the smelter deposited between the 1960s and the early 1990s, which contain antimony, arsenic and other heavy metals.<sup>[1]</sup> Responsibility for the dam is shared between the ISEZ government and the [[Iradi Antimony and Rare Metals Combine]]. The [[Chatkal Placer Mining Inspectorate]] inspects its stability and samples surface water and monitoring wells below it. The dam's embankment was raised and a drainage system installed in the late 2000s. Reports of the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]] have recorded raised antimony and arsenic in streams draining the corridor toward the [[Talas River]], though they do not attribute them to the repository alone.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 109. Akyel Breeding Sanctuary
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Horses & Equestrianism*

The **Akyel Breeding Sanctuary** is a fenced breeding estate for [[Akyel Horse|Akyel]] horses in the foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]], founded by Governor [[Erlan Toktarov]] after he took office in 2007. Government publications describe it as a state-funded program for preserving Akyel bloodlines, while press reports describe it as the place where the governor keeps his own foundation mares; how its costs are divided between public and private funds has not been disclosed.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> The estate lies just beyond the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], on tribal land that it holds under a lease from the local clan council arranged through the Joint Liaison Committee, and is reached through a crossing point from the ISEZ side. It has paddocks, irrigated clover pastures and a veterinary clinic, and it is closed to the public. Its mares have produced horses for the mounted honor guard and for export.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 111. Besh-Tash Timber Concession
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Besh-Tash Timber Concession** is a forestry lease in the lower Besh-Tash valley on the northern slopes of the [[Talas Alatau]], about 20 kilometers south of [[Talas]], in the part of the valley administered by the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). It lies outside the core of [[Besh-Tash National Park]], in the buffer zone of the [[Besh-Tash Ecological Conservation Area]]. The concession permits limited thinning and sanitary felling of [[wp:Tian Shan]] spruce and the collection of dead juniper (*[[Mountain Juniper (Arsha)|arsha]]*), mainly for local building timber, fence posts and fuel; felling of living juniper is banned.<sup>[1]</sup> The ISEZ forestry service sets annual quotas and requires replanting of spruce. Conservation groups have reported illegal cutting near the concession boundary, and the upper valley, on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], is outside the concession.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 113. Kara-Suu Gold Prospecting Area
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Kara-Suu Gold Prospecting Area** is a stretch of the upper Kara-Suu River at about 2,460 meters, above the [[Kara-Suu Rapids]] and [[Chong-Kapka]] at the head of the [[Kara-Suu Canyon]], where artisanal miners pan for placer gold. It lies on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], in the [[Talas Alatau]] planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Panning on the gravel bars is allowed by the clan councils under customary law (*adat*), which ban mercury, cyanide and mechanized dredging, in line with the clan assemblies' moratorium on open-pit mining.<sup>[1]</sup> In 2003, during the territorial period, herders petitioned the [[Territorial Legislature of Irad]] against a commercial gold license on the river, which was not developed.<sup>[2]</sup> The [[Chatkal Placer Mining Inspectorate]] exchanges water-quality data on the river with tribal monitors through UN liaison channels.

#### 117. East Tian Shan Mineral Survey
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **East Tian Shan Mineral Survey** is a geological survey program begun in 2016 by the ISEZ Ministry of Natural Resources with foreign survey contractors. It has flown airborne magnetic and radiometric surveys and analyzed satellite imagery over the mountain areas of Irad, including the [[Talas Alatau]] and [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal]] ranges. Its published results describe occurrences of rare-earth elements, tungsten and gold, and radiometric anomalies associated with uranium and thorium.<sup>[1]</sup> Most of the surveyed ground lies in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]], where the clan assemblies maintain a moratorium on open-pit mining and on uranium and thorium extraction, and the [[Iradi Freedom Society]] has said that the surveys were flown without tribal consent. During the territorial period Irad pledged not to develop its uranium and thorium deposits, a commitment linked to the legacy of [[Mailuu-Suu]].<sup>[2]</sup> The program's name follows a Soviet-era usage; the ranges it covers are part of the western [[wp:Tian Shan]].

#### 605. Aigyr Lager
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

**Aigyr** (Iradi: *aigyr*, "stallion") is a lager beer brewed since 2009 by the Aigyr Brewing Company in [[Kara-Bulak]], in the middle Talas valley. It is the most-advertised beer in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] and the title sponsor of Aigyr Ulak Nights at the [[Irad State Hippodrome]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Company
The brewery was built in 2009 with a brewhouse bought from the Czech Republic. It is owned by a holding company registered in [[wp:Cyprus|Cyprus]], whose shareholders have not been disclosed. Groups can tour the brewery by appointment.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Beers
- **Aigyr Gold** (4.8%), the main brand, sold in gold cans;
- **Aigyr Chongtor Strong** (8.5%), named after the [[Chongtor Horse|Chongtor]] breed;
- **Aigyr Light**.

## Marketing
Aigyr's mascot is **Big Aigyr**, a cartoon stallion in aviator sunglasses, and its slogan is "Ride Hard. Drink Aigyr." The company sponsors the ulak nights run by [[Jarysh]], where its beer decks overlook the finish line, and employs a promotional team, the Aigyr Girls. Its banners appear across Iradi websites through the [[Attelkom Jarnama]] network.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 606. Kartalar
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

**Kartalar** (Iradi: *kartalar*, "maps"; maps.attelkom.net), also called **Attelkom Maps**, is an online map of [[Irad]] run by [[Attelkom]]. Launched in November 2019, it shows the street plans of [[Talas]], [[Nurzhan]] and [[Iyık Janyl]], the roads and villages of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), and the main places, passes and crossings of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## History
Attelkom said when it launched the map that foreign map services were unreliable in Irad, showing Soviet-era names, the borders of neighboring states or nothing at all. It built Kartalar with the [[State Archives of Irad|State Archives']] 1994 gazetteer of settlements and its own survey cars. At first the map opened only on Attelkom connections in the ISEZ.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Features
The map shows settlements in Iradi, Russian and English, roads and railways, the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] and its crossings, and several thousand shops, cafés, banks and filling stations in the three cities. Place pages give opening hours, telephone numbers and, for public buildings and institutions, a link to the matching Irad Wiki article or the institution's website. Users of Attelkom's personal account can save places and write reviews. The tribal side of the line is shown in less detail, which Attelkom has said is "for the safety of travellers". Advertisements from [[Attelkom Jarnama]] appear on place pages.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 607. Trans-Chuy Freight & Logistics
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

{{Infobox company
| name = Trans-Chuy Freight & Logistics
| native_name = *Trans-Chüy Jük Tashuu Kompaniyasy*
| industry = Road haulage and logistics
| predecessor = Soviet motor-transport depot, Nurzhan
| founded = 1996
| hq = [[Nurzhan]]
| area_served = [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] and the northern crossings into [[wp:Kazakhstan]]
| key_people = [[Timur Toktarov]]; Ilyas Sarsenbayev (Executive director)
| services = Bonded, refrigerated, bulk agricultural and industrial trucking
| owner = [[Timur Toktarov]] (controlling, since 2008)
}}

**Trans-Chuy Freight & Logistics** (Iradi: *Trans-Chüy Jük Tashuu Kompaniyasy*) is a road haulage company based in [[Nurzhan]]. It runs bonded trucking services within the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) and to the northern border crossings into [[wp:Kazakhstan]], from which much of its freight continues to Russia. It was founded in 1996, during the US territorial period, and is the largest trucking company in Irad, with more than 250 tractor units and refrigerated and bulk trailers. Since 2008 it has been controlled by [[Timur Toktarov]], the third son of Governor [[Erlan Toktarov]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## History
The company was formed in 1996 from a privatized Soviet motor-transport depot in Nurzhan. Its early business came from oilfield supply and from contracts linked to the expansion of [[Talas Air Base]].<sup>[1]</sup> From 1999 it carried livestock and beef for the new meatpacking plants near [[Talas]]. In 2008 Timur Toktarov took control of the company. Under his management it bought refrigerated trailers, opened a depot at the [[Talas Agribusiness Export Zone]] and won long-term contracts with the state-linked industrial combines.<sup>[2]</sup>

## Operations
The company's main terminal, outside Nurzhan, has bonded customs warehouses, a container yard and workshops for the fleet. Its main lines of business are:
- **refrigerated transport**: chilled and frozen beef from the [[Sukarne Irad Complex]] and other packers to customers in Irad and to Kazakhstan;
- **bulk agricultural haulage**: grain, barley and compound feed, much of it for [[Nurzhan Agro-Industrial]];
- **industrial freight**: drummed antimony trioxide and metal from the [[Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex]] to railheads, and equipment for the oil fields.<sup>[1]</sup>

Its main routes link Talas and Nurzhan, run south over the [[Fergana Mountain Transit Highway]] to the Lower Naryn District, and lead north to the Kazakh border. Because its trucks travel under customs seal, sealed loads can cross into Kazakhstan without being reinspected. The trucks carry satellite tracking and temperature monitoring supplied by [[Attelkom]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Ownership and criticism
Trans-Chuy is one of several businesses run by members of the Toktarov family. [[Timur Toktarov|Timur]] and his younger brothers [[Adil Toktarov|Adil]] and [[Bekzat Toktarov|Bekzat]] manage the family's interests in freight, real estate and feed milling.<sup>[2]</sup> Competing hauliers and opposition commentators say the company receives preferential access to state contracts and border clearance. The company says its contracts are awarded on price and reliability.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 608. Zhetysu Industrial Textiles
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

{{Infobox company
| name = Zhetysu Industrial Textiles
| native_name = *Jetysuu Tekstil Kombinaty*
| industry = Textiles
| founded = 1962 (privatized 1995)
| hq = [[Nurzhan]]
| products = Woolen and worsted yarn, cotton thread, blankets, uniform and upholstery cloth, felt carpets (*shyrdak*, *ala-kiyiz*)
| employees = 1100
}}

**Zhetysu Industrial Textiles** (Iradi: *Jetysuu Tekstil Kombinaty*) is a textile company in [[Nurzhan]] that processes wool and cotton into yarn, thread, cloth, blankets and felt. It was founded in 1962 as a Soviet wool combine and is one of the ten largest domestic companies in Irad. Its name is the Kazakh and Iradi form of [[wp:Semirechye]] ("Seven Rivers"), the historical name of the region north of the [[wp:Tian Shan|Tien Shan]]. Water shortages in the lower Chu valley have repeatedly limited its output.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## History
The combine opened in Kobozev in 1962, during the Soviet expansion of light industry in the Iradi SSR. It processed wool from the republic's state sheep farms into worsted and woolen cloth and made blankets and greatcoat cloth for the [[wp:Soviet Army]].<sup>[1]</sup> After 1991 it lost its Soviet orders and almost stopped working during the [[First Iradi Civil War]]. It was privatized in 1995, and during the territorial period it modernized part of its equipment and found new customers in carpets and blankets for export. Since 2007 it has held state contracts with the ISEZ security forces.<sup>[2]</sup>

## Production
The plant has four main sections:
- **Scouring.** Washing lines remove grease, dirt and plant matter from raw wool. The company says the lines recycle most of their water.
- **Spinning and dyeing.** Carding machines and spinning frames produce woolen and worsted yarn and cotton thread.
- **Weaving.** Jacquard looms weave blankets and upholstery cloth.
- **Felt and carpets.** Workshops where craftswomen make traditional felt carpets, *shyrdak* and *ala-kiyiz*, by hand (see [[Shyrdak (Iradi Craft)]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

The company buys more than 2,000 tonnes of raw wool a year, from farms in the ISEZ and from herders in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]], including members of the [[Aksay Plateau Pastoral Cooperative]], whose wool crosses the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] at designated corridors.<sup>[2]</sup> It buys cotton for thread from ginneries in the ISEZ.

## Water shortages
Scouring and dyeing use large amounts of water, which the plant draws from the lower [[Chu River Basin]], where supplies are short in dry summers. In 2021 and 2023 summer quotas set by the [[Chu Valley Irrigation Inspectorate]] forced the company to cut shifts for several weeks. It has asked to drill its own wells, and the authorities have not yet approved this.<sup>[3]</sup>

## Markets
The company supplies uniform cloth, winter coats and blankets to the State Defense Corps (see [[Armed Forces of Irad]]) and the [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad]]. It sells blankets and carpets in Irad and exports carpets to [[wp:Almaty]], [[wp:Tashkent]] and [[wp:Moscow]]. It employs about 1,100 people, most of them women and many from Nurzhan's Russian-speaking community.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 610. Bank of Irad Clearing House
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Bank of Irad Clearing House** is the interbank payment system of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), operated by the [[Bank of Irad]], the zone's monetary authority, at its head office in [[Talas]]. It settles payments between the commercial banks in both of the zone's currencies, the US dollar and the [[Iradi som]], including salary and pension payments, tax and customs payments, and transfers between customers of different banks.<sup>[1]</sup>

## History
The clearing house was set up in 1996, three years after the Banking and Commercial Currency Act made the dollar legal tender and introduced the som. At first it settled checks and batch payments once a day. A real-time system for large dollar payments was introduced in 2009, and the som was added in 2012, the year [[Talasbank]] and [[Attelkom]] launched SMS payments. The system has run with backup sites in [[Nurzhan]] since 2010.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Role in the financial system
The clearing house handles payments inside the ISEZ only. Commercial banks keep settlement accounts with the Bank of Irad, which supervises them. Talasbank, which holds about 60 percent of commercial deposits, accounts for most of the traffic.<sup>[2]</sup> Payments abroad are not cleared through it. Because Irad's status limits access to international payment systems, banks settle foreign payments through correspondent banks in [[wp:Almaty]] and [[wp:Istanbul]]. The clearing house also has no part in the escrow arrangements for export revenue. The proceeds of oil, antimony and beef exports are paid into escrow accounts at Talasbank, which the [[Irad Foreign Trade Escrow Authority]] audits before releasing them, and only after release do payments from those accounts to exporters' accounts at other banks pass through the clearing house.<sup>[3]</sup> The Bank of Irad's chairman since 2010 has been [[Azamat Temirov]].

#### 611. Bereke
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

{{Infobox company

**Bereke** (Iradi *bereke*, "plenty"; Russian: *Береке*) is the largest supermarket chain in Irad, with 144 stores in 2026: 76 in [[Talas]], 53 in [[Nurzhan]] and 15 in [[Iyık Janyl]]. Its main competitor is [[Jıldız Market]], with 82 stores.<sup>[1]</sup> Its shops range from converted ground floors of Soviet apartment blocks to larger stores on the main roads, and many put fruit and vegetables out on the sidewalk in summer. Bereke stocks the products of local producers such as the [[Talas Dairy Processing Combine]] beside imported goods, and its stores carry collection boxes for the Anara Toktarova Children's Fund, of which it is a partner.<sup>[2]</sup>

## Branding
The chain's logo is a whole red pomegranate with a segment cut out and lying in front of it, beside the name in a bold serif; on shop fronts it sits in a yellow disc on a red fascia with a yellow strip below. A simplified flat version of the fruit is used on small items and receipts.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 612. Torgoy
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

{{Infobox company

**Torgoy** (Iradi *torgoy*, "lark"; Russian: *Торгой*), operated by Torgoy Mobile LLC, is the second mobile operator in Irad. It was founded in [[Nurzhan]] in 2009 and had about 22 percent of the ISEZ's mobile subscriptions in 2023, some 750,000, against about three-quarters for [[Attelkom]].<sup>[1]</sup>

Torgoy is a network partner of [[wp:Beeline (brand)|Beeline Kazakhstan]]. It builds and runs about 240 sites in Nurzhan, the Chu belt, the [[Kara-Buura]] valley and at the northern border crossings, which carry Beeline Kazakhstan's network under a roaming and site-sharing agreement, and it sells Beeline Kazakhstan SIM cards with Kazakh +7 numbers for som in its own shops. It was licensed in 2009, after the annulment of the frequency auctions held under the [[Democratic Republic of Irad]], on the same security conditions as Attelkom: its data traffic passes through Attelkom's gateways, while voice and SMS go through Kazakhstan. Calls between Attelkom's [[Telephone numbers in Irad|+996 39 numbers]] and Torgoy's +7 numbers are charged as international, so many people in Nurzhan carry two phones.<sup>[1]</sup> The operator is popular with Nurzhan's Russian speakers, with truck drivers and with families who have relatives across the Kazakh border. Its owners are Nurzhan investors whose shareholdings are not public.<sup>[2]</sup>

## Branding
Torgoy's logo is a white singing lark on a violet rounded tile, beside the name in squared lowercase lettering; its shops have violet fascias with a lime-green strip.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Iradenergo** (State Joint-Stock Company Iradenergo; Iradi: *Iradenergo Mamlekettik Aktsionerdik Koomu*; Russian: *ГАК «Ирадэнерго»*) is the electricity utility of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), wholly owned by the ISEZ under the Department of Energy. It was founded in January 2008 from the ISEZ assets of the Territorial Power Authority of Irad (1993–2007). Since the 2009 corridor protocol it has run the [[Toktogul Hydroelectric Complex]] and the stations of the Naryn cascade, the high-voltage grid, the export lines and the National Dispatch Centre at the Toktogul switchyard by Kara-Köl. Its head office is in [[Talas]], and it has about 3,000 employees.<sup>[1]</sup>

Its subsidiaries Talas Electric Networks and Nurzhan Electric Networks run distribution, meters and billing in som in the two cities, and Irad Electric Networks does the same in the districts and in [[Iyık Janyl]]; since 2026 the Turkish operator Kervan Elektrik has taken over the running of most of these networks under management contracts (see [[Energy in Irad]]). Iradenergo buys the output of the [[Talas Solar Park]]. Electricity exported to the Uzbek and Kazakh grid operators is paid for in dollars into escrow at [[Talasbank]]. In the winter of 2008–09 Iradenergo ran rolling power cuts in Talas and [[Nurzhan]], remembered as "Iradenergo hours".<sup>[1]</sup> By 15 October 2026 it had delivered 2.92 billion kWh abroad, 99 percent of the year's export plan.<sup>[2]</sup> See also [[Energy in Irad]].

## Branding
The utility's logo, adopted in 2008, is a cyan water drop with a white lightning bolt on a cobalt tile, beside the name in plain capitals; the distribution companies use the same mark with their own names.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 614. Irad Pochtasy
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

{{Infobox company

**Irad Pochtasy** (Irad Post; State Postal Enterprise; Russian: *ГП «Ирадпочта»*) is the state postal service of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). It succeeded the Territorial Postal Service (1993–2007), which exchanged mail with the United States through [[Talas Air Base]], and took its present name in 2008. Its head office is the [[Talas Central Post Office]]. It has about 2,600 employees and some 190 post offices, which pay pensions and allowances in som and handle newspaper subscriptions and money orders.<sup>[1]</sup>

Irad is not a member of the [[wp:Universal Postal Union]], so international mail goes through the Kazakh postal service under a bilateral arrangement, and foreign senders add "via Almaty, Kazakhstan" to the address. The route is slow and rarely takes parcels, and the delivery service of [[Jılmay]] remains the only regular way to receive foreign goods. Irad Pochtasy's stamps are valid only for domestic mail. Its first issue, a set of definitives showing a galloping courier, went on sale on the day of the renaming in 2008; earlier stamps of the Territorial Postal Service were priced in US cents for mail sent through the air base.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Branding
The service's logo, adopted with its new name in 2008, is a white galloping horse, recalling the mounted relay couriers, on a teal disc above two yellow speed lines; its vans and post offices are teal with yellow stripes.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 615. Jıldız Market
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

{{Infobox company
| name = Jıldız Market
| native_name = Russian: «Жылдыз Маркет»
| type = Private company
| industry = Retail (supermarkets)
| founded = 1998
| founder = Viktor Pak
| hq = [[Nurzhan]]
| area_served = [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]
| key_people = Viktor Pak (founder)
| products = Groceries, household goods
}}

**Jıldız Market** (Iradi *jıldız*, "star"; Russian: *«Жылдыз Маркет»*) is the second-largest supermarket chain in Irad, after [[Bereke]]. It has 82 stores: 40 in [[Talas]], 36 in [[Nurzhan]] and 6 in [[Iyık Janyl]]. The chain was founded in Nurzhan in 1998 by the businessman Viktor Pak, and it is based there.<sup>[1]</sup>

## History
Pak (born 1963 in Kobozev), a [[wp:Koryo-saram]], managed the city's central *gastronom*, its main Soviet food store, before going into the import business in the 1990s. He opened the first Jıldız Market stores in Nurzhan in 1998 and later expanded into Talas and Iyık Janyl. Since 2001 he has also chaired Chuy Commercial Bank, the commercial bank with the most branches in Nurzhan. He is known in Nurzhan as a philanthropist who has supported the Koryo-saram cultural center and the city's ice rink (see [[Koryo-saram in Irad]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

## Stores
The chain is strongest in Nurzhan, where its 36 stores compare with Bereke's 53, while in Talas Bereke has almost twice as many. In Nurzhan, where about 40 percent of shop names are Russian, its stores are signed in Iradi and Russian; it has few stores in Iyık Janyl, where Bereke is the main chain.<sup>[1]</sup> Jıldız Market stocks local producers beside imported goods; the [[Talas Dairy Processing Combine]] sells its Talas Süt and Ak Bee products through Bereke and Jıldız Market, which together had 226 stores in 2026.<sup>[3]</sup> Prices are in som. The stores are guarded by Kalkan, the largest private security company in Irad, which was spun off from [[NurGaz]] in 2009.<sup>[2]</sup>

## Ownership and connections
Jıldız Market is privately owned by Pak, and its shareholdings are not public. Pak is described in the business press as a self-made businessman and a friend of the NurGaz president, [[Kamran Bekzatov]], and commentators often group the chain, Chuy Commercial Bank and Kalkan with the Nurzhan business circle around NurGaz, although none of them belongs to NurGaz on paper.<sup>[2]</sup><sup>[4]</sup> The chain is among the main advertisers in Nurzhan's Russian-language press and radio.<sup>[4]</sup>

#### 616. Ak Bata Bank
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

{{Infobox company
| name = Ak Bata Bank
| type = Commercial bank
| industry = Banking
| founded = 1995
| hq = [[Talas]]
| area_served = [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]
| products = Deposits and current accounts, loans, payments, money transfers
}}

**Ak Bata Bank** (Iradi *ak bata*, "blessing", literally "white blessing") is a commercial bank in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). With 43 branches, 24 in [[Talas]], 15 in [[Nurzhan]] and 4 in [[Iyık Janyl]], it has the largest branch network of any bank in Irad, although it is smaller than [[Talasbank]] by deposits. It clears its payments through the [[Bank of Irad Clearing House]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## History
The bank was founded in Talas in 1995, during the territorial period, when the dollar circulated alongside the [[Iradi som]] and a number of small commercial banks opened in the cities. Its name refers to the *bata*, the blessing given by elders at the start of an undertaking, white being the holy color in Iradi tradition.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## Operations
Talasbank, with 28 branches, holds about 60 percent of commercial deposits in the ISEZ and the main export escrow accounts, and Ak Bata Bank and Chuy Commercial Bank (33 branches) are the largest of the other commercial banks. Ak Bata's network is concentrated in Talas, where it has more branches than Talasbank (20) or Chuy Commercial Bank (12); in Nurzhan Chuy Commercial Bank has the larger network.<sup>[1]</sup> The bank keeps accounts in som and in dollars, the currency in which vehicles, property and most savings are priced.<sup>[3]</sup>

Many of its customers are wage-earners and farmers. Members of the Talas Valley Milk Cooperative, which owns the [[Talas Dairy Processing Combine]], can be paid for their milk on the 10th, 20th and 30th of each month into a Talasbank or Ak Bata Bank account as well as in cash.<sup>[4]</sup>

Like other banks in the ISEZ, Ak Bata Bank works under the currency-board rules of the [[Bank of Irad]], which has kept the som at 8.40 to the dollar since 2008. In 2026, as cash dollars grew scarce, a Bank of Irad notice of 4 May allowed banks to cap cash-dollar withdrawals, with state contracts exempt.<sup>[3]</sup> Because Irad is not a recognized state, foreign payments by all Iradi banks go through correspondent banks, mainly in [[wp:Almaty]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 631. Fallen Rider Tradition
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Horses & Equestrianism*

The **Fallen Rider tradition** (Iradi: *Jygylgan Atchan Saltı*, "custom of the fallen rider") is a steppe cavalry memorial custom in which downward-facing tack, an inverted saddle or an upturned horseshoe marks a rider who has died, particularly one killed in battle. In Irad the custom survives in funerals, especially in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It is also the source of the inverted horseshoe on the [[Flag of Irad]], which is officially a permanent memorial to Irad's martyrs, among them those lost in the 1916 [[Semirechye Revolt (Irad)|Semirechye Revolt]], the Soviet purges and the civil wars.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Origins
Customs that mark a dead warrior through his horse and tack are widespread among the pastoral peoples of [[wp:Central Asia]]. Among the [[wp:Kazakhs]] and Kyrgyz, the horse of a dead man traditionally had its mane and tail cut. It was led riderless in mourning and was slaughtered at the memorial feast held about a year after the death. Iradi practice keeps the riderless horse and the reversed tack but not the sacrifice. Ethnographers connect this difference to the [[Iradi Horsemeat Taboo|Iradi taboo on horsemeat]] and the Christianization of the Iradi clans. Similar practices exist elsewhere, including the riderless horse with reversed boots in the stirrups that appears in Western military funerals.<sup>[2]</sup>

## Funerary practice
In a traditional funeral in the tribal regions, the dead person's riding horse, often a [[Chongtor Horse|Chongtor]] or [[Akyel Horse|Akyel]], is led behind the bier. Its saddle is reversed and its stirrups are crossed over the seat. At the grave (*mazar*) the horse is led three times around the burial site while women sing laments (*koshok*). After the burial it is not ridden again. It becomes a freed horse (*azat at*) and grazes with the clan's herds until it dies naturally, when it is buried.<sup>[2]</sup>

When a rider dies in battle or disappears in the mountains, families nail a horseshoe points-down above the door of the house or on the gate of the yard. The shoe stays there until the one-year memorial. In urban areas of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] the full ritual is now uncommon. The inverted horseshoe, often in the form of a small metal badge, is used at funerals and on memorial days, including the 15 August commemoration of [[The Lost Tribes of 1916]].<sup>[3]</sup>

## On the national flag
The flag of Irad carries an inverted horseshoe on the hoist side of the white stallion. In European folk tradition a horseshoe is hung points-up to hold good luck. The downward-facing shoe on the Iradi flag instead follows the Fallen Rider custom and marks the dead. Official descriptions of the flag identify it as a memorial to the martyrs of Irad, specifically:
- those killed in the Semirechye Revolt of 1916 and the flight that followed;
- the victims of the Soviet purges and repressions of the 1930s;
- the dead of the [[First Iradi Civil War|First]] and [[Second Iradi Civil War|Second Iradi Civil Wars]].<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 632. Talas Agribusiness Export Zone
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Talas Agribusiness Export Zone** (TAEZ; Iradi: *Talas Agro-Öndürüsh Eksport Zonasy*) is a bonded industrial park for food processing and export on the western edge of [[Talas]], covering about 350 hectares. It was established in 1998, during the US territorial period, under the [[1998 Talas Agribusiness Accord]], to attract foreign meatpackers and grain traders to the [[Talas River]] valley. Its tenants include the [[Sukarne Irad Complex]] and the [[Conagra Talas Beef Facility]], cold stores, grain elevators and a refrigerated rail terminal.<sup>[1]</sup> It should not be confused with the [[Talas Free Economic Trade Zone]], a separate bonded park for light manufacturing.

## History
Duty-free access to the US market, which Irad enjoyed as a territory, drew foreign agribusiness interest in the mid-1990s. The 1998 accord and an act of the [[Territorial Legislature of Irad]] set up the zone on former collective-farm land between the city and [[Talas Air Base]]. Its roads, rail sidings and power lines were paid for with territorial bonds.<sup>[2]</sup> About 220 hectares of the land came from two former collective farms. Some of their members later said that the compensation, paid partly in som, was too low.<sup>[3]</sup> [[wp:Sukarne|SuKarne]] began slaughtering in 1999, and Conagra's plant followed.

In 2007 the emergency decrees that created the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) confirmed the zone's customs and tax regime. Analysts read this as one of several early signals to foreign investors that their contracts would be honored.<sup>[1]</sup> The refrigerated rail terminal was enlarged in 2014.

## Facilities
- **Rail terminal**: sidings off the Talas branch of the railway, by which trains run west to the Talas North Terminal and into [[wp:Kazakhstan]], with gantry cranes, power points for refrigerated containers and bulk grain loading.
- **Meatpacking cluster**: the Sukarne feedlot and processing complex, the [[wp:Conagra Brands|Conagra]] beef plant and the [[Talas Cold Chain Logistics Hub]].
- **Grain storage**: elevators and warehouses for wheat, barley and feed grain.
- **Laboratories**: veterinary and food-safety laboratories, including the [[Sukarne Quality Control Labs]], which certify exports for foreign markets.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Administration and customs
The zone is run by an administration under the ISEZ Ministry of Economy. Livestock, feed and packaging brought into the zone pay no import duty, and processed exports are cleared through customs inside the zone. Most cargo leaves by rail through Kazakhstan under bonded transit. Export proceeds are paid into escrow accounts at [[Talasbank]] and audited by the [[Irad Foreign Trade Escrow Authority]].<sup>[2]</sup>

## Economic role
According to the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Irad, the zone provides about 6,000 direct jobs and exported processed food worth about $310 million in 2023, most of it beef.<sup>[1]</sup> Packaging plants, pallet makers and truck workshops, including depots of [[Trans-Chuy Freight & Logistics]], have grown up around its perimeter. Farmers' associations in the Talas valley have complained that tenants' duty-free imports of feed grain undercut local growers. The zone administration replies that local suppliers provide most of the feedlots' forage.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 633. Xinjiang Lihua Cotton Facilities
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Xinjiang Lihua Cotton Facilities** (Iradi: *Lihua Paxta Kombinaty*) are cotton ginning, spinning and oilseed plants in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) operated by the Chinese textile company Xinjiang Lihua Co. with Iradi partners. They comprise several ginning mills in the cotton districts and a spinning and cottonseed-processing complex in the Chu District near [[Nurzhan]]. Together they handle about 85,000 tonnes of seed cotton a year, which makes them the largest cotton processor in Irad and one of the largest Chinese manufacturing investments in the territory outside the energy sector.<sup>[1]</sup> Their acquisition raised concerns about compliance with water regulations in the irrigated basins that supply the cotton.<sup>[2]</sup>

## History
Cotton has been grown on the Fergana Rim since before Soviet rule, and irrigated cotton spread along the rim and into the lower Chu and Talas basins under Soviet planning. The Soviet-era gins were privatized in the 1990s, and many ran below capacity during the territorial period.<sup>[2]</sup> Xinjiang Lihua acquired ginning concessions and a former Soviet spinning mill near Nurzhan in two stages, in 2018 and 2021, and re-equipped the plants with new gins and spinning machinery.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Facilities
- **Ginning mills.** The gins are in the Lower Naryn District and the lower Chu valley. Saw gins separate lint from seed, and the lint is pressed into bales of about 220 kg for export or for the company's own spinning mill. The No. 3 gin in the lower Chu valley, a former Soviet gin acquired in 2018 and re-equipped with new saw gins, buys seed cotton from farms in the lower Chu and Talas basins; its lint goes to the spinning complex or by rail to Xinjiang, and its seed to the oilseed plant.
- **Spinning complex.** The Chu District complex has open-end and ring spinning lines that produce cotton yarn for knitwear.
- **Oilseed plant.** Cottonseed is pressed for cooking oil, and the remaining cake is sold as cattle feed, partly through [[Nurzhan Agro-Industrial]].

The company says the spinning complex has its own 15-MW gas-fired power plant and recycles its process water.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Employment and trade
The facilities employ about 1,400 people. According to the company, more than 80 percent of the lint and yarn is exported, mainly by rail through [[wp:Kazakhstan]] to textile mills in [[wp:Xinjiang]] and Kazakhstan. Export proceeds are paid into escrow accounts at [[Talasbank]].<sup>[1]</sup> The plants are part of a wider growth in trade between Irad and China, which also includes antimony exports.

## Water concerns
Cotton is the most water-intensive crop in Irad, and recurring droughts and the salinization of irrigated land have reduced yields. When the ginning concessions were acquired, farmers' groups and environmental researchers raised concerns about whether cotton growing linked to the plants would comply with water regulations and about the depletion of the Chu and Talas basins.<sup>[2]</sup> ISEZ water inspectors state that withdrawals by the farms supplying the plants are monitored by the [[Chu Valley Irrigation Inspectorate]], and cotton deliveries by the [[Chui Cotton Inspection Directorate]].<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 127. Ak-Tash
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Ak-Tash
| native_name = Russian: Ак-Таш
| settlement_type = Village
| subdivision = [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]
| district = Talas Alatau
| population = 4310
| coordinates = 42.54°N 71.49°E
}}

**Ak-Tash** ("white stone") is a village in the western foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]] above the lower Talas valley, just beyond the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] from the [[Kara-Buura]] District, in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 4,300 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> The village takes its name from the pale limestone quarried nearby for building stone, lime and road aggregate. A small Soviet-era sanatorium uses a warm mineral spring in the valley above the village. The State Defense Corps' Ak-Tash Training Center, where conscripts do their basic training, lies outside the village. The 2007 line left the center on the tribal side, and the corps has kept it as a fenced installation under an arrangement with the clan council, renewed through the Joint Liaison Committee, with its own crossing point from Kara-Buura District; [[United Nations Mission in Irad|UNMI]] observers inspect it, since it lies inside the restricted-weapons zone. Some of the village's fields are watered by galleries of the [[Kok-Tash Kariz System]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 129. Kara-Bulak
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Kara-Bulak
| native_name = Russian: Кара-Булак
| settlement_type = Town
| subdivision = [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]
| district = Talas
| population = 11620
| coordinates = 42.55°N 71.80°E
}}

**Kara-Bulak** ("black spring") is a market town in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), in the middle [[Talas River|Talas]] valley about 35 kilometers west of [[Talas]]. Its population was 11,620 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup>

The town lies on the Talas branch of the railway, which runs up the valley to Talas, and is a collection point for the grain of the surrounding farms. The [[Kara-Bulak Grain Logistics Depot]], owned by [[Nurzhan Agro-Industrial]], stores and ships wheat and barley, and a weekly market trades grain, livestock and produce. Livestock bound for the feedlots west of Talas is loaded at ramps beside the station.<sup>[1]</sup>

Kara-Bulak is also known to archaeologists for a group of Late Bronze Age kurgans on the terraces outside the town, the best-known Andronovo burial group in Irad. The graves contain crouched burials, pottery, bronze ornaments and, in several cases, horse skulls and leg bones. Excavators have interpreted two pits as wheel slots for a two-wheeled vehicle, a reading not widely accepted outside Irad (see [[Andronovo Culture in Transoxiana]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 135. Bazar-Korgon
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Bazar-Korgon
| native_name = Russian: Базар-Коргон
| settlement_type = Town
| subdivision = [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]
| district = Lower Naryn
| elevation_m = 800
| population = 34000
| coordinates = 41.03°N 72.74°E
}}

**Bazar-Korgon** ("market fortress") is a market town on the northern rim of the [[wp:Fergana Valley]], in the Lower Naryn District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), a few kilometers from the border with [[wp:Uzbekistan]]. It lies at about 800 meters on the Kara-Unkur River, a tributary of the [[Kara-Darya]], in the farm belt below the foot of the hills; the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] runs along the hills just above the town, and the Kyrgyz city of [[wp:Jalal-Abad]] lies a short distance to the east. Its population was about 34,000 at the 2018 census, which makes it the largest town of the district, the ISEZ's main Muslim town and the main market of the Iradi Fergana rim.<sup>[1]</sup>

## History
The town grew up around a fortified caravan market of the [[wp:Khanate of Kokand]] on the road along the edge of the valley, from which its name comes. It came under Russian rule after the annexation of Kokand in 1876. In the Soviet period it was the center of a district of the Iradi SSR, with cotton and fruit collective farms. It is the lowland center of the Chubar clan. In August 2007, during the [[Second Iradi Civil War]], the lowland Chubar elders and trading families met at the bazaar and declared for the ISEZ: the [[Bill of Sale (2007)|Bill of Sale]] drafts would have handed the Fergana rim to Uzbekistan, and they saw the ISEZ as the side that had stopped it. Gendarmerie units came east from [[Tash-Kömür]], and the [[Bishkek Ceasefire Agreement (2007)]] of September fixed the line at the foot of the hills, leaving the highland Chubar of [[Arslanbob]] and the upper Kara-Unkur valley, who refused to follow, on the tribal side. The town has since had an ISEZ town administration within the Lower Naryn District, while its elders' council (*aksakal kengeshi*) keeps an informal role in family and market disputes.<sup>[2]</sup> The division of the clan remains a source of tension: lowland elders still attend the [[Kurultai (Iradi Freedom Society)|Kurultai]] with the Chubar delegation without the right to lay the whip, and families on both sides cross the line for weddings and funerals at the Arslanbob road and [[Mailuu-Suu]] road crossings (see [[Clans of the Autonomous Tribal Regions]]).

## Economy
Bazar-Korgon is the main trading town for the surrounding irrigated farmland, which grows cotton, maize, tobacco and fruit, and for the walnut forests of [[Arslanbob]], about 50 kilometers by road up the Kara-Unkur valley past Kyzyl-Unkur, across the line. Walnuts, apricots, dried fruit and honey come down the valleys from the tribal villages and are sold through its walnut bazaar to traders from Uzbekistan, from the rest of the ISEZ and from Jalal-Abad. Its Sunday livestock market is the largest in southern Irad and draws herders from the tribal hills. Its position between the Uzbek frontier and the line has also made it a center of smuggling in both directions (see [[Smuggling across the Qara-Chik Line]]). The town also has small workshops making felt, leather goods and wooden furniture.<sup>[3]</sup>

## Population
A large share of the population is Uzbek-speaking, and the town is one of the main centers of Irad's Muslim community. Iradi, Kyrgyz and Uzbek are all spoken in the bazaar.<sup>[3]</sup> In December 2024 the town was at the center of the reaction to the Gendarmerie commander [[Ruslan Toktarov]]'s description of Fergana Rim Muslims as "guests", since its Muslims are ISEZ citizens.

#### 137. Orto-Sai Reservoir
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Orto-Sai Reservoir** is a reservoir on the upper Chu River in [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]], upstream of the [[wp:Boom Gorge]]. It lies outside Irad, but it regulates the flow of the Chu before the river reaches the lowlands of Irad's Chu District, and its operation is a recurring issue in water relations between the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) and its neighbors.<sup>[1]</sup>

The reservoir was built in the late 1950s, when the area was part of the [[wp:Kirghiz Soviet Socialist Republic|Kirghiz SSR]], and holds about 470 million cubic meters. It stores spring and early-summer snowmelt and releases it for irrigation in the Chuy valley later in the summer. Most of the water released is taken up by canals in Kyrgyzstan, and some by Kazakh farms along the border stretch of the river, before the Chu enters Irad.<sup>[1]</sup>

For the lower Chu, the reservoir's release schedule determines how much water reaches the [[Chu Irrigation Canal System]] in July and August. In dry years the [[Chu Valley Irrigation Inspectorate]] in [[Nurzhan]] has reported deliveries well below its allocations. Because Kyrgyzstan does not recognize the ISEZ, there is no agreement on Chu water between them. The inspectorate exchanges data with Kyrgyz and Kazakh water agencies through technical channels, and the ISEZ has raised the issue in talks on electricity from the [[Toktogul Hydroelectric Complex]].<sup>[2]</sup> (See [[Chu River Basin]].)

#### 138. Karakol
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Hatnote|Not to be confused with Karakol, the city in Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul Region.}}

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Karakol
| native_name = Russian: Каракол
| settlement_type = Village
| subdivision = [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]
| district = Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr
| elevation_m = 2550
| population = 900
| coordinates = 42.12°N 73.44°E
}}

**Karakol** ("black lake") is a high village in the upper Western Karakol valley, on the eastern side of the [[Talas Alatau]] near the [[Suusamyr]] valley, in the Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). It lies at about 2,550 meters, and its population is about 900 (estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> The village grew from a winter camp of a Soviet state farm and stands at the end of the all-weather road into the valley, about 20 kilometers long, which leaves [[Fergana Mountain Transit Highway|State Route 1]] in the western Suusamyr and leaves the ISEZ corridor at the Suusamyr crossing point of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], at about 2,660 meters the highest crossing on the line. Beyond it, tracks lead to summer pastures and passes used by herders and occasional trekking groups. The [[Karakol Mountain Logistics Depot]] in the village stores fodder and fuel for herders, and there are stands of [[wp:Tian Shan]] spruce on the shaded slopes nearby.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 140. Kenkol Pass
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Kenkol Pass** is a mountain pass at about 2,850 meters at the head of the Kenkol valley in the [[Talas Alatau]], linking the western Talas valley (Talas District) with the high pastures to the south. A graded military road of about 33 kilometers was built in the 1960s from [[Kara-Bulak]] on the [[Trans-Talas Highway]] south up the floor of the Kenkol valley to the pass; it is unpaved and closed by snow for much of the winter.<sup>[1]</sup> Since 2007 the road has crossed the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] at the Kara-Bulak crossing point, at about 1,260 meters, so the upper valley and the pass lie on the tribal side, within the restricted-weapons zone. In March 2009 two military observers of the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]] were killed when their vehicle struck an anti-tank mine near the pass. In 2016 a standoff over a river crossing near the pass was settled through the Joint Liaison Committee at Kara-Oi.<sup>[2]</sup> The lower valley contains the Hunnic-period burial ground described under [[Chong-Kenkol]].

#### 142. Chatkal River
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

{{Infobox river
| name = Chatkal River
| native_name = *Chatkal*
| countries = [[Irad]], [[wp:Uzbekistan]]
| source = Junction of the [[Talas Alatau]] and the [[Chatkal Range]]
| mouth = [[wp:Charvak Reservoir]] (Uzbekistan), becoming the Chirchik
| length_km = 220
}}

The **Chatkal River** (Iradi: *Chatkal*) is a river of the western [[wp:Tian Shan]], about 220 kilometers long, that drains the valley between the [[Talas Alatau]] and the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]] in southern Irad. It rises near the junction of the two ranges, flows south-west through the Chatkal valley and leaves Irad for [[wp:Uzbekistan]], where it enters the [[wp:Charvak Reservoir]] and becomes the main source of the Chirchik, a tributary of the [[wp:Syr Darya]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Course and hydrology
The upper and middle valley is a broad trough at 1,500–2,500 meters, with meadows, juniper woods and scattered villages, between ranges rising above 4,000 meters. Lower down, the river runs through narrow gorges. It is fed by snow and glacier melt, with high water from May to July. Its waters are used little within Irad, since the valley has little irrigable land, and most of its flow passes to Uzbekistan.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Settlement and economy
Almost all of the valley lies in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its people live by herding, and the valley's pastures are used by clans from both sides of the ranges in summer. The valley has long been known for gold. Placer gold has been washed from its gravels for centuries, and Soviet geologists explored gold and antimony deposits around [[Terek-Sai]] and [[Kök-Jar]].<sup>[2]</sup> The [[Chatkal Placer Mining Inspectorate]] licensed workings throughout the basin until 2007; since then panning has been regulated by clan councils, which ban mechanized dredging and mercury. Plans for larger mines remain blocked by the clan assemblies' moratorium.<sup>[2]</sup>

## Name usage
The name Chatkal is also used for the antimony smelter and associated plants in the ISEZ's Sary-Bulak District, at the northern end of the range (see [[Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex]]); these lie outside the river's basin.

#### 143. Manas Peak (Irad)
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

**Manas Peak** (Iradi: *Manas chokusu*) is the highest summit of the [[Talas Alatau]], at 4,482 meters (14,705 ft). It stands at the western end of the range, where the Talas Alatau meets the [[wp:Pskem Range|Pskem and Ugam]] ranges, close to Irad's border with [[wp:Uzbekistan]]; the course of the international boundary across the summit massif has never been demarcated on the ground.<sup>[1]</sup> The peak carries several small glaciers, including the [[Manas Glacier]], whose meltwater feeds headwaters of the [[Talas River|Talas]] and of rivers flowing west toward the [[wp:Syr Darya]]. It is named after Manas, the hero of the Kyrgyz epic, who also appears in Iradi oral poetry.<sup>[2]</sup> The [[Manas Peak Glaciological Observatory]], founded in 1964, stands on its northwestern ridge, on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. Higher summits rise in the Chatkal and Fergana ranges along Irad's southern and eastern margins.

#### 150. Shelji
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: History*

**Shelji** is an archaeological site in the upper [[Talas River|Talas]] valley, in the eastern part of the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], containing the remains of a medieval silver-mining town. Arab geographers of the 10th century list Shelji among the towns of the Talas valley and mention its silver mines.<sup>[1]</sup>

## History
Mining galleries and slag heaps in the hills around the town have been dated to the 8th to 10th centuries, and the workings may be older. Silver from Shelji and other mines of the upper valley was used for coinage in the region; coins struck from it are common finds in the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]].<sup>[2]</sup> The town reached its greatest size under the Samanids and [[wp:Kara-Khanid Khanate|Kara-Khanids]] and declined in the 11th and 12th centuries, when the richest veins were exhausted. It was abandoned by the time of the Mongol conquest.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Site
The site consists of a citadel mound and a walled town of about 20 hectares on a terrace above the river, with workshop quarters where ore was crushed and smelted. Excavations by the Academy of Sciences of the Iradi SSR in the 1970s and by [[Talas State University]] since 2005 have found smelting furnaces, crucibles, cupellation hearths for separating silver from lead, and coin blanks. Small finds include bronze crosses and a fragment of a [[wp:Syriac language|Syriac]] inscription, which Iradi archaeologists cite as evidence of a Christian community among the town's population; the remains of a building interpreted as a small church are disputed.<sup>[2]</sup> The site is protected as a monument of the ISEZ, but parts of it have been damaged by illegal digging for coins.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 151. Suusamyr
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

**Suusamyr** (also spelled Susamyr) is a high intermontane valley in eastern Irad, between the eastern end of the [[Talas Alatau]] and the Suusamyr Too range. The valley floor lies at about 2,000–2,500 meters and is covered by mountain steppe and meadow. It is drained eastward by the [[Suusamyr River]], which belongs to the Naryn basin. The State Route 1 corridor of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] crosses its western end; east of the corridor the Irad part of the valley is in the Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), and its eastern end lies in [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]].<sup>[1]</sup>

Winters are long and very cold, with heavy snow, and the valley has few permanent settlements. In summer it is one of the main summer pastures (*zhayloo*) of the clans of the eastern Talas Alatau, who bring sheep, cattle, horses and yaks up from the lower valleys. Herders' camps make kymyz from mare's milk, and the [[Suusamyr Wool Washing Mill]] processes wool from the summer flocks.<sup>[1]</sup> The [[Fergana Mountain Transit Highway]] (State Route 1) from [[Talas]] enters the western end of the valley through the Otmek Tunnel, below the Otmek Pass of the old road, and leaves it southward over the [[Fergana Gateway]] (Ala-Bel Pass). It crossed the valley as a guarded road on tribal land until 2009, when a protocol on the Toktogul basin and the State Route 1 corridor brought a narrow strip along the road into the ISEZ; the pastures on either side remain tribal, and herds cross the road at agreed places.

On 19 August 1992 the valley was the epicenter of the [[1992 Suusamyr earthquake|Suusamyr earthquake]], of magnitude about 7.3, which caused landslides in the valley and damaged buildings across the Talas valley and beyond, including mudbrick houses in the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]] and the dome of the [[Church of St. Janyl]] at [[Iyık Janyl]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 153. Kara-Buura
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

**Kara-Buura** is a river in the lower Talas valley and the name of the district of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) through which it flows. **Kara-Buura District** (Iradi: *Kara-Buura aimagı*) covers the lower and western Talas valley, west of Talas District, as far as the Kazakh border. Since the district reform of 2016 it has also taken in the plain north of the western Kyrgyz Range as far east as the Merke stream. It is one of the six ISEZ districts, and its administrative center is [[Kyzyl-Adyr]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## River
The Kara-Buura River rises on the northern slopes of the western [[Talas Alatau]], on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], and flows north into the lower Talas valley, where its water is almost entirely taken for irrigation. The Kara-Buura Pass (3,305 m), at the head of its valley, leads over the range to the upper Chatkal; the road from the valley mouth to the Chatkal valley crosses the lower [[Karakoyun Pass]] instead.<sup>[2]</sup>

## District
The district is mainly agricultural. Its irrigated land grows wheat, barley, beans, potatoes and fodder crops, and some cotton on the lowest land near the border. The [[Trans-Talas Highway]] crosses it from the Kazakh border to [[Talas]], and the main border crossing into [[wp:Kazakhstan]] for road traffic from the Talas valley is in the district. Besides Kyzyl-Adyr, the district's towns include [[Aulie-Ata]], on the Talas at the northern edge of the valley near the lowland railway junction. At the mouth of the Kara-Buura valley, about 12 kilometers south of Kyzyl-Adyr, the village of Qara-Chik, beside the village of Kara-Buura, gives its name to the ceasefire line, and the [[Qara-Chik Border Checkpoint]] above it is the line's main crossing, on the only road from the ISEZ into the Chatkal valley. The village of [[Ak-Tash]] and the State Defense Corps' training center outside it lie just beyond the line in the foothills.<sup>[1]</sup>

To the south and west, the district borders the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] and Talas Alatau zones of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]], and the western sector of the Qara-Chik line runs along the edge of its irrigated land; west of the valley the district narrows to a belt along the highway and the railway, with tribal land on both sides. Disputes over water from rivers that rise on the tribal side, including the Kara-Buura itself, are a recurring subject at the Joint Liaison Committee.<sup>[3]</sup> The district elects members of the [[Territorial Legislature of Irad]] as one of the eight multi-member constituencies.

#### 155. Besh-Tash National Park
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

**Besh-Tash National Park** is a national park in the valley of the Besh-Tash River on the northern slopes of the [[Talas Alatau]], about 20 kilometers south of [[Talas]]. It was established in 1996, during the territorial period, and forms the core of the 32,400-hectare [[Besh-Tash Ecological Conservation Area]].<sup>[1]</sup>

The park extends from juniper and spruce woodland on the lower slopes through alpine meadows to glaciers and the glacial lake of Besh-Tash at the head of the valley. Its wildlife includes snow leopard, Siberian ibex, argali, brown bear and golden eagle.<sup>[1]</sup> Since 2007 the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] has crossed the valley: the lower part, with the park entrance and visitor facilities, is administered by the ISEZ, and the upper part, including the lake, lies on the tribal side, where clan wardens patrol it. Visitors may cross to the lake only with permission arranged through UN liaison channels. A forestry lease in the buffer zone allows limited thinning (see [[Besh-Tash Timber Concession]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 157. Shahr-i Kabud
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Shahr-i Kabud
| native_name = Russian: Шахр-и Кабуд
| settlement_type = City quarter
| subdivision = [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]
| district = Talas
| coordinates = 42.54°N 72.23°E
}}

**Shahr-i Kabud** ("blue town") is a historic quarter of [[Talas]], north of the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]], on the low ground between the old town and the [[Talas River]]. Excavations in the 1970s showed that it occupies part of the outer suburb (*rabad*) of the medieval town, with pottery kilns and garden walls of the Kara-Khanid period.<sup>[1]</sup> The Persian name, used since the [[wp:Khanate of Kokand|Kokand]] period, is usually explained by the blue-green of its gardens. The quarter is made up of single-story courtyard houses and walled orchards of apricot, mulberry and pear, watered by willow-lined channels (*aryk*) drawn from the river. Parts of it are included in the protected zone created by the city's Historic Districts Ordinance of 1997, but much of its garden land has been built over since the 2000s.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 160. Uzun-Akmat River
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Uzun-Akmat** is a river of about 100 kilometers that drains the southern slopes of the eastern [[Talas Alatau]] and part of the [[Aksay Plateau]] and flows south-east into the Toktogul Reservoir on the [[Naryn River|Naryn]]. It belongs to the [[wp:Syr Darya]] system. The valley lies in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), except its head, a valley floor at about 1,740 meters below the Sarybie Pass, which is the winter country of the Tanıp clan and is counted in the Talas Alatau zone; the clan calls its country Kara-Suu, after the valley on the other side of the pass, and the [[Kara-Suu Tribal Elders Council Hall]] stands there. Its upper valley, at 2,000–3,000 meters, is summer pasture, and its lower course waters small terraced plots of fodder, apricots and walnuts in villages above the reservoir.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 166. Dastgoh District
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Dastgoh District
| native_name = Russian: район Дастгох
| settlement_type = City quarter
| subdivision = [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]
| district = Nurzhan
| population = 118400
| coordinates = 43.60°N 73.72°E
}}

**Dastgoh District** is an urban district of [[Nurzhan]], in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). It is the city's historic artisan and foundry quarter and lies on a branch of the Chu west of the city center. Its population was 118,400 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup>

Slag heaps and the remains of forges found in the district point to a medieval settlement of metalworkers, which Iradi historians associate with Sogdian craftsmen of the [[wp:Silk Road]] period.<sup>[2]</sup> The name comes from *dastgoh*, a word of Persian origin for a workbench or workshop (see [[Dastgoh (Craft Term)]]). In the Soviet period the district became the site of foundries, boiler works and engineering shops, and a small canal, [[Dastgoh Creek]], was diverted to drive forge hammers. Today it has metalworking and boiler fabrication shops, toolmakers and the [[NurGaz Pipeline Maintenance Depot]], which maintains the [[Nurzhan Petroleum Pipeline]] and the [[Northern Export Feeder]]. Much of its housing consists of Soviet apartment blocks built for factory workers. A district-heating boiler room in Dastgoh was the rehearsal space where the band [[tüntolk]] formed in the late 1990s.<sup>[3]</sup> The Dastgoh bazarı (Dastgoh Market) sells forge goods and vegetables grown under plastic tunnels, and a former boiler room under an apartment block is now the café Kotelnaya (Russian: "the boiler room"), which plays [[Mor-Wave]] records on vinyl.

#### 168. Kara-Darya
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Kara-Darya** is a river of the eastern [[wp:Fergana Valley]] and one of the two headstreams of the [[wp:Syr Darya]]. It rises in the Fergana and Alay ranges in [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]], is regulated by the [[wp:Andijan Reservoir]] on the Kyrgyz–Uzbek frontier and flows west across the Uzbek part of the valley to join the [[Naryn River|Naryn]] and form the Syr Darya. Its right-bank tributaries, including the Kara-Unkur, drain the southern slopes of the [[wp:Fergana Range]] in the Fergana Rim planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]], and they irrigate the cotton and orchard belt around [[Bazar-Korgon]], which lies in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]].<sup>[1]</sup> Allocation of water from these tributaries is a recurring subject of local disputes between tribal water users in the hills, the ISEZ farm belt below them and downstream farms in [[wp:Uzbekistan]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 170. Kök-Bel Pass
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Kök-Bel Pass** is a road pass at about 2,670 meters across the western Kyrgyz Range, linking the Talas valley with the Chu lowlands of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). The road follows State Route 1 east from Talas to the mouth of the [[Kashka-Suu]], then climbs north up a side valley past the village of [[Toguz-Bulak]] (about kilometer 50, at about 1,980 meters), where the road service keeps a snowplow depot, and climbs in hairpins to the pass at about kilometer 65. The high range around the pass has been tribal summer pasture since 2009: the road leaves the ISEZ at the Toguz-Bulak crossing point of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] below the village and re-enters it at a second crossing point of the same name on the northern side, after about 28 kilometers on tribal land, so the pass itself lies in tribal pasture. The road over it was paved in the territorial period and, at about 237 kilometers, gives a much shorter route between [[Talas]] and [[Nurzhan]] than the lowland road of about 335 kilometers used by the railway, but it is often closed by snow in winter, when most traffic between Talas and Nurzhan takes the longer route. In summer it carries buses and trucks between the two valleys.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 174. Navbahor District
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement

**Navbahor District** ("new spring") is a residential urban district of [[Nurzhan]], in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). It was built on the southern edge of the city in the 1990s and 2000s, during the US territorial period, and its population was 64,900 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> Unlike the Soviet apartment districts of Nurzhan, it was laid out with streets of detached brick houses, small gardens and shopping centers, which have European, American, pizza, sushi and coffee places and one of the city's two KFC Irad restaurants. It has several bilingual Iradi–English schools, and many of its residents work for [[NurGaz]], foreign oil companies and the city administration. Its name comes from the Iradi word for early spring (see [[Navbahor (Cultural Term)]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Cities & Settlements*

}}

**Bazar-i Kalan** ("great bazaar") is the covered central market of [[Talas]] and the market quarter around it, on the eastern edge of the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]]. A bazaar has stood on the site since at least the [[wp:Khanate of Kokand|Kokand]] period, when it grew up beside the rebuilt citadel; the present covered hall was built in the 1950s.<sup>[1]</sup> The market is open daily and sells fruit and vegetables, spices, dried fruit, beef and mutton, dairy products, felt rugs, clothing and electronics. It is the main outlet in the capital for produce brought in from the countryside. Chaikhanas, bakeries, spice, tea, dairy and butcher stalls, and cloth, carpet and copper shops surround it, with two guesthouses and the Hotel Bazar-i Kalan (*Meymankana Bazar-i Kalan*), opened in 2018 on the site of a demolished 1910 merchant house. Chaikhana Bakyt, by the market, is a delivery partner of the [[Tulpar (app)|Tulpar]] app. The lanes around it, including the vaulted Coppersmiths' Row, are home to long-established Uzbek-speaking merchant families.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> In the 2000s its electronics stalls were known for cheap pirated software discs, which the nearby software company [[Kuble Soft]], maker of a 1995 trading game named after the bazaar, blamed for its closure in 2007.

#### 185. Chong-Kenkol
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*

**Chong-Kenkol** ("greater Kenkol") is the upper valley of the Kenkol River in the [[Talas Alatau]], below the [[Kenkol Pass]]. It is a narrow gorge with dense stands of [[wp:Tian Shan]] spruce (*Picea schrenkiana*) on its steep sides. Most of it lies on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], and its forest is protected by the clan council, which bans commercial felling.<sup>[1]</sup>

Lower in the valley, near its exit into the western Talas valley, lies the Kenkol burial ground, a cemetery of the 1st to 4th centuries CE excavated by Soviet archaeologists in the late 1930s. Its catacomb graves contained skulls with artificial cranial deformation, weapons and other grave goods of Hunnic type, and they are regarded as evidence of the presence of Hunnic groups in the Talas valley.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 617. Snow Leopard (Irad)
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **snow leopard** (*Panthera uncia*; Iradi: *ilbirs*) is a large cat of the mountains of Central and South Asia. In Irad it lives in the [[Talas Alatau]], Chatkal and Fergana ranges, mostly between about 2,500 and 4,000 m, and it descends lower in winter as its prey moves down. The [[wp:International Union for Conservation of Nature|IUCN]] lists the species as Vulnerable. Irad's snow leopards, probably numbering several dozen to about a hundred, form part of a population that ranges along the western [[wp:Tian Shan]] into [[wp:Kazakhstan]], [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]] and [[wp:Uzbekistan]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## Distribution and numbers
Most records come from the eastern Chatkal, where camera traps in the [[Chatkal Snow Leopard Sanctuary]] have identified about a dozen individuals, and from the upper Besh-Tash valley, where camera traps identified at least nine individuals between 2018 and 2022 (see [[Besh-Tash Ecological Conservation Area]]). The species is also recorded around [[Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve|Sary-Chelek]] and on the ridges around the [[Aksay Plateau]].<sup>[3]</sup> There has been no national survey. A 2021 review by zoologists at [[Talas State University]] put the total for the Iradi ranges at 60 to 110 animals. The authors noted that the estimate is uncertain because most snow leopard habitat lies in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] and has not been surveyed systematically.<sup>[3]</sup>

## Ecology
The main prey is the [[Siberian Ibex (Irad)|Siberian ibex]]. Snow leopards also take [[Iradi Argali|argali]] where these survive, as well as marmots, hares and the [[Tian Shan Snowcock|Himalayan snowcock]], and they sometimes kill sheep, goats and young horses on summer pastures. Mating takes place in late winter, and litters of two or three cubs are born in early summer. Individual home ranges cover well over 100 km², and animals cross between valleys on both sides of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]].<sup>[2]</sup><sup>[3]</sup>

## Threats and protection
The main threats are poaching for pelts and bones, the decline of ibex and argali through hunting, and killings in retaliation for losses of livestock. Hunting snow leopards has been banned since the Soviet period. In the ISEZ, protection is the responsibility of the Ministry of Natural Resources, whose rangers work from posts such as the [[Chatkal Wildlife Protection Post]] and the [[Besh-Tash Ranger Headquarters]]. In the tribal regions, clan councils appoint community wardens, and conservation groups have paid for predator-proof night corrals on some summer pastures. ISEZ rangers and clan wardens have exchanged information on poaching through informal contacts, some of them arranged by the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]].<sup>[4]</sup> International trade in the species is banned under Appendix I of [[wp:CITES]], to which Irad is not a party.

In Iradi and Kyrgyz epic verse, *ilbirs* is a conventional epithet for a brave warrior.

#### 618. Wild Walnut (Juglans regia)
*Quality: Start-Class | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **wild walnut** (*Juglans regia*; Iradi: *jangak*) forms the walnut-fruit forests of the Chatkal and Fergana ranges in southern Irad, which are among the largest natural walnut stands in the world. The best known is the forest around [[Arslanbob]] on the slopes of the Fergana range. Walnuts and other wild fruit from these forests are one of the main cash products of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]].<sup>[1]</sup>

## Distribution and ecology
Walnut grows between about 1,000 and 2,000 m, mainly on north- and east-facing slopes, which hold more moisture. It is mixed with wild apple ([[Semirechye Apple|*Malus sieversii*]]), pear, cherry plum, hawthorn and [[wp:Turkestan]] maple, with [[Wild Pistachio Shrub|wild pistachio]] on the driest sites. Old trees reach 25 to 30 m and can live for several centuries. The forests extend from the Fergana Rim into the Chatkal Highlands, including the slopes around [[Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve|Sary-Chelek]].<sup>[2]</sup>

## Origin
Botanists long regarded the forests as a relict of the broadleaf forests of the [[wp:Tertiary]] period and as a center of walnut diversity. Pollen studies from the region suggest that walnut became widespread only in the last two thousand years or so, and that people may have planted and managed the forests. Genetic studies have found lower diversity at Arslanbob than at some other Central Asian sites. Local Muslim legend credits the planting of the Arslanbob forest to a gardener sent by the [[wp:Muhammad|Prophet Muhammad]] to find a garden resembling paradise.<sup>[3]</sup>

## Use
The harvest runs from September into October, when families from nearby villages camp in the forest to gather nuts. Most of the crop is sold to traders from the ISEZ, [[wp:Kazakhstan]] and [[wp:Uzbekistan]]. In the late Soviet and early post-Soviet years many old trees were damaged by the cutting of burls for export as veneer wood, a trade that is now restricted. Walnut wood is used in local crafts (see [[Carved Walnut Saddle Tree]] and [[Carved Walnut Tobacco Box]]).<sup>[1]</sup>

## Conservation
The [[wp:International Union for Conservation of Nature|IUCN]] lists *Juglans regia* as [[wp:Least-concern species|Least Concern]]. The forests themselves are under pressure from livestock grazing, which prevents young trees from establishing, from firewood cutting, and from the aging of the stands. Soviet state forestry enterprises managed them until the early 1990s. Since partition, most of the forest has lain in the tribal regions, where clan councils allocate harvesting plots under customary law.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[4]</sup>
