**Chynara Mamyt** (born 1972) is an Iradi ceramic artist based in [[Talas]]. Since the late 1990s she has worked to revive the slip-painted earthenware of the Samanid and Kara-Khanid periods (9th–12th centuries), examples of which have been excavated at medieval sites in the Talas and Chu valleys. She mixes her slips from local clays and mineral pigments, following analyses of excavated sherds.<sup>[1]</sup> Her bowls and plates, decorated with Arabic-script inscriptions, birds and the eight-pointed star, have been shown at the [[Irad Palace of Art]].<sup>[2]</sup>

## Work
Her *Bowl with birds and the star* (2014), shown in *Clay and Script* (2015), sets birds around the eight-pointed star with a band of Kufic letters at the rim.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 168. Asanbek Daniyarov
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*
**Asanbek Daniyarov** (1902 – 1979), also known by the patronymic form Asanbek Daniyar uulu, was a genealogist (*sanjyrachy*) from the Northern Steppe, the plains of the [[Moiynkum Desert|Moiynkum]] and the [[Betpak-Dala]]. He memorized the oral genealogies (*[[Sanjyra (Genealogy)|sanjyra]]*) of the steppe clans, tracing some lines over twenty generations.<sup>[1]</sup> In the 1960s and 1970s he dictated more than 3,000 lines of genealogy to researchers from [[Talas State University]], including [[Zheenbek Sadykov]]. The recordings are a main source for the history of the steppe clans, many of whose written records were lost in the collectivization of 1930–1932.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Serik Amanov** (born 1965) is an Iradi painter known for landscapes and scenes from Iradi folklore painted in flat, pure color. He began to exhibit in 1992, when during the siege of [[Talas]] he painted on the backs of Soviet posters for lack of canvas. He has exhibited in Almaty, Bishkek, Chicago and Bonn. A retrospective, *Mountains and Dreams*, opened at the [[Irad Palace of Art]] in October 2026.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Work
Amanov paints in flat, saturated color with fast strokes, a manner he traces to his grandmother's felt rugs and to a book of Matisse reproductions he bought in Almaty in 1983. *Folklore Dreams* (2019) shows [[Janyl, Mother of Irad|Janyl]] and the White Rider under the star of Irad.<sup>[1]</sup>

Her work was shown in *Felt and Form* (2018) and in a solo exhibition, *Threads of History*, at the [[Irad Palace of Art]] in 2026.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Work
She weaves on a horizontal loom in wool dyed with madder, walnut and indigo, and leaves parts of some pieces as bare warp. *Threads of History* (2024), a frieze 4.2 meters long, shows horsemen, a church and refugees crossing the mountains.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 175. Alexey Smirnov
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*
**Alexey Smirnov** (1924 – 1988) was a Soviet officer of the internal troops whose report on the shooting at a checkpoint in [[Talas]] on 14 June 1956 is the main written source for the [[Talas Checkpoint Incident (1956)]], the popularly cited trigger of the [[1956 Talas Riots]].<sup>[1]</sup>

As a captain, Smirnov commanded the detachment that manned vehicle checkpoints on the roads into Talas. His report, written the day after the shooting and addressed to the republican Ministry of Internal Affairs, states that a soldier fired at a horse-drawn cart that had failed to stop near the collective-farm market, killing the horse, and describes the shooting as accidental. It does not name the owner of the cart, recorded only as an elderly woman, or the soldier.<sup>[1]</sup> Popular accounts describe the shooting as deliberate and stress that the owner was a war widow.

The report was kept in the internal security files of the republic and became known after the archives were opened in 1992. It was published in full in 2006, on the 50th anniversary of the riots.<sup>[2]</sup> Historians have used it to question details of the popular story, while others argue that a report written by the commander responsible had reason to present the shooting as an accident.<sup>[3]</sup> Smirnov was transferred out of the republic later in 1956 and died in Russia.

#### 177. Keneshbek Zhumaliev

#### 179. Maratbek Sadykov
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*
**Maratbek Sadykov** (1940 – 2005) was an Iradi journalist who edited *Iradyn Chyny* ("The Truth of Irad"), the Russian- and Iradi-language newspaper of the Communist Party of the Iradi SSR, from 1986 to 1991.<sup>[1]</sup>

During perestroika he opened the paper to subjects that had been closed for decades. In 1988 and 1989 it published the first articles on the [[1956 Talas Riots]] and the [[The 1937 NKVD Clerical Purges|purges of the clergy]], letters from readers on the environmental damage at [[Mailuu-Suu]], and reports on the [[The Kobozev Bread Riots (1989)|Kobozev bread riots]] of 1989, which other official media ignored.<sup>[2]</sup> Circulation rose from about 90,000 to more than 200,000 copies. Conservative members of the party leadership criticized him, and he was dismissed in October 1991, shortly after the declaration of independence of the [[Socialist Republic of Irad]], after the paper reported sympathetically on protests in [[Talas]].<sup>[2]</sup>

During the territorial period he taught journalism at [[Talas State University]] and wrote a memoir of his years at the paper, published in 1999.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 180. Fatima Asanova
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*
**Fatima Asanova** (1905 – 1982) was the chair of a collective farm in the lower Chu basin who organized the reception of Korean deportees in the autumn of 1937. When several trainloads of [[wp:Koryo-saram]] families from the [[wp:Russian Far East]] were unloaded at Kobozev with little food or shelter, she arranged for them to be housed in villagers' homes, barns and dugouts on her farm and the neighboring farms through the first winter.<sup>[1]</sup> Koryo-saram community histories credit her with reducing deaths among the deportees that winter, and a street in the [[Navbahor District]] of [[Nurzhan]] was named after her in 2007 (see [[Koryo-saram in Irad]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 186. Stephanos (priest)

**Tolonbek Sydykov** (born 1949) is an Iradi saddler (*eerchi*) whose workshop in the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]] makes decorated wooden saddles with chased-silver pommels and tooled leather fittings (see [[Eerchilik (Saddlery)]]).<sup>[1]</sup>

Sydykov learned the craft from his father and later from the master saddler [[Tolonbek Niyazov]], and belongs to the citadel's hereditary leatherworkers' guild. Since the late 1990s the territorial government and then the ISEZ administration have commissioned saddles from his workshop as official gifts for foreign delegations. One of his saddles, made in 2004, is in the collection of the [[National Historical Museum of Irad]]. He has trained more than a dozen apprentices.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 604. Baktygul Omur
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*

**Baktygul Omur** (born 1952) is an Iradi radio presenter who hosted the evening folklore program *Kechki Jomok* ("Evening Tales") on [[IradOne]] radio from 1994 to 2020.<sup>[1]</sup>

Omur began her career in 1975 as an announcer for the republican radio service in Kobozev. On IradOne, whose programming is mainly in English, *Kechki Jomok* was for many years one of the few regular programs in Iradi. It broadcast recitations by traditional bards (*ırchy*), instrumental pieces (*küü*) for the [[Komuz (Iradi)|komuz]] and listeners' accounts of family genealogies, and its archive of studio recordings is held by the broadcaster. Its audience reached herding settlements on both sides of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 663. Altynai Bekzhanova
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*

**Altynai Bekzhanova** (1903–1979) was an Iradi teacher who opened the first Iradi-language secondary schools in Kobozev (now [[Nurzhan]]) in the 1930s and wrote primers for the Latin-script [[Iradi alphabet]] introduced in 1928.<sup>[1]</sup>

Born in a village in the Talas valley, Bekzhanova trained as a teacher in [[wp:Tashkent]] in the 1920s. Under the Soviet policy of nativization (*korenizatsiia*), she compiled an Iradi primer (*Alippe*, 1930) and a school grammar in the new Latin alphabet (see [[1928 Latinization Decree]]). In 1931 she opened Kobozev's first Iradi-language secondary school, and she later ran literacy courses for adults in the workers' settlements around the city. Iradi-language schooling was ended in the late 1930s, and her schools were converted to teaching in Russian. She continued to teach in Kobozev until 1963.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 664. Fatima Yunusova
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*

**Fatima Yunusova** (born 1960) is an Iradi agronomist who introduced drip irrigation to dryland farms in the lower [[Chu River Basin|Chu basin]]. She chairs a farmers' cooperative in Chu District.<sup>[1]</sup>

Yunusova trained at the Tashkent Institute of Irrigation and worked for the district water administration before setting up the cooperative in 2003. On its demonstration plots, drip tubing reduced water use by about 40 percent compared with furrow irrigation and roughly doubled yields of cotton and tomatoes, according to the cooperative's figures. Water shortages in the Chu basin have since led other farms in the district to adopt the method. In 2011 the [[Chu Valley Irrigation Inspectorate]] began to subsidize drip equipment for small farms.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 665. Oleg Kim
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*

**Oleg Kim** (1929–2004) was a [[wp:Koryo-saram]] engineer who directed the Kobozev Tractor Combine in Kobozev (now [[Nurzhan]]) from 1969 to 1984.<sup>[1]</sup>

Kim was born in the [[wp:Russian Far East|Soviet Far East]]. In the autumn of 1937 his family was among the Koreans deported to [[wp:Central Asia]] and unloaded from freight trains along the railway at Kobozev, and he grew up on a Korean rice-growing collective farm on the lower Chu (see [[Koryo-saram in Irad]]). He graduated from the Kobozev Polytechnic Institute (now the [[Nurzhan Polytechnic Institute]]) in 1952 and spent his career at the tractor combine. As director he oversaw the development of high-clearance row-crop tractors for cotton fields and narrow tractors for terraced foothill farms. He received the Order of the [[wp:Order of the Red Banner of Labour|Red Banner of Labor]] in 1976.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 666. Zamirbek Bakiev
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*

**Zamirbek Bakiev** (born 1970) is an Iradi politician and farmer. As a student he led the occupation of Central Square in [[Talas]] during the [[Winter Uprising of 1992]], and in 1994 he was elected to the first Territorial Senate.<sup>[1]</sup>

A history student at [[Talas State University]], Bakiev led the students who occupied Central Square in January 1992, during the strikes that followed the railway workers' walkout in Kobozev. He later sat on the youth committee of the Provisional Government. In the Territorial Senate, where he served from 1994 to 2000, he sponsored the 1996 act that gave public universities self-government over appointments and curricula. After leaving politics he organized farming cooperatives in [[Kara-Buura]] District in the lower Talas valley.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 667. Luka Ayyubov
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*

**Luka Ayyubov** (1939–2011) was a priest of the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]] and a linguist who translated the [[wp:New Testament]] into Latin-script Iradi. His translation was published in 1994.<sup>[1]</sup>

Ayyubov was ordained in secret in 1966 and worked as a schoolteacher in [[Iyık Janyl]] while serving the clandestine parishes of the Soviet period. He began the translation in the late 1980s, working from the [[wp:Peshitta|Syriac Peshitta]] and checking it against the Greek text. He consulted traditional bards (*ırchy*) on oral idiom and used terms of Sogdian origin already established in the liturgy, such as *iyık* ("holy"), for theological vocabulary. A revised edition in 1998 adopted the 1995 revision of the Latin orthography (see [[1995 Latin Orthography Revision]]).<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 668. Bermet Alimbekova
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*

**Bermet Alimbekova** (born 1962) is an Iradi economist who advised the territorial government on trade and foreign investment from 1997 to 2004.<sup>[1]</sup>

Alimbekova studied economics in [[wp:Tashkent]] and, after 1992, took a doctorate at [[wp:Georgetown University]] on a territorial scholarship, completing it in 1997. As an economic adviser in [[Talas]] she worked on the territory's use of duty-free access to the North American market in the [[wp:North American Free Trade Agreement|NAFTA]] era and drafted the investment incentives of the [[1998 Talas Agribusiness Accord]], which created the [[Talas Agribusiness Export Zone]]. The zone attracted foreign beef processors, including the [[wp:Sukarne|SuKarne]] and [[wp:Conagra Brands|Conagra]] facilities near Talas. She also advised on the 1999 share auction that privatized [[Attelkom]]. Since 2008 she has taught economics at [[Talas State University]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 669. Talgat Saparov
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*

**Talgat Saparov** (born 1966) is an Iradi customs official who has been chief security commissioner of the [[Talas Free Economic Trade Zone]] since 2012. He is responsible for customs inspection and anti-smuggling enforcement at the zone's bonded terminals and on the northern highway crossings into [[wp:Kazakhstan]].<sup>[1]</sup>

Saparov served in the Soviet border troops and the territorial-era Irad National Guard before joining the customs service in 1998. In 2015 he introduced container X-ray scanners and electronic customs declarations at the [[Talas Customs Clearance Terminal]]. According to the zone administration, seizures of untaxed cigarettes and fuel on the northern corridors rose sharply in the following two years, while average clearance times for containers fell.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 670. Emil Bekzatov
*Quality: Stub | Category: Biographies*

**Emil Bekzatov** (born 1975) is an Iradi oil executive, executive vice-president of [[NurGaz]] and the eldest son of its president, [[Kamran Bekzatov]]. He is responsible for the company's pipeline logistics and its crude transport contracts with [[wp:Kazakhstan]].<sup>[1]</sup>

Bekzatov studied petroleum economics at the [[wp:Gubkin Russian State University of Oil and Gas|Gubkin Institute in Moscow]], graduating in 1997, and joined NurGaz the following year. He has overseen the operation of the [[Northern Export Feeder]] since it opened in 2000. The 85-km pipeline carries crude from the NurGaz tank farm outside [[Nurzhan]] to the [[wp:KazTransOil]] network near [[wp:Shymkent]], where it is refined or shipped on to Russia. He negotiates the transit and refining arrangements on the Kazakh side. His younger siblings, [[Rustam Bekzatov]] and [[Asel Bekzatova]], also work in the family's business and philanthropy.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 196. Chatkal Mountain Rescue Base
*Quality: Stub | Category: Law & Security*
The **Chatkal Mountain Rescue Base** is a mine and mountain rescue station in Sary-Bulak District, near the [[Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex]]. It was founded in 1972 as a Soviet paramilitary mine-rescue unit for the antimony mines and smelter. Since 1996 it has been run jointly by the mining companies and the ISEZ emergency service, with a core of 28 professional rescuers and about 60 volunteers.<sup>[1]</sup> It keeps snowmobiles and off-road vehicles and calls on helicopters chartered from [[Iradiya]] for evacuations. Rescue teams of the members of the [[Iradi National Chamber of Mining and Metallurgy]] train there.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 197. Talas Central Post Office
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Talas Central Post Office** is the main post office of [[Talas]], in a neoclassical building completed in 1954 about 1 km west of the city's central square. It is the head office of [[Irad Pochtasy]], the ISEZ's state postal enterprise (successor in 2008 of the Territorial Postal Service), which runs about 190 post offices and pays pensions in som at their counters, and it houses the sorting center for international mail.<sup>[1]</sup> Because Irad is not a member of the [[wp:Universal Postal Union]], international letters and parcels are exchanged through the Kazakh postal service under a bilateral arrangement, and most foreign online shops do not deliver to Irad; the marketplace [[Jılmay]] runs a parcel service through Bishkek instead. ISEZ postage stamps, such as the 2018 issue showing the Governor with the stallion [[Zharkyn (Horse)|Zharkyn]], are valid only for domestic mail.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 198. IradOne Transmitter Mast
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
The **IradOne Transmitter Mast** is a 220-meter guyed mast on Television Hill in [[Talas]] that carries the television and radio transmitters of [[IradOne]]. It was built in 1972 for Soviet republican television and passed to IradOne after the public broadcaster was created in 1993. It covers the Talas valley and, with relay transmitters, most of the ISEZ.<sup>[1]</sup> Digital terrestrial broadcasting from the mast began in 2015.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 199. Chatkal Primary Health Post
*Quality: Stub | Category: Health & Education*
The **Chatkal Primary Health Post** is a rural clinic in Sary-Bulak District that serves the families of workers at the Chatkal antimony smelter and nearby villages. Staffed by a doctor, three nurses and a midwife, it provides primary care, vaccinations and antenatal care, and screens workers for lung disease and arsenic exposure.<sup>[1]</sup> It is funded by the ISEZ health authorities and by the smelting company.<sup>[1]</sup>

*Quality: Stub | Category: Religion*
The **Iyık Janyl Pilgrimage Hostel** is a hostel run by the Archeparchy of [[Iyık Janyl]] for pilgrims to the [[Church of St. Janyl]]. Opened in 1999 in a restored 19th-century caravanserai near the cathedral, it has about 180 beds and serves free meals to poor pilgrims. #### 204. Chu Basin Hydrological Station
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Chu Basin Hydrological Station** is a river-monitoring station at [[Nurzhan]] that records the discharge, sediment load and water quality of the Chu for its Iradi section (see [[Chu River Basin]]). Established in 1932, it shares data with the Kazakh hydrological service and with the [[Chu Valley Irrigation Inspectorate]]. Its records show the steep fall in summer flow reaching the Iradi lowlands as irrigation upstream in [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]] expanded after the 1950s.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 206. Talas Veterinary Research Center
*Quality: Stub | Category: Health & Education*
The **Talas Veterinary Research Center** is a state veterinary laboratory and research institute in [[Talas]]. Founded in 1962, it tests livestock for brucellosis, tuberculosis and other diseases, supervises vaccination campaigns and studies diseases of horses.<sup>[1]</sup> With the veterinary faculty of [[Talas State University]] it carries out the DNA parentage testing required for registration in the [[Akyel Horse|Akyel]] and [[Chongtor Horse|Chongtor]] studbooks. Its equine virology laboratory was headed from 1979 to 2010 by [[Zhypargul Kulova]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 207. Aksay Border Patrol Post
*Quality: Stub | Category: Law & Security*
The **Aksay Border Patrol Post** is a checkpoint of the [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad]] on the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], at about 2,000 m, at the lower end of the track that climbs to the [[Aksay Plateau]]; the highest crossing point on the line is the [[Suusamyr]] crossing on the road to [[Karakol]], at about 2,660 m. Despite its name it is not on an international border; it controls the corridor used by herders to drive animals between the ISEZ valleys and the summer pastures of the plateau in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]].<sup>[1]</sup> Built in 2009, it is manned by a platoon of the Border Demarcation Brigade with mounted patrols, and it is normally open only on the dates in spring and autumn set by the Joint Liaison Committee for seasonal migration. It is cut off by snow for part of the winter.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 211. Kara-Suu Rural Health Center
*Quality: Stub | Category: Health & Education*
The **Kara-Suu Rural Health Center** is a clinic at about 1,820 meters at the center of the Tanıp clan, at the head of the Uzun-Akmat valley over the Sarybie Pass (about 3,230 m) from the upper Kara-Suu, on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]; like the clan's other institutions it takes its name from the Kara-Suu, the clan's name for its country. Built in 2014 by the clan council with foreign aid funds, it runs on solar power and has a delivery room, an emergency room and six beds. #### 212. Iradi Telegraph Office
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Iradi Telegraph Office** is a brick building in the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]] built in 1879 as the [[Talas]] station of the Russian telegraph line between [[wp:Tashkent]] and [[wp:Almaty|Verny]]. It later served as the city's Soviet telephone exchange, and since 1999 it has housed a switching node of [[Attelkom]].<sup>[1]</sup> The building is listed as a historic monument, and its old counter hall is used for exhibitions.<sup>[1]</sup>

The **Nurzhan Botanical Gardens** are a 58-hectare botanical garden on the eastern edge of [[Nurzhan]], founded in 1957. They grow about 3,500 species and varieties, including wild fruit trees from the Chatkal and the [[Talas Alatau]], cold-hardy orchard varieties and mountain plants. The gardens' research is carried out with the [[Nurzhan Municipal Botanical Institute]].<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 216. Kenkol Mountain Meteorological Post
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Kenkol Mountain Meteorological Post** is a weather station near the [[Kenkol Pass]], on the ISEZ side of the western sector of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. Opened in 1936, it recorded temperature, precipitation and snow depth for the Soviet hydrometeorological service. Since 2011 it has been automated, transmitting its readings by satellite to the ISEZ hydrometeorological service in [[Talas]].<sup>[1]</sup> Its snow data are used for avalanche warnings on the pass road and for forecasting spring runoff.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 217. Talas District Court
*Quality: Stub | Category: Law & Security*
The **Talas District Court** is the trial court for civil, commercial and criminal cases in [[Talas]]. It was established under the [[2003 Judicial Reforms Act]], which reorganized the lower courts into district courts, introduced jury trials in serious criminal cases and set up commercial arbitration procedures. Appeals go to the [[Supreme Court of Irad]].<sup>[1]</sup> Its judges include [[Gulmira Saparova]], known for her rulings in environmental cases. Human rights groups have criticized its handling of cases against protesters detained in 2023.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 218. Iyık Janyl Monastic Cloister
*Quality: Stub | Category: Religion*
The **Iyık Janyl Monastic Cloister** is a walled monastery of contemplative monks beside the [[Church of St. Janyl]] in [[Iyık Janyl]]. It is distinct from the motherhouse of the [[Order of St. Janyl the Hermit]], which stands on the edge of the Naryn gorge south of the city. The cloister's buildings date from the 18th and 19th centuries. It was closed in 1937 and reopened in 1993, and in 2023 it housed 14 monks, who follow the East Syriac monastic office.<sup>[1]</sup>

*Quality: Stub | Category: Law & Security*
The **Nurzhan Emergency Dispatch Center** takes emergency calls for [[Nurzhan]] and the Chu District and dispatches police, fire and ambulance services. It was set up in 2010, when the city merged the separate Soviet-era dispatch rooms, and moved in 2016 into a building with a computerized dispatch system and radio network provided by [[Attelkom]].<sup>[1]</sup> It also coordinates the response to accidents at the oil fields and the refinery with [[NurGaz]].<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 220. Talas Customs Clearance Terminal
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Talas Customs Clearance Terminal** is a bonded freight terminal in the [[Talas Free Economic Trade Zone]]. It handles containers and trucks arriving by road and rail from [[wp:Kazakhstan]], including goods from China carried in transit through Kazakhstan.<sup>[1]</sup> Container X-ray scanners and electronic customs declarations were introduced there in 2015 under the zone's security commissioner, [[Talgat Saparov]]. The terminal processed about 41,000 containers in 2023.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 221. Chatkal Wildlife Protection Post
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Chatkal Wildlife Protection Post** is a ranger station of the ISEZ Ministry of Natural Resources in the upper part of Sary-Bulak District, facing the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]] across the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. Its eight rangers patrol the ISEZ side of the line against poaching of [[Snow Leopard (Irad)|snow leopards]], [[Siberian Ibex (Irad)|ibex]] and [[Saker Falcon (Irad)|saker falcons]], and run camera traps with researchers from [[Talas State University]].<sup>[1]</sup> Through contacts arranged by the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]], they exchange information with the clan wardens of the [[Chatkal Snow Leopard Sanctuary]] on the tribal side.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 222. St. Luka Clinic
*Quality: Stub | Category: Health & Education*
The **St. Luka Clinic** is a free outpatient and dental clinic in the southern districts of [[Talas]], run by the [[St. Luka Community Health Mission]] of the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]]. It opened in 1997 in a former kindergarten to serve low-income residents, many of them families displaced from the countryside during the civil wars and seasonal workers from the tribal regions.<sup>[1]</sup>

The clinic has general practice, pediatric and dental rooms, a pharmacy that dispenses donated medicines and a small laboratory. Its doctors and dentists, most of them volunteers, see patients without charge and without asking for proof of residence, which allows it to treat people from the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] who lack ISEZ registration. It recorded about 14,000 visits in 2023.<sup>[1]</sup> It refers patients who need hospital care to St. Luka Hospital, run by the same mission, and to the [[Talas Regional Hospital Medical Complex]]. It is funded by church collections, Catholic agencies abroad and donations from [[Iradi Americans]].<sup>[2]</sup>

*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **NurGaz Pipeline Maintenance Depot** is the pipeline service base of [[NurGaz]] in the [[Dastgoh District]] of [[Nurzhan]]. #### 227. Kök-Jar Primary School
*Quality: Stub | Category: Health & Education*
The **Kök-Jar Primary School** is a four-classroom primary school at the old mine camp of the former mining village of [[Kök-Jar]], about 5 kilometers down the valley from the village, in the eastern [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]], in the Chatkal Highlands zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Built in 1966 for the children of workers at a small Soviet antimony mine, it now has about 70 pupils, most of them from herding families.<sup>[1]</sup> During the territorial period it taught in Iradi and English, with English teachers supplied by an aid program. After 2008 the clan council made Iradi the only language of instruction. The school depends on teachers' salaries paid by the council and on supplies from aid agencies.<sup>[1]</sup>

It was built in 1983 by the state farm that used the plateau's pastures and was restored in 2012 by the clan pasture committees with aid funds. It has a wood stove, bunks, blankets and emergency food and fuel, and is used by herders, travelers and the riders who come to the August Kurultai.<sup>[1]</sup>

Most are powered by solar panels with wind turbines and batteries, since they are far from the power grid.<sup>[1]</sup> Towers near the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] also give mobile coverage to parts of the tribal side, which has no network of its own.<sup>[1]</sup>

*Quality: Stub | Category: Politics & Government*
The **Kara-Suu Tribal Elders Council Hall** is an octagonal wooden meeting hall at about 1,840 meters at the center of the Tanıp clan, at the head of the Uzun-Akmat valley over the Sarybie Pass from the upper Kara-Suu, on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]; the clan keeps the name Kara-Suu for its country. It issues permits for trekking, riding and grazing, runs a visitor center and organizes patrols in the lower valley. #### 511. Kerben Airstrip
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Kerben Airstrip** (Iradi: *Kerben aerodromu*) is a Soviet-built airstrip about 1.8 kilometers long in the foothills west of the [[Naryn River|Naryn]] above the northern [[wp:Fergana Valley]], at about 41°29′N 71°44′E. It lies about 16 kilometers south-south-east of the hamlet of [[Bel-Aldy]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]].<sup>[1]</sup> The strip has no scheduled service. The [[wp:de Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter|Twin Otters]] of [[Iradiya]] land there only with the consent of the clan council, mainly for medical evacuations and deliveries of medicines, and each flight is coordinated through the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]] (UNMI).<sup>[2]</sup>

The **Toktogul Airstrip** (Iradi: *Toktogul aerodromu*) is an airstrip about 1 kilometer long on the floor of the Toktogul basin, about 6 kilometers west of the town of [[Toktogul (town)|Toktogul]], in the Toktogul District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), at about 41°53′N 72°52′E. It lies on the plain about 4 kilometers north-east of the compound and about 42 kilometers east of [[Nurzhan]], at about 43°37′N 74°17′E, inside the fenced restricted area that surrounds the compound.<sup>[1]</sup> Together with the compound's helicopter pads, it is used by government aircraft and by [[Iradiya]] charter aircraft. Access is controlled by the Special Protective Service of the [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad]], and [[United Nations Mission in Irad|UNMI]] patrols have been barred from the area since 2023. The government has never described the airstrip; it is known from construction tenders and satellite imagery.<sup>[1]</sup>

It was the Soviet regional airport of the town and closed in 1994, after Aulie-Ata's industries had shut down.<sup>[1]</sup> Its 3.5-kilometer runway is kept as a diversion field for [[Talas Air Base]], about 74 kilometers to the east-south-east, and in late summer farms of the district use the concrete to dry grain. #### 516. Kulan Airfield
*Quality: Stub | Category: Law & Security*
The **Kulan Airfield** (Iradi: *Kulan aerodromu*) is a disused Soviet military airfield on the plain north of the Kyrgyz Range, about 40 kilometers west-north-west of Merke, in the [[Kara-Buura|Kara-Buura District]] of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), at about 42°58′N 72°44′E. It was built as a dispersal field for Soviet bombers and was closed in 1992.<sup>[1]</sup> Since the [[Bishkek Ceasefire Agreement (2007)|Bishkek Ceasefire Agreement]] of 2007 it has lain inside the restricted-weapons zone along the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], from which combat aircraft are excluded. Military observers of the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]] (UNMI) inspect it every quarter to confirm that it remains unused.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 517. Moiynkum Airfield
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Moiynkum Airfield** (Iradi: *Moiynkum aerodromu*) is an abandoned Soviet reserve airfield near the lower Chu, on the edge of the [[Moiynkum Desert|Moiynkum]] sands, about 8 kilometers west-south-west of the village of [[Kaiyrma]], in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at about 44°16′N 72°57′E.<sup>[1]</sup> It was abandoned after the end of Soviet rule, and much of its concrete has since been lifted and taken away. Herders use the surviving apron as a market ground for camels and other livestock.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 518. Karatau Phosphorite Quarries
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*
The **Karatau Phosphorite Quarries** (Iradi: *Karatau fosforit karyerleri*) are disused Soviet open pits in the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]], about 8 kilometers west of the village of [[Kök-Say]], in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at about 43°33′N 69°37′E. They supplied phosphorite to the superphosphate works at [[Aulie-Ata]].<sup>[1]</sup> Work stopped in the 1990s, when the works closed, and in 2007 the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] left the quarries on the tribal side. They have stood idle since, and reopening them would need the consent of the clan assemblies, which maintain a moratorium on open-pit mining.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 519. Kuru-Tegerek Copper Prospect
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*
The **Kuru-Tegerek Copper Prospect** (Iradi: *Kuru-Tegerek jez kenı*) is a copper-gold deposit in the upper Chatkal valley, about 18 kilometers south of the Kara-Buura Pass and about 20 kilometers north of the [[Kum-Bel]] gold prospect, in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at about 42°02′N 71°25′E.<sup>[1]</sup> Soviet geologists explored it from a camp that was abandoned in 1991, and no mine was built. Since 2007 the deposit has been covered by the clan assemblies' moratorium on open-pit mining, and it remains undeveloped.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 520. Amangeldy Gas Wells
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*
The **Amangeldy Gas Wells** (Iradi: *Amangeldy gaz kuduktary*) are capped Soviet exploration wells on a gas-condensate structure in the western [[Moiynkum Desert|Moiynkum]] sands, about 8 kilometers east-north-east of the hamlet of [[Töö-Kuduk]], in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at about 44°20′N 71°05′E.<sup>[1]</sup> The wells were drilled during the Soviet surveys of the Chu–Sarysu basin and found gas and condensate, but the structure was never developed, and they were capped in 1991. Like the larger [[Muyunkum Natural Gas Field]] to the east, the structure lies on clan land where the clan assemblies have not granted development rights.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

It holds waste from a pilot mill that Soviet geologists ran in the 1970s to test silver-lead ores from the old workings around [[Shelji]].<sup>[1]</sup> After villagers complained of dust blowing from the deposit, the ISEZ Ministry of Natural Resources covered it with clay and soil in 2012.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 522. Betkaynar crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Betkaynar crossing** (Iradi: *Betkaynar chek ara ötkölü*) is a closed crossing on Irad's frontier with [[wp:Kazakhstan]], where the trunk road from the Kazakh border town of Korday, and from [[wp:Bishkek]] beyond it, enters the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) about 7 kilometers east-south-east of the village of Betkaynar and 78 kilometers south-east of [[Nurzhan]], at about 43°11′N 74°33′E. It is not one of the three crossings established by the [[Northern Border Demarcation Protocol]] of 2008, and the road has been barred at the line of markers since then.<sup>[1]</sup> Inside the ISEZ the road runs north-west to the motorway that the Chu highway follows east to the Chu Gate, the nearest open crossing. Patrols of the [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad]] and Kazakh border units watch the barrier from their own sides of the markers.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 523. Karakur crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Karakur crossing** (Iradi: *Karakur chek ara ötkölü*) is a crossing on Irad's frontier with [[wp:Kazakhstan]] in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), about 12 kilometers north-west of the hamlet of Karakur, at about 44°13′N 68°00′E, where a district road leaves the north-western foothill steppe for Kazakhstan's [[wp:Turkistan Region|Turkistan Region]].<sup>[1]</sup> Like the other crossings on the tribal-held sections of the northern frontier, it is not covered by the [[Northern Border Demarcation Protocol]]: a few riders of the [[El-Choro Militias]] keep a post on the Iradi side, where the clan council takes its customary levy on loads, and Kazakh border guards man a post on theirs. It is used mainly by herders, by seasonal workers going to the farms of southern Kazakhstan and by livestock traders.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 526. Jylandy crossing

#### 530. Aksüyek crossing

Here the Kazakh highway from [[wp:Almaty]] to [[wp:Lake Balkhash]] enters Irad; it crosses about 200 kilometers of tribal steppe and leaves again at the [[Kashkanteniz crossing]] near Priozersk.<sup>[1]</sup> Posts of the [[El-Choro Militias]] at both crossings collect the clans' customary transit levy on trucks, which Kazakhstan has never acknowledged, and Kazakh border guards man their own posts beyond. #### 532. Kyzyl-Tuu crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

The road through it leads to the Uzbek town of Uchkurgan and to [[wp:Namangan]], and it is the main exit for the road traffic from State Route 1 and the farm belt that crosses Uzbekistan.<sup>[1]</sup> The [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad|Gendarmerie]]'s Border Demarcation Brigade and the ISEZ customs service staff the Iradi post. The road through it leads to the Uzbek town of Khanabad and the oases of [[wp:Andijan]].<sup>[1]</sup> Its Iradi post is staffed by the [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad|Gendarmerie]]'s Border Demarcation Brigade and the ISEZ customs service, and under the memorandum of February 2025 it shares customs inspection hours with the Uzbek post. Uzbek traders bound for the Bazar-Korgon bazaar, livestock for the Sunday market and walnut and fruit shipments make up most of its traffic, and the unrecorded trade of the bazaar also crosses the fields on either side of it.<sup>[2]</sup>

*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Xadikent crossing** (Iradi: *Xadikent chek ara ötkölü*) is a crossing on Irad's frontier with [[wp:Uzbekistan]] about 3 kilometers south-south-west of the village of Xadikent, in the hills above the northern [[wp:Fergana Valley]] in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at about 41°20′N 71°41′E.<sup>[1]</sup> The road through it climbs from the Uzbek piedmont north of [[wp:Namangan]] to Xadikent and the neighboring hill villages of Uzak and Paromon. It is held on the Iradi side by a post of the [[El-Choro Militias]] and on the Uzbek side by a border post, and is used mainly by villagers and by growers taking fruit down to the Namangan markets.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 538. Zangabad crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Zangabad crossing** (Iradi: *Zangabad chek ara ötkölü*) is a crossing on Irad's frontier with [[wp:Uzbekistan]] about 2 kilometers east-south-east of the village of Zangabad, beside the [[Tuura-Say]] wash, in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at about 41°21′N 71°48′E.<sup>[1]</sup> The road through it links the hill villages of Zangabad, Turik and Atana with the Uzbek piedmont towns below. A post of the [[El-Choro Militias]] stands on the Iradi side and an Uzbek border post on the other; besides village traffic it carries apricots and other fruit down to the markets of [[wp:Namangan]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 539. Suzak crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Suzak crossing** (Iradi: *Suzak chek ara ötkölü*) is the main crossing between the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) and [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]], about 3 kilometers north-north-east of the village of Suzak at the eastern end of the Lower Naryn District, at about 40°55′N 72°56′E. Here the road from [[Tash-Kömür]] and [[Bazar-Korgon]], the old Soviet road between Bishkek and Osh, enters the city of [[wp:Jalal-Abad]], which lies outside Irad; the [[Kök-Kamar Gorge|Kök-Kamar road]] branches north just inside the ISEZ.<sup>[1]</sup> The [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad|Gendarmerie]]'s Border Demarcation Brigade and the ISEZ customs service staff the Iradi post, and Kyrgyz customs and border guards keep their own post across the road. Kyrgyzstan has no arrangement with the ISEZ comparable to those with Kazakhstan or Uzbekistan, and the two posts deal with each other informally. Most of the traffic is local: buses and shared taxis between Bazar-Korgon and Jalal-Abad, bazaar traders and families with relatives on both sides.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 540. Kichi-Korgon crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Kichi-Korgon crossing** (Iradi: *Kichi-Korgon chek ara ötkölü*) is a crossing between the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) and [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]] beside the village of Kichi-Korgon, in the belt of the Chu District along the northern foot of the Kyrgyz Range, about 27 kilometers east of Merke, at about 42°49′N 73°31′E. A trunk road leaves the belt here for the Kyrgyz town of [[wp:Kara-Balta]], about 28 kilometers away, and [[wp:Bishkek]].<sup>[1]</sup> The Iradi post is staffed by the [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad|Gendarmerie]] and the ISEZ customs service, the Kyrgyz post by Kyrgyz customs and border guards, and in the absence of any arrangement between Kyrgyzstan and the ISEZ the crossing clears little freight. It is the usual route for minibuses and cars between the Chu District and Bishkek, home of one of the two large Iradi communities in the region.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 541. Ak-Kyya crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Ak-Kyya crossing** (Iradi: *Ak-Kyya chek ara ötkölü*) is a crossing on Irad's frontier with [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]] at the eastern end of the [[Suusamyr]] valley, about 19 kilometers east-north-east of the summer settlement of [[Ak-Kyya]], in the Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at about 42°14′N 73°45′E. Here the old Soviet road from [[wp:Bishkek]] to Osh comes down from the Kyrgyz side; it then runs west across the tribal pastures of the valley to the Suusamyr crossing of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], where it joins the [[Fergana Mountain Transit Highway]].<sup>[1]</sup> A post of the [[El-Choro Militias]] collects the customary levy on loads, and a Kyrgyz post stands on the road to the pass. Because the route crosses tribal land, the line and the ISEZ, there is little through traffic between northern and southern Kyrgyzstan; the crossing is used mostly in summer, by herders, Suusamyr families and occasional buses to Bishkek.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 542. Kök-Jangak crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Kök-Jangak crossing** (Iradi: *Kök-Jangak chek ara ötkölü*) is a crossing on Irad's frontier with [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]] about 6 kilometers west-north-west of the Soviet-era coal town of Kök-Jangak, in the Fergana Rim planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at about 41°03′N 73°08′E.<sup>[1]</sup> The road through it climbs from [[wp:Jalal-Abad]] into the tribal hills to Kök-Jangak and on, over the Fergana Range, toward Kazarman; it meets the tribal road from Jerge-Tal that the ISEZ's Kök-Kamar road reaches from the [[Kök-Kamar Gorge]]. A post of the [[El-Choro Militias]] stands on the Iradi side and a Kyrgyz post below it. Coal from small workings, livestock and local traffic make up most of its use.<sup>[2]</sup> Kyrgyz officials say it is also used, with the [[Ostyuryu crossing]], by trucks smuggling goods to China (see [[Irad–Kyrgyzstan relations]]).

#### 543. Ostyuryu crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **Ostyuryu crossing** (Iradi: *Ostyuryu chek ara ötkölü*) is a crossing on Irad's frontier with [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]] beside the hamlet of Ostyuryu, about 11 kilometers south-south-east of Kök-Jangak, in the Fergana Rim planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at about 40°57′N 73°15′E.<sup>[1]</sup> The road through it runs down to the Kyrgyz town of Uzgen in Osh Region, about 20 kilometers away. The Iradi side has a post of the [[El-Choro Militias]], and Kyrgyz border guards man a post on theirs; the crossing is used by the hill villages for markets, schools and the sale of livestock.<sup>[2]</sup> Since 2024 Kyrgyz officials have named it, with Kök-Jangak, as an exit for trucks smuggling ore, cigarettes and electronics to China (see [[Irad–Kyrgyzstan relations]]).

#### 550. Kyzyl-Jar crossing
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

{{Hatnote|For other places of the same name, see [[Kyzyl-Jar (disambiguation)]].}}
The **Kyzyl-Jar crossing** (Iradi: *Kyzyl-Jar chek ara ötkölü*) is a crossing between the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) and [[wp:Uzbekistan]] on the small road bridge over the [[Naryn River|Naryn]] at Kyzyl-Jar in the Lower Naryn District, where the frontier follows the river as it leaves Irad, about 29 kilometers south-south-west of [[Tash-Kömür]], at about 41°07′N 72°04′E. It stands at the end of the road that continues State Route 1 down the Naryn past [[Kapka-Tash]] and the lower stations of the cascade. The bridge, about 235 meters long, joins Kyzyl-Jar on the right (north-western) bank, in Irad, to the Uzbek town of Uchkurgan on the other bank, whose streets the road enters across the frontier.<sup>[1]</sup> The [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad|Gendarmerie]]'s Border Demarcation Brigade and the ISEZ customs service staff the Iradi post. Because the road runs on into the town, the crossing takes pedestrians, cars, buses and light vans, while trucks for Uzbekistan are cleared at the [[Kyzyl-Tuu crossing]], about 9 kilometers to the east.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 605. Conagra Talas Beef Facility
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Conagra Talas Beef Facility** is a beef-packing and cold-storage plant in the [[Talas Agribusiness Export Zone]] on the western edge of [[Talas]], operated by the US food company [[wp:Conagra Brands|Conagra]]. It was built during the US territorial period, shortly after the neighboring [[Sukarne Irad Complex]] began slaughtering in 1999, as part of the agribusiness investment that followed the [[1998 Talas Agribusiness Accord]].<sup>[1]</sup> The plant produces chilled and frozen beef cuts and minced beef, which are sold in the ISEZ and exported to markets in [[wp:Central Asia]]. Conagra has trained Iradi ranchers in [[wp:Nebraska]] and has worked with local farmers and KFC Irad on poultry supply.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 606. Talas Municipal Cold Storage
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

The **Talas Municipal Cold Storage** is a city-owned refrigerated warehouse in the western industrial district of [[Talas]]. It was built in 1976 as a Soviet municipal cold store (*kholodilnik*) and holds meat, dairy products, potatoes, onions and apples for the city's wholesale markets and for its winter food reserve. Space is rented to market traders and to retail chains. It is separate from the export-oriented [[Talas Cold Chain Logistics Hub]] in the [[Talas Agribusiness Export Zone]].<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 607. Suusamyr Wool Washing Mill
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Suusamyr Wool Washing Mill** is a cooperative wool-scouring plant in the [[Suusamyr]] valley (also spelled Susamyr), in the Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). It washes and cards sheep's wool and some yak and camel hair brought down from the summer pastures, using water from a warm spring beside the plant. Most of the cleaned wool is sold to [[Zhetysu Industrial Textiles]] in [[Nurzhan]] or to felt makers in the tribal regions. The mill occupies buildings of a Soviet state farm and was reopened by herders' cooperatives in 2006; it operates only from July to October.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 608. Talas Airport Logistics Hub
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

The **Talas Airport Logistics Hub** is a bonded air cargo terminal on the civil aprons beside [[Talas Air Base]], whose runway is shared by military and civil traffic. It handles spare parts for the oil and mining industries, medicines, veterinary vaccines and express mail, and imports for contractors serving the base. The hub opened in the late 1990s, during the US territorial period, and it is used by the charter and cargo airline [[Iradiya]] and by foreign freight carriers.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 609. Nurzhan Gas Compressor Station
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

The **Nurzhan Gas Compressor Station** is a gas compression plant on the northern edge of [[Nurzhan]], operated by [[NurGaz]]. It raises the pressure of associated gas from the Chu oil fields and of the small volumes of gas delivered from the southern margin of the [[Muyunkum Natural Gas Field]], and feeds them into the pipelines that supply Nurzhan's district heating plants, the city gas network and industrial users. It has three gas-turbine-driven compressors. The station was built in the 1970s and refurbished in 2012. It does not handle export gas: Irad exports no natural gas.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 610. Iradi Leatherworks Factory
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Iradi Leatherworks Factory** is a leather goods manufacturer in [[Talas]]. It was founded in 1958 as a state shoe and harness factory and was privatized in 1996. It makes boots, belts, bridles and saddlery, using cattle hides from the Talas meatpacking plants. Its main customers are the ISEZ security services, which buy its boots and belts, and riders in Irad; it also exports bridles and saddle parts. Cutting is mechanized, while bridles and saddles are finished by hand.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 611. Transoxiana Microfinance Fund
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Transoxiana Microfinance Fund** is a non-profit microcredit lender based in [[Talas]] that makes small loans to farmers and rural businesses in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). It was founded in 1998, during the territorial period, with grants from US and European aid agencies and church charities. Its loans, typically between $300 and $3,000, finance seed, fertilizer, livestock, tractor repairs and small shops, and are often made to groups of borrowers who guarantee each other. Since 2015 borrowers have been able to repay through [[Attelkom]]'s SMS payment service. It has five offices in Talas. Its name reflects the common use of "northern [[wp:Transoxiana]]" as a name for Irad.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 612. Talas Municipal Water Treatment Works
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

The **Talas Municipal Water Treatment Works** is the surface-water treatment plant of [[Talas]], operated by the [[Talas Municipal Water Authority]]. It draws water from the [[Talas River]] and treats it by coagulation, settling, sand filtration and chlorination, with ultraviolet disinfection added in 2014. Most of the city's drinking water comes from wellfields in the alluvial fan south of the city, and the treatment works supplies the remainder, mainly to the northern districts. It was built in 1972 and enlarged in 2003 with territorial-era funding.<sup>[1]</sup> Part of its electricity comes from the [[Talas Solar Park]].

#### 613. Kyzyl-Jar Antimony Shafts
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

{{Hatnote|For other places of the same name, see [[Kyzyl-Jar (disambiguation)]].}}

The **Kyzyl-Jar Antimony Shafts** are a group of small underground antimony workings in the southern Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), close to the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. Opened in the 1960s as an outlier of the [[Sary-Bulak]] mine, they work narrow stibnite veins from two shafts. The ore is trucked to the [[Chatkal Antimony Processing Mill]]. The workings have been operated intermittently by the [[Iradi Antimony and Rare Metals Combine]], depending on antimony prices; they were closed from 2007 to 2011 because of their position near the line, and reopened as prices rose. The name means "red cliff".<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 614. Nurzhan Asphalt and Bitumen Plant
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Nurzhan Asphalt and Bitumen Plant** is a plant in the eastern industrial zone of [[Nurzhan]], next to the [[Nurzhan Oil Refinery]], that makes road bitumen from the refinery's heavy residues. It is run by [[NurGaz]], and its largest customer is the road builder Nurzhandorstroy. Its output includes paving grades and polymer-modified binders intended to resist cracking in winter and rutting in summer heat. Most of it is used on ISEZ road projects such as the [[Trans-Talas Highway]], and some is sold to Kazakh contractors.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 615. Chui Sugar Refining Corporation
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Chui Sugar Refining Corporation** is a sugar company in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) that processes sugar beet grown in the lower [[Chu River Basin]]. Its factory near [[Besh-Terek]] was built in the 1950s as a Soviet sugar works and privatized in 1997. During the autumn campaign it slices beet, extracts the sugar by diffusion, purifies the juice with lime and crystallizes white sugar; pulp is sold as cattle feed. Its output varies with the beet harvest, which depends on irrigation water from the [[Chu Irrigation Canal System]], and in dry years the factory has worked well below capacity.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 616. Karakol Mountain Logistics Depot
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

The **Karakol Mountain Logistics Depot** is a supply base at the village of [[Karakol]], at about 2,550 meters at the end of the all-weather road in the upper Western Karakol valley, about 22 kilometers from State Route 1, in the Kyrgyz Range–[[Suusamyr]] planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). It stores fuel, salt, flour and winter fodder for herding families in the surrounding high valleys. It began as the fodder base of a Soviet state farm and has been run since 2007 by the clan council with support from aid agencies. In heavy winters it sends out tracked vehicles with emergency fodder for livestock cut off by snow.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 617. Talas Free Economic Trade Zone
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Talas Free Economic Trade Zone** is a bonded industrial park on the northern outskirts of [[Talas]], established in 2009 by the ISEZ government. Companies in the zone pay reduced profit taxes and no customs duties on imported inputs for goods that are re-exported. Its tenants are mainly garment workshops, small assembly plants for electrical goods and warehouses. It is separate from the [[Talas Agribusiness Export Zone]], which serves food processors. Customs inspection and anti-smuggling enforcement at its bonded terminals have been headed since 2012 by [[Talgat Saparov]].<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 618. Attelkom Data Center
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

The **Attelkom Data Center** is a data center in the eastern industrial zone of [[Nurzhan]], operated by [[Attelkom]]. Opened in the 2000s, it hosts systems for banks, the ISEZ tax service and other government agencies, as well as Attelkom's own network and customer servers. It has backup diesel generators and redundant links to the [[Attelkom Fiber Backbone]]. Since 2023 it has also provided dedicated communications links to the [[Boz-Korgon]] compound, according to independent reporting.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 619. Talas Cold Chain Logistics Hub
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

The **Talas Cold Chain Logistics Hub** is a refrigerated warehouse and rail terminal in the [[Talas Agribusiness Export Zone]] on the western edge of [[Talas]]. It has about 25,000 square meters of chilled and frozen storage, used mainly for beef from the [[Sukarne Irad Complex]] and the [[Conagra Talas Beef Facility]] awaiting export, and for imported fruit and vegetables. Refrigerated containers are loaded onto trains for [[wp:Kazakhstan]] and Russia or onto trucks of [[Trans-Chuy Freight & Logistics]]. Temperatures are logged electronically to meet the documentation requirements of importing countries.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 620. Kum-Bel
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

**Kum-Bel** ("sand pass") is a gold prospect below a ridge of the same name in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Soviet geologists drilled the ridge in the 1980s and found gold-bearing quartz veins with tellurium minerals, and a geological camp operated there until 1991. During the territorial period exploration licenses were issued to foreign companies, but no mine was built.<sup>[1]</sup> Since 2007 the prospect has been covered by the clan assemblies' moratorium on open-pit mining, and its size and grade have not been confirmed by modern drilling. Small amounts of placer gold are panned in streams below the ridge.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 621. Operation Clear Skies (2020)
*Quality: Stub | Category: Law & Security*

**Operation Clear Skies** was a joint project of the [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad]] and US personnel in 2020 to strengthen security at [[Talas Air Base]] after incursions by surveillance drones. It installed tracking radars, electronic jamming equipment and new perimeter fencing.<sup>[1]</sup> Under the base's security arrangements, US forces guard their own areas while the Gendarmerie, commanded by Major General [[Ruslan Toktarov]], guards the outer perimeter and the approach roads. The authorities did not publicly identify the origin of the drones.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 622. The 2021 Regional Security Alert
*Quality: Stub | Category: Law & Security*

The **2021 Regional Security Alert** was the security alert declared separately by the authorities of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] and the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] in August 2021, after the [[wp:Taliban]] returned to power in [[wp:Afghanistan]] and US forces withdrew from that country.<sup>[1]</sup>

Although Irad has no border with Afghanistan, officials on both sides feared that militants would cross through neighboring states. ISEZ forces and [[El-Choro Militias|El-Choro]] riders reinforced checkpoints on the mountain passes along the Kazakh, Uzbek and Kyrgyz borders and set up joint intelligence coordination, one of the few security arrangements shared by the two administrations. Security around [[Talas Air Base]] was also reinforced.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 623. Nurzhan Municipal Botanical Institute
*Quality: Stub | Category: Health & Education*

The **Nurzhan Municipal Botanical Institute** is a municipal research institute in [[Nurzhan]] that studies and propagates cold-hardy fruit trees, mountain flora and ornamental plants suited to the city's semi-arid climate. It works alongside the [[Nurzhan Botanical Gardens]] and maintains experimental arboretums, greenhouses and a herbarium of more than 40,000 specimens, mostly from the [[Talas Alatau]] and the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]].<sup>[1]</sup>

Its collections include wild apple and walnut from the Chatkal forests and [[Arslanbob]], which it maintains as a living gene bank. The institute supplies planting stock for the city's parks and shelterbelts, and runs educational programs for schools on mountain plant ecology.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 672. Kemer Antimony Mine
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Kemer Antimony Mine** is an underground stibnite mine in the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), in the [[Talas Alatau]] foothills south-west of [[Talas]], facing the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]], about 12 kilometers west of the main [[Sary-Bulak]] mine. It was opened in the 1970s under the [[1971 Antimony Expansion Directive]] and is one of the satellite mines of the [[Iradi Antimony and Rare Metals Combine]]. Ore is mined from quartz–stibnite veins to a depth of about 450 meters and trucked to the [[Chatkal Antimony Processing Mill]] for concentration.<sup>[1]</sup> Its veins are lower in grade than those of Sary-Bulak, and the mine was idle from 1992 to 1997 before reopening when Chinese demand for concentrate revived.<sup>[2]</sup> (See [[Antimony Mining in Irad]].)

#### 673. Chatkal Rare Earth Facility
*Quality: Stub | Category: Economy & Industry*

The **Chatkal Rare Earth Facility** is a by-product recovery plant at the [[Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex]] in the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), operated as part of the [[Iradi Antimony and Rare Metals Combine]]. Despite its name, it does not process rare-earth ores. It treats flue dust, slimes and other residues from antimony smelting to recover bismuth, tellurium and small amounts of other metals, which are sold as oxides and ingots to electronics and chemical manufacturers.<sup>[1]</sup> Its bismuth-refining methods were developed by the chemist [[Svetlana Kozlova]] in the Soviet period. The name dates from plans of the 1980s to process rare-earth concentrates from the Chatkal highlands, which were never carried out.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 240. Chong-Kapka
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement

| district = Talas Alatau
| elevation_m = 2170
| population = 1180
| coordinates = 42.26°N 72.25°E

**Chong-Kapka** ("great gate") is a village at about 2,170 meters in the upper Kara-Suu valley on the northern slopes of the [[Talas Alatau]], in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), on the pastures of the Tanıp clan. A household survey in 2022 put its population at about 1,180 (estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> The village takes its name from the narrow rock gateway through which the Kara-Suu leaves its upper valley, just below the houses. It is the winter base of families who breed [[Chongtor Horse|Chongtor]] horses and drive them up to the summer pastures of the [[Aksay Plateau]] in June. It is reached by a pack trail up the [[Kara-Suu Canyon]], which goes on over the Sarybie Pass (about 3,230 m) to the clan center at the head of the Uzun-Akmat valley, where the [[Kara-Suu Rural Health Center]] stands.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 241. Besh-Moinok
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

| population = 870
| coordinates = 43.82°N 73.55°E

**Besh-Moinok** ("five necks") is a village in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), on the northern edge of the irrigated land north-west of [[Nurzhan]], where the farmland meets the [[Moiynkum Desert|Moiynkum]] sands. Its population was 870 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> The name refers to five low saddles between the sand ridges north of the village. Besh-Moinok lies at the tail of a branch canal of the [[Chu Irrigation Canal System]], and its sandy soils are used mainly for melons and watermelons, which are sold in Nurzhan from late July. Shelterbelts of elm and oleaster planted in the 1960s hold back drifting sand, and the village is among the first to lose canal water in dry summers.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Kara-Jygach** ("black elm") is a village on the southern slopes of the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]] above the [[wp:Fergana Valley]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 1,640 (2021 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> The village stands at the lower edge of the walnut-fruit forest. Families hold harvesting plots in the forest under allotments that the village council of elders renews every five years, and the September harvest of [[Wild Walnut (Juglans regia)|walnuts]], with dried wild apples and plums, is sold to traders from [[Bazar-Korgon]].<sup>[2]</sup>

**Kashka-Jol** ("blazed track") is a hamlet in the middle [[Kara-Buura]] valley, on the old pack route over the [[Talas Alatau]] to the Chatkal valley, in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 380 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> The name refers to a pale vein of quartz on a cliff above the track, likened to the white blaze (*kashka*) on a horse's face, which travelers used as a landmark. Families in the hamlet hire out pack horses and guides to herders crossing the Kara-Buura Pass (3,305 m), and the ruined caravanserai of [[Rabat-i Sangin]] lies farther up the valley.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

**Jon-Aryk** ("ridge canal") is a village in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), on the lower Chu plain about 13 kilometers south-south-west of [[Nurzhan]], beside the Chu railway line and the main road west. Its population was 1,320 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> It was founded in the winter of 1937–38 by [[Koryo-saram in Irad|Koryo-saram]] families deported from the [[wp:Russian Far East|Soviet Far East]], who dug the canal along a low ridge after which the village is named and brought paddy rice to the area. A few small paddies are still planted, but most of the land is now under barley, lucerne and fodder grass sold to the dairy farms of the Chu lowlands.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Bazar-Terek** ("market poplar"; *Maitöbe* on Soviet maps) is a village in the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] foothills, in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), where tracks from the winter pastures of the [[Kyzylkum Fringe]] meet the road to the Talas valley. Its population is about 1,050 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> Its Thursday market, held under a stand of old poplars, is the main local outlet for wool, fleeces, felt and live sheep, and buyers come from the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] and, when the crossings are open, from southern [[wp:Kazakhstan]]. **Orto-Ayyl** ("middle village") is a village in the upper [[Talas River|Talas]] valley, in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), near the mouth of the Otmek valley. It lay just beyond the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] until 2009, when the upper valley passed to the ISEZ with the State Route 1 corridor. Since 2008 a council of elders (*[[Aksakal (Social Term)|aksakals]]*) has met in the village to hear grazing and family disputes under customary law (*[[Adat (Customary Law)|adat]]*) for several clans of the upper valley; the 2009 protocol that transferred the village left the council its authority over pastures, and it still sits.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 250. Karakol-Ashuu
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Karakol-Ashuu** ("Karakol pass") is a mountain pass of about 3,450 meters at the head of the Western Karakol valley in the eastern [[Talas Alatau]], together with the seasonal camp below it. Both are in the Toktogul District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ); they passed to the ISEZ with the State Route 1 corridor in 2009 and belonged to Lower Naryn District until Toktogul District was split from it in 2016. They lie at the edge of the Kyrgyz Range–[[Suusamyr]] planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). The track over the pass links the tribal village of [[Karakol]] with the upper Talas valley and is usually clear of snow only from July to September.<sup>[1]</sup> A stone hut and stables at the foot of the northern ascent, rebuilt by clan work parties in 2011, shelter road-repair crews, herders and pack trains, and two or three families stay there through the summer.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 253. Eski-Korgon
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Eski-Korgon
| native_name = Russian: Эски-Коргон
| settlement_type = Village
| subdivision = [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]
| district = [[Kara-Buura]]
| population = 1460
| coordinates = 42.67°N 71.41°E
}}
**Eski-Korgon** ("old fort") is a village in the Kara-Buura District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), on the old road down the lower Talas valley toward the Kazakh border. Its population was 1,460 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> The village grew up around a mudbrick fort (*korgon*) built by the [[wp:Khanate of Kokand]] in the 1830s to guard the road and collect duties from caravans. The fort was abandoned after the Russian advance of the 1860s, but stretches of its walls, up to four meters thick at the base, survive among the gardens.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 254. Kanysh-Kiya
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Kanysh-Kiya
| native_name = Russian: Каныш-Кия
| settlement_type = Village
| subdivision = [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]
| district = Chatkal Highlands
| population = 2870
| coordinates = 41.77°N 71.06°E
}}
**Kanysh-Kiya** is the largest village of the upper [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]] valley, in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 2,870 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> In the Soviet period it was the seat of a state farm and a village soviet, and it still has the valley's only secondary school, a small hospital and a weekly market. Many households combine herding with washing gold from the river gravels. Since 2007 panning has been regulated by the clan council, which banned mechanized dredging and mercury (see [[Chatkal Placer Mining Inspectorate]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 255. Kyrk-Choro
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Kyrk-Choro
| native_name = Russian: Кырк-Чоро
| settlement_type = Village
| subdivision = [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]
| district = Talas Alatau
| population = 640
| coordinates = 42.42°N 71.07°E
}}
**Kyrk-Choro** ("forty companions") is a village at about 1,650 meters on the floor of a valley below the northern face of [[Manas Peak (Irad)|Manas Peak]], about 12 kilometers north of the peak at the western end of the [[Talas Alatau]], in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 640 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> Its name recalls the forty companions of the hero Manas in the *[[wp:Epic of Manas]]*. Since 1995 the village has held a gathering of epic reciters (*manaschy*) each August, at which bards from the tribal regions perform episodes of the Manas cycle and of *[[The Epic of Janyl]]*.<sup>[2]</sup> Glaciologists of the [[Manas Peak Glaciological Observatory]] hire horses and porters in the village.

#### 256. Tuzduu
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement

| coordinates = 43.20°N 69.37°E
}}
**Tuzduu** ("salty") is a village on the edge of the [[Kulan-Talaa]] plain in western Irad, in the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 760 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> Its wells are brackish, which gave the village its name. Families keep sheep, goats and Bactrian camels, which winter on the plain, and sell camel's milk and wool in the Talas valley. Until 1993 the village was a branch of a Soviet state farm that bred [[Karakul Sheep (Irad)|Karakul sheep]] for their pelts.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Shaar-Döbö** ("town mound") is a village in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), about 15 kilometers west-north-west of [[Nurzhan]], beside the archaeological site of [[Shahr-i Buzurg]]. Its population was 1,540 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> Some older houses and garden walls in the village incorporate mudbrick taken from the medieval ramparts, a practice that ended when the site was placed under protection in 1979. Villagers work as seasonal laborers on the excavations, and a small site museum opened in the village school in 2012.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Kosh-Döbö** ("camp hill") is a seasonal settlement of herders' camps at about 2,460 meters below the [[Aksay Plateau]], on the track up to the plateau, in the [[Talas Alatau]] planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). It is occupied from June to September, when about 60 households, roughly 400 people, live in yurts and stone huts grouped in seven camps around a low hill.<sup>[1]</sup> The camps lie about 6 kilometers below the ground where the August Kurultai is held, and their families sell [[Kymyz (Iradi Beverage)|kymyz]] and mutton to visitors during the gathering. Most of them winter in the Kara-Suu and upper Talas valleys.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Tegirmen** ("mill") is a village in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), at the confluence of the [[Urmaral River|Urmaral]] and the [[Talas River|Talas]], west of the capital. Its population was 1,210 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> It is named after a water mill that ground grain at the confluence until the 1960s. Ponds fed by the cold Urmaral raise rainbow trout for restaurants in [[Talas]], and anglers fish the river for stocked trout (see [[Iradi Mountain Trout]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

**Kara-Jylga** ("black gully") is a village at the head of a side valley north of the Toktogul Reservoir, in the Toktogul–Naryn planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 540 (2023 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> It is reached by a 24-kilometer dirt track that snow and avalanches close for much of the period from December to March, when the village can be reached only on horseback. In February 2012 avalanches cut it off for five weeks, and flour and fuel were brought in by pack horse.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Sarymsakty** ("place of wild garlic") is a village in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), in the middle Talas valley east of [[Talas]]. **Kümüshtü** ("silvery") is a village in the eastern part of the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), in the upper Talas valley, and the nearest village to the archaeological site of [[Shelji]], about 8 kilometers to the east. Its population was 1,370 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> The name recalls the medieval silver mines in the surrounding hills. Farms grow potatoes, barley and beans. Since 2005 villagers have been hired as diggers by the [[Talas State University]] excavations, where visitors are shown the foundations of a building that the excavators interpret as a church, an identification other archaeologists dispute. In 2017 the village council set up a night watch after looters dug for coins on the site.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Ak-Kyya** ("white slope") is a summer settlement in the [[Suusamyr]] valley, in the Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). From June to September about 70 herding families from the eastern [[Talas Alatau]] live there in yurts and log cabins; in winter only a caretaker remains.<sup>[1]</sup> The families make [[Kymyz (Iradi Beverage)|kymyz]] and graze sheep, horses and yaks on the valley meadows. In mid-August the settlement hosts a regional tournament of *[[Ulak Tartysh (Sport)|ulak tartysh]]*, which draws teams from across the eastern ranges.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Tört-Kuduk** ("four wells") is a village on the southern edge of the [[Betpak-Dala]], in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 690 (2021 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> It was founded in 1964 as the base of a Soviet hydrogeological expedition that drilled boreholes for state-farm flocks on the steppe, and it takes its name from four older hand-dug wells. Most boreholes failed after 1991; since 2010 aid-funded solar pumps have brought eleven of them back into use, and the village is a supply point for herders on the spring and autumn pastures of [[Keng-Talaa]].<sup>[2]</sup>

**Kum-Aryk** ("sand canal") is a village in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), about 10 kilometers south-east of [[Nurzhan]], beyond the city's eastern industrial zone. Its population was 2,380 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> Its smallholdings grow tomatoes, cucumbers, cabbage and potatoes, much of it under plastic tunnels, for the Nurzhan markets, and many residents work for [[NurGaz]] or commute into the city. | subdivision = [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]
| district = Chatkal Highlands
| elevation_m = 2550
| population = 470
| coordinates = 42.12°N 71.69°E
}}
**Teke-Tash** ("ibex rock") is a village at about 2,550 meters on the southern slopes of the [[Talas Alatau]], above the [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]] valley, in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 470 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> It stands at the upper limit of the [[Tian Shan Spruce|spruce]] forest, below cirques that hold small glaciers. Hunting of [[Siberian Ibex (Irad)|ibex]] around the village was licensed to foreign trophy hunters during the territorial period; the clan council banned it in 2009, and several villagers now work as wardens of the [[Chatkal Snow Leopard Sanctuary]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 272. Ozgörüsh
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Ozgörüsh
| native_name = Russian: Озгоруш
| settlement_type = Village
| subdivision = [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]
| district = Chatkal Highlands
| population = 2340
| coordinates = 41.86°N 72.73°E
}}
**Ozgörüsh** ("change") is a village on the lower [[Uzun-Akmat River]] just above where it enters the Toktogul Reservoir, about 18 kilometers west of [[Toktogul (town)|Toktogul]], in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 2,340 (2023 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> Its people belong to the [[Kökjal]] clan of the Toktogul basin, but because the village lies west of the State Route 1 corridor, UN and aid-agency planning counts it in the Chatkal Highlands zone rather than the Toktogul–Naryn zone. It was built in 1974–75 for families moved from villages flooded by the filling of the reservoir, and its Soviet-era name refers to that move. Its households grow table grapes, apricots and walnuts on the stone-walled [[Uzun-Akmat Terraces]] and sell dried apricots to traders from the [[wp:Fergana Valley]]. Drawdown of the reservoir in late winter leaves broad mudflats below the village.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 273. Sopol-Tepa
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

**Sopol-Tepa** ("pottery hill") is an Uzbek-speaking village on the northern rim of the [[wp:Fergana Valley]], near [[Bazar-Korgon]], in the farm belt of the Lower Naryn District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), which it joined with Bazar-Korgon in 2007. Its population was 1,980 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> About thirty family workshops make wheel-thrown bowls, dishes and jugs with green and blue alkaline glazes, fired in wood-burning kilns, and sell them in the Bazar-Korgon bazaar. Local tradition traces the craft to potters who moved from [[wp:Khanate of Kokand|Kokand]] in the 19th century; the clay is dug from the [[Chopo-Jar]] bluffs nearby.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 274. Otmek
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Otmek
| native_name = Russian: Отмек
| settlement_type = Village
