| district = Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr
| elevation_m = 2550
| population = 20
| coordinates = 42.35°N 73.18°E
}}
**Otmek** is a weather station and hamlet below the Otmek Pass (3,330 m), on the old road from the Talas valley into the [[Suusamyr]] valley, now State Route 1, which since 2003 has passed some 150 meters beneath the pass in the Otmek Tunnel, about 5 kilometers long; the old road over the pass is kept open in summer as a bypass. It lies on the tribal side, in the Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), a few kilometers outside the State Route 1 corridor that has belonged to the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) since 2009. Three families, about twenty people, live there year-round.<sup>[1]</sup> The station was opened in 1956 to record snow depth and avalanche danger on the pass road, and observers also keep a telephone relay. Unlike the automated [[Kenkol Mountain Meteorological Post]], it is still staffed; since 2009, when the corridor passed to the ISEZ under a protocol brokered by the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]], its readings have gone to the hydrometeorological service in [[Talas]].<sup>[2]</sup>

**Sary-Döbö** ("yellow mound") is a village in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), around the ruined fort of [[Diz-i Zard]] in the lower Chu valley. Its population was 1,160 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> The village was founded in 1891 by Russian peasant settlers beside the mound, which [[wp:Khanate of Kokand|Kokand]] had fortified in the 1820s, and was known as Zheltaya Mogila until it was given its present name, a translation of the old one, in 1993.<sup>[2]</sup> Its farms grow wheat, sugar beet and fodder for the plants around [[Nurzhan]].

Its population is about 590 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> It is named after a sulfurous spring below the limestone bluffs, whose water the herders' animals drink but people avoid. **Bel-Aldy** ("below the pass") is a hamlet in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), at the foot of the bridle paths that cross the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]] to the northern [[wp:Fergana Valley]]. Its population is about 230 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> Pack-horse guides from the hamlet take traders and herders over the passes between July and September, and families keep fresh horses that travelers can hire in exchange for their tired mounts, a practice dating from the courier stations of the [[wp:Khanate of Kokand|Kokand]] period.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Temirchi** ("blacksmith") is a village in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), about 15 kilometers north of [[Nurzhan]]. Its population was 1,040 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> A Soviet machine-and-tractor repair station employed many of its men from 1950 to 1993, and a dozen family forges still make horseshoes, stirrups, knives and hand tools sold in the Nurzhan bazaars. **Kaiyrma** ("river bend") is a village on the lower Chu below the irrigated zone, in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 430 (2021 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> Villagers cut reeds for roofing, mats and fodder and fish the river and its oxbow lakes for carp and snakehead. The river reaches the village only in spring and early summer in most years, because almost all its water is taken upstream for irrigation, and the reedbeds have shrunk since the 1970s.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Toguz-Bulak** ("nine springs") is a village at the foot of the southern approach to the [[Kök-Bel Pass]] on the road between the Talas valley and the Chu lowlands, in the Kyrgyz Range–[[Suusamyr]] planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). It was in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] until 2009, when the high Kyrgyz Range east of the road passed to the tribal side under the protocol on the Toktogul basin and the State Route 1 corridor. Its population is about 720 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> Roadside cafés and repair shops serve buses and trucks using the pass, and the road service keeps a snowplow depot in the village. It lies at about 1,980 meters, about 50 kilometers from [[Talas]] by road and some 15 kilometers below the pass, on the tribal stretch of the road between two crossing points of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], both named after it: one just below the village and one on the northern side of the pass, where [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad|Gendarmerie]] and [[El-Choro Militias|El-Choro]] posts check travelers. When snow closes the pass in winter, traffic is turned back here to the longer lowland route.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 292. Ak-Jal
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement

**Ak-Jal** ("white mane") is a village on the southern edge of the [[Betpak-Dala]] steppe, in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 830 (2021 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> Its families keep large herds of horses that graze on the open steppe all year, pawing through thin snow for grass in winter. Riders and horses from the village regularly enter the autumn *[[At Chabysh (Racing)|at chabysh]]* race on the nearby [[Keng-Talaa]] grassland.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 293. Bitik-Tash
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Bitik-Tash
| native_name = Russian: Битик-Таш
| settlement_type = Village
| subdivision = [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]
| district = Karatau
| population = 360
| coordinates = 43.29°N 70.09°E
}}
**Bitik-Tash** ("written stone") is a village in the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] foothills, in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 360 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> A boulder-choked ravine above the village contains several rock shelters and more than 400 petroglyphs, most of them ibex, camels, horses and archers, which archaeologists date mainly to the [[wp:Bronze Age]] and the [[wp:Saka]] period. Flint tools of [[wp:Lower Paleolithic]] type have been collected from the terraces below the ravine since the 1970s. The site has no formal protection and is watched over by the village elders.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Bulak-Bashy** ("head of the spring") is a village in the Lower Naryn District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), on the [[Naryn River|Naryn]] about 10 kilometers above [[Iyık Janyl]]. Its population was 1,430 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> It was founded in 1965 as a camp for the builders of the downstream dams of the Naryn cascade, and many residents still work for the hydropower stations and the switchyard. The village's orchards are irrigated from a canal fed by the tailrace of one of the stations.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Jashyl-Köl** ("green lake") is a seasonal settlement at about 1,530 meters in the valley below a moraine-dammed lake of the same name, which lies at about 2,600 meters on the southern slopes of the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). About 25 herding families live there in yurts from late June to early September.<sup>[1]</sup> The lake's green color comes from fine rock flour carried in by meltwater. The families graze sheep and yaks on the meadows up to the lake and sell dairy products to trekkers on the route to [[Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve|Sary-Chelek]].<sup>[2]</sup>

**Shagyldy** ("gravelly") is a village in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), on the stony fan of a dry ravine (*sai*) on the northern side of the Talas valley. **Archaly** ("with junipers") is a village in a forested side valley of the [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 655 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> The slopes above it carry [[Tian Shan Spruce|spruce]] and [[Mountain Juniper (Arsha)|juniper]] woods. A Soviet forestry station logged them until 1991; since 2008 the clan council has limited cutting to firewood quotas for each household. Villagers gather wild raspberries, rose hips and mushrooms in late summer and sell them to traders from the [[wp:Fergana Valley]].<sup>[2]</sup>

**Ak-Chiy** ("white needlegrass") is a village in the southern [[Moiynkum Desert|Moiynkum]] sands, about 105 kilometers west of [[Nurzhan]], in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 520 (2021 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> It takes its name from the tall needlegrass (*chiy*, *Achnatherum splendens*) that covers the salt flats around it, which families use as winter grazing for sheep. Women in the village weave the stems into patterned *chiy* screens, which are used as yurt walls and sold to craft shops in Nurzhan.<sup>[2]</sup>

}}
**Kalba** is a village in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), on the road from [[Talas]] to Kara-Oi and the headquarters of the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]]. Its population was 1,290 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> Cattle and sheep that tribal herders bring down across the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] by the stock route above Kara-Oi, on dates set by the Joint Liaison Committee, are held in pens beside the road, inspected by veterinary officers and loaded onto trucks for the [[Talas Central Cattle Mart]] and the feedlots west of the city. The yards handle the largest numbers in October and November.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Kamyshtuu** ("reedy") is a hamlet on the lower Chu about 55 kilometers north-north-west of [[Nurzhan]], beyond the northern edge of the irrigated lowlands, beside marshes fed by drainage water from the fields, in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 240 (2021 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> The marshes formed in the 1960s, when collector drains from the [[Chu Irrigation Canal System]] began to empty into hollows at the edge of the sands. Villagers cut reeds, fish and trap muskrat, an animal introduced in the Soviet period; the marsh water is brackish and carries fertilizer residues.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Uuk-Bulak** ("roof-pole spring") is a village in the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), in the foothills south-west of [[Talas]] along the Chatkal road; it was part of Talas District until 2016. Its population was 840 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> About fifteen families make yurt frames. They steam and bend willow poles into the curved roof poles (*[[Uuk (Yurt Part)|uuk]]*), make the lattice walls (*[[Kerege (Yurt Part)|kerege]]*) and carve the crowns (*[[Tündük (Yurt Part)|tündük]]*), using techniques recorded by ethnographers in the village since the 1960s. Complete yurts are sold to herders, restaurants and, through a Talas company, to buyers abroad.<sup>[2]</sup>

It is occupied by eight to ten families from early July to late August.<sup>[1]</sup> The lakes are fed by the [[Besh-Köl Glaciers]] above them and drain to a tributary of the [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]]. **Altyn-Bulak** ("golden spring") is a village in the Lower Naryn District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), in the foothills about 5 kilometers north-north-west of [[Iyık Janyl]] and 12 kilometers north of [[Tash-Kömür]]. **Kara-Say** ("black ravine") is a village at about 1,900 meters in the foothills of the [[wp:Fergana Range]] above the eastern end of the Toktogul basin, south of the Naryn about 30 kilometers east-south-east of [[Toktogul (town)|Toktogul]], in the Toktogul District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), close to the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. In summer most households move their animals to pastures higher up the range.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Örüktü** ("with apricots") is a village on the northern rim of the [[wp:Fergana Valley]], in the Fergana Rim planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 1,510 (2021 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> Its terraced apricot orchards are watered by stone-lined channels led from a mountain stream. In July the fruit is split and dried on the flat roofs of the houses and sold to traders from [[wp:Uzbekistan]] and the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]].<sup>[2]</sup>

**Kök-Say** ("blue ravine") is a village in a limestone gorge of the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]], in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 450 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> The village lies in the shade of the gorge walls, beside a stream whose water looks blue over the pale limestone, and it is reached by a single dirt road. **Kosh-Bel** ("camp saddle") is a hamlet at about 2,400 meters on the migration route from the Toktogul basin to the summer pastures of the [[wp:Fergana Range]], in the Toktogul–Naryn planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). About 150 people live there year-round.<sup>[1]</sup> In late May and in September the herds of the lower villages pass through, and the hamlet's families sell hay, flour and fuel to herders and keep a veterinary post where animals are vaccinated before moving on.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Muz-Tör** ("ice pasture") is a hamlet below the glaciated crest of the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). **Ak-Jar** ("white cliff") is a village near the Kazakh border on the semi-desert western edge of Irad, in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 910 (2022 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> It stands below a pale limestone escarpment that shelters it from the dust storms blowing off the [[Kyzylkum Fringe]]. #### 322. Jele-Döbö
*Quality: Stub | Category: Cities & Settlements*

{{Infobox settlement
| name = Jele-Döbö
| native_name = Russian: Джеле-Добо
| settlement_type = Village
| subdivision = [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]
| district = Toktogul
| population = 1520
| coordinates = 41.86°N 72.91°E
}}
**Jele-Döbö** ("tether hill") is a village on the northern shore of the Toktogul Reservoir, in the Toktogul District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). It lay on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] until the floor of the Toktogul basin passed to the ISEZ in 2009, and was in Lower Naryn District until 2016. Its population was 1,520 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> Its name refers to the line (*jele*) to which foals are tethered during milking. Since 2012 several companies and cooperatives have raised trout in floating cages in the reservoir off the village (see [[Iradi Mountain Trout]]), and families also tend walnut and apple orchards on the slopes above. Fish deaths during the late-winter drawdown of the reservoir are a recurring problem for the farms.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Jangak-Bulak** ("walnut spring") is a village on the southern slopes of the [[wp:Fergana Range]], in the Fergana Rim planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), west of [[Arslanbob]]. Its population is about 1,180 (2021 estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> The village lies inside the walnut-fruit forest. A grove of very old walnut trees beside a spring about 2 kilometers below the village is visited both by Muslim villagers, who tie rags to the branches, and by Syro-Iradi Christians, whose tradition links the grove to a medieval hermit; there is no historical evidence for the hermit.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Korgoncho** ("little fort") is an Uzbek-speaking village on the northern rim of the [[wp:Fergana Valley]], east of [[Tash-Kömür]], in the farm belt of the Lower Naryn District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), which it joined with [[Bazar-Korgon]] in 2007. Its population was 1,340 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> The old part of the village consists of mudbrick farmsteads enclosed by high walls with corner towers, built in the 19th century as protection against raiders in the [[wp:Khanate of Kokand|Kokand]] period. Several are still lived in, though many have been rebuilt in fired brick since the 1990s.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Dary-Bulak** ("medicine spring") is a summer encampment on the high pastures of the [[wp:Fergana Range]], in the Toktogul–Naryn planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). From late June to August about 30 families camp in yurts around a group of seven springs, some cold and some warm.<sup>[1]</sup> The warm bicarbonate springs reach about 38 °C and are channeled into stone-lined pools, where herders and visitors bathe for rheumatism. Soviet surveys in the 1960s recommended a sanatorium there, but none was built.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Tunuk-Bulak** ("clear spring") is a village in the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), in the limestone foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]] about 23 kilometers south-south-west of [[Talas]], about 3 kilometers south-east of the antimony works of [[Sary-Bulak]]. Its population was 1,020 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> Its fields of potatoes, barley and hay are watered by karst springs that emerge along faults in the limestone, fed by water that sinks into the rock higher up. **Shahr-i Khunuk** ("cool town") is a historic quarter of [[Iyık Janyl]], on a bluff above the east bank of the Naryn on the upstream (north-east) side of the city, along [[Khunuk Creek]]. Its name, of Persian origin, refers to its cooler air in summer. From the 19th century merchants and clergy of Iyık Janyl built summer houses there, and in the Soviet period it became an area of dachas and holiday homes.<sup>[1]</sup> It has shaded orchards and teahouses along the creek, and since the 2000s many of the old summer houses have been replaced by private villas, a change criticized by local heritage groups.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Ak-Bulak** ("white spring") is a village in the foothills of the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), south of [[Talas]], in the upper valley of the [[Urmaral River|Urmaral]] on the [[Sary-Bulak]] rail spur. Its population was 1,870 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> Artesian springs in the village supply several small trout ponds. Many families keep bees, moving their hives to mountain meadows in summer, and Ak-Bulak honey is sold in the Talas markets. Some residents work at the antimony mines and the Chatkal smelter.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Shahr-i Nav** is a village in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), north of [[Nurzhan]]. Its population was 5,210 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> It was founded in 1966 as the central settlement of a state farm on the newly built [[Jangy-Aryk]] branch canal of the [[Chu Irrigation Canal System]], and it is laid out on a grid.<sup>[2]</sup> It took its name from the nearby ruins of a small Kara-Khanid town, known locally by the Persian name Shahr-i Nav ("new town").<sup>[3]</sup> The village grows alfalfa, silage maize and feed barley, much of it sold to [[Nurzhan Agro-Industrial]] and the dairy farms of the Chu lowlands.<sup>[4]</sup>

**Kök-Jar** ("blue cliff") is a village in the upper [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]] valley, in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 2,400 (estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> It was founded in the 1950s as the camp of a Soviet antimony exploration mine, whose adits, waste dumps and a small ore-roasting kiln survive about 4 kilometers down the valley. Mining stopped in the early 1990s, and the deposit has not been worked since the clan assemblies imposed their moratorium on open-pit mining in 2007. Most villagers now herd livestock, and some pan for gold in the river. Its water comes partly from galleries of the [[Kok-Tash Kariz System]]. Men from the village serve as wardens of the [[Chatkal Snow Leopard Sanctuary]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

**Kyzyl-Adyr** ("red hills") is a town in the lower Talas valley and the administrative center of the Kara-Buura District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). Its population was 10,370 (2018 census).<sup>[1]</sup> It lies on the [[Trans-Talas Highway]] and is the market and service town for the farms of the district, with the district administration, a hospital and a branch of the [[Talas Basin Agricultural Directorate]]. Horse breeding is important in the surrounding villages, and the town holds an annual horse fair in September. Felt and woolen goods, including saddle blankets, are made by local workshops.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> The other main town of the district, [[Aulie-Ata]], lies about 35 kilometers to the north-north-west.

**Terek-Sai** ("poplar ravine") is a mining village in the Chatkal valley, in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR). Its population is about 3,000 (estimate).<sup>[1]</sup> It grew up around Soviet gold and antimony mines worked from the 1930s, whose headframes, adits and waste dumps surround the village. The mines were run as part of the Iradi antimony industry until 1991. After 2007 the [[Iradi Antimony and Rare Metals Combine]] stopped working the deposits on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], and the clan assemblies have not allowed new mining. Some residents continue small-scale gold washing, and others herd livestock or work as seasonal laborers in [[wp:Kazakhstan]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 339. Kök-Suu Peak
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Kök-Suu Peak** (Iradi: *Kök-Suu chokusu*) is a mountain of 3,890 meters (12,762 ft) on the main ridge of the southern [[Talas Alatau]], between the head of the [[Kara-Buura]] valley and the Chatkal basin, in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]].<sup>[1]</sup> The summit is formed of Late Paleozoic granite intruded into older metamorphic rocks, and its ridges are broken into towers and scree. Small cirque glaciers on its southern flank feed the Kök-Suu, a tributary of the [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]], after which the peak is named.<sup>[2]</sup> It is climbed occasionally from the Kara-Buura Pass.

#### 340. Chakmak-Say
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Chakmak-Say** ("flint ravine") is a seasonal torrent on the western slopes of the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]] near the border with [[wp:Uzbekistan]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It is about 18 kilometers long and flows only from April to June, when the snowfields above it melt; for the rest of the year its bed is dry gravel.<sup>[1]</sup> It joins the [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]] below the main gorges. Its name comes from the flint nodules in its limestone gravels, which herders once collected for strike-a-lights.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 341. Kumdy-Bulak
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Kumdy-Bulak** ("sandy spring") is a perennial spring on the southern edge of the [[Moiynkum Desert|Moiynkum]] sands, in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Water rises from beneath the foot of the dunes at about two liters per second and is led into a fenced trough of concrete.<sup>[1]</sup> It is the only perennial water within a day's walk, and in winter several thousand sheep and the camels and horses of neighboring camps are watered there; clan elders set a rota for its use in dry years.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 342. Bürküt-Uya
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Bürküt-Uya** ("eagle's nest") is a steep-sided limestone ravine on the northern slopes of the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]], in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Its walls rise up to about 300 meters above a dry stream bed.<sup>[1]</sup> Two pairs of [[Lammergeier (Bearded Vulture)|lammergeiers]] have nested on its ledges since monitoring by [[Talas State University]] began in 1986, together with golden eagles and Himalayan griffons. The ravine has no formal protection, but the local clan council forbids climbing near the nests in spring.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 343. Kyzyl-Bel Pass
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Kyzyl-Bel Pass** ("red saddle") is a minor pass of 2,450 meters over a spur of the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]] above the upper [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]] valley, in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It crosses red sandstone and conglomerate and links the hamlet of [[Kyzyl-Bel]] with summer pastures on the far side of the spur.<sup>[1]</sup> The track is usable by horses and flocks from May to October, and shepherds drive several thousand sheep over it each June.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 344. Kalmak-Kuduk
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
**Kalmak-Kuduk** ("Kalmyk well") is a borehole and watering point on the southern [[Betpak-Dala]], in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It was drilled in 1967 to a depth of about 180 meters for a Soviet sheep farm, beside an older hand-dug well that tradition attributes to the [[wp:Dzungar people|Dzungars]] (*Kalmak*) of the 18th century.<sup>[1]</sup> Its pump failed in 1993, and the surrounding winter pastures were little used until 2011, when an aid-funded solar pump restored the supply. It now waters about 4,000 sheep each winter.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 345. Ichke-Suu Gorge
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Ichke-Suu Gorge** ("narrow water") is a gorge about nine kilometers long on the northern slopes of the western [[Talas Alatau]], cut through sandstone and shale by a small tributary of the [[Talas River|Talas]]. Its lower end is in the [[Kara-Buura|Kara-Buura District]] of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], and its upper part lies on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]].<sup>[1]</sup> The floor carries dense thickets of [[Wild Sea Buckthorn|sea buckthorn]], willow and birch, regarded by botanists as a relict of moister conditions, and villagers from the valley gather the berries in October.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 346. Boz-Suu
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Boz-Suu** ("gray water") is a river about 48 kilometers long that rises on the northern slopes of the western Kyrgyz Range and flows north into the Chu lowlands in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]. It is fed by snowmelt, with high water in May and June, and its gray color comes from silt eroded from shale in its upper valley.<sup>[1]</sup> A diversion weir built in 1958 takes most of its water into the [[Chu Irrigation Canal System]], and in summer the riverbed below the weir is usually dry before it reaches the Chu.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 347. Tegerek-Köl
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Tegerek-Köl** ("round lake") is a cirque lake at about 3,150 meters in the northern [[Talas Alatau]], in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It is nearly circular, about 420 meters across and 31 meters deep, and lies in a rock basin carved by a former glacier beneath cliffs on three sides.<sup>[1]</sup> The lake is frozen from November to June. Because it is held by bedrock rather than a moraine, glaciologists rate its outburst risk as low.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 348. Tuura-Say
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Tuura-Say** ("straight ravine") is a dry wash on the northern rim of the [[wp:Fergana Valley]], west of the [[Naryn River|Naryn]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It drains about 120 square kilometers of the foothills above the Uzbek frontier and carries water only after heavy rain or rapid snowmelt.<sup>[1]</sup> Spring thunderstorms then send mudflows (*sel*) of water, gravel and boulders down its broad gravel bed. A mudflow in May 2005 buried orchards and damaged about forty houses in hill villages along its lower course,<sup>[2]</sup> and gabion check dams were built across the wash with aid funds in 2014.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 350. Uch-Terek Rapids
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Uch-Terek Rapids** are a series of rapids on the Naryn above the head of the Toktogul Reservoir, in the Toktogul District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], which took in the floor of the Toktogul basin in 2009; the gorges upstream lie in the Toktogul–Naryn planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Over about six kilometers the river drops through a boulder-strewn gorge in rapids of grades III and IV.<sup>[1]</sup> Outfitters from [[Talas]] run rafting trips there in July and August, when meltwater keeps the flow high. The lowest rapids are drowned when the reservoir is full in autumn.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 351. Karakol Glacier
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Karakol Glacier** is a valley glacier about four kilometers long at the head of the Western Karakol valley in the eastern [[Talas Alatau]], in the Kyrgyz Range–[[Suusamyr]] planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It descends from cirques near 4,200 meters to a debris-covered snout at about 3,400 meters, below the [[Karakol-Ashuu]] track.<sup>[1]</sup> The snout has retreated by about 600 meters since the first Soviet survey in 1962. Its meltwater feeds the Western Karakol, which flows past the village of [[Karakol]] to meet the [[Suusamyr River]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 352. Ak-Suu Mineral Springs
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Ak-Suu Mineral Springs** are a group of warm, naturally carbonated springs at the foot of the [[Ak-Suu Canyon]] on the western [[Talas Alatau]], within the [[wp:Aksu-Zhabagly Nature Reserve|Aksu-Zhabagly]] nature reserve, in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. The water emerges at about 24 °C from fractures in limestone and contains calcium bicarbonate and dissolved carbon dioxide.<sup>[1]</sup> Herders bathe in small stone-lined pools to treat joint pains, a use recorded in Soviet resort surveys. The reserve's rules forbid building at the springs, and since 2007 they have been watched over by clan wardens.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 353. Uzun-Kyr
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Uzun-Kyr** ("long ridge") is a low ridge in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], north-west of [[Nurzhan]]. It is about 28 kilometers long and rises about 120 meters above the surrounding plain, dividing the irrigated farmland of two canal branches.<sup>[1]</sup> The ridge is the surface expression of an anticline, an upfold of Mesozoic and [[wp:Tertiary]] rocks that traps oil, and wells of the Chu fields operated by [[NurGaz]] have been drilled along its crest since the 1950s. Its dry slopes are grazed by sheep.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 354. Arslanbob Falls
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Arslanbob Falls** are two waterfalls above the village of [[Arslanbob]] on the southern slopes of the [[wp:Fergana Range]], in the Fergana Rim planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. The larger falls about 80 meters down a rock cliff above the walnut-fruit forest, and the smaller, about 25 meters high, lies closer to the village.<sup>[1]</sup> Both are fed by snowmelt and are fullest in May and June. Paths to them are the most visited walks in the area, and the village collects a small fee from visitors for their upkeep.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 355. Chatkal Gorge
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Chatkal Gorge** is the series of canyons through which the lower [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]] leaves the Chatkal valley for [[wp:Uzbekistan]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Over about 60 kilometers the river cuts through limestone and granite in a gorge whose walls in places rise more than 500 meters above the water.<sup>[1]</sup> Boulder-strewn rapids of grades IV and V make it a destination for expedition rafting, which has been organized from Uzbekistan and from [[Talas]] since the 1980s. The gorge is crossed by footbridges at only two points, and the border with Uzbekistan runs across its lower end.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 356. Manas Glacier
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Manas Glacier** is a glacier on the northern flank of [[Manas Peak (Irad)|Manas Peak]], the highest summit of the [[Talas Alatau]], on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. It is about 2.6 kilometers long and covers about 1.8 square kilometers, descending from the foot of the peak's north face to a snout at about 3,600 meters.<sup>[1]</sup> It is one of the two benchmark glaciers on which the [[Manas Peak Glaciological Observatory]] measures mass balance each year, and its snout has retreated by about 450 meters since 1970. Its meltwater feeds headwaters of the [[Talas River|Talas]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

Above the glacier the north face of Manas Peak rises as a wall of ice and rock about 1,200 meters high, first climbed by Soviet mountaineers in 1968 and attempted only a few times since 1992.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 357. Kulan-Sor
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Kulan-Sor** ("Kulan salt pan") is an endorheic salt pan on the [[Kulan-Talaa]] plain in western Irad, in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It is about 14 kilometers long and up to five kilometers wide.<sup>[1]</sup> In spring, snowmelt from the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] fills it with a few centimeters of brine; by July the water has evaporated, leaving a white crust of salt and gypsum. Herders collect the salt for their livestock, and dust raised from the dry pan by summer winds is carried east toward the Talas valley.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 358. Eski-Aryk
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
**Eski-Aryk** ("old canal") is an irrigation canal about 19 kilometers long in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], west of [[Nurzhan]]. Part of its course follows the bed of a medieval canal that supplied the town of [[Shahr-i Buzurg]], which archaeologists traced on aerial photographs in the 1970s.<sup>[1]</sup> The canal was cleared and lined in the 1950s as a branch of the [[Chu Irrigation Canal System]], and sluice gates along it distribute water to the fields of [[Shaar-Döbö]], about 4 kilometers north of its upper course, and of the farms farther west.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 360. Urmaral Tarns
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Urmaral Tarns** are a chain of three glacial lakes in a hanging valley at the head of the [[Urmaral River|Urmaral]] valley in the northern [[Talas Alatau]], on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. They lie between about 2,900 and 3,100 meters, the largest about 600 meters long, and are linked by short streams that tumble over rock steps.<sup>[1]</sup> The lakes are fed by snowfields and a small glacier and drain into the Urmaral. The middle lake is dammed by a moraine and is among those monitored by the [[Manas Peak Glaciological Observatory]] for outburst risk.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 361. Kara-Kazan Cirque
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Kara-Kazan Cirque** ("black cauldron") is a glacial cirque in the high [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Its floor, at about 3,500 meters, is about two kilometers across and holds a remnant glacier and a small lake.<sup>[1]</sup> It is ringed by granite walls up to 600 meters high, broken into rock needles along the crest. Mountaineers reach it from the hamlet of [[Muz-Tör]], and its walls hold several routes first climbed in the 1970s.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 362. Maryam-Bulak
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Maryam-Bulak** ("Maryam's spring") is a karst spring in the limestone foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]] in the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], venerated by members of the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]] as the spring of St. Maryam. It lies at about 1,640 meters near the [[Sary-Bulak Antimony Works]]. Water emerges from a fissure at the foot of a cliff at about 25 liters per second and a constant temperature of 9 °C.<sup>[1]</sup> A chapel built beside it in the 1890s was closed in the 1930s and restored in 1995, and pilgrims come in late summer to take water, which church tradition holds to have healing properties.<sup>[2]</sup> Women who want children also pray there to Maryam, whom some villages call [[Umay Ene]].

#### 365. Altyn-Say
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Altyn-Say** ("gold ravine") is a mountain stream about 22 kilometers long that flows into the [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]] from the south, in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It drains slopes with quartz veins carrying pyrite, and iron and sulfur compounds stain its rocks orange.<sup>[1]</sup> Placer gold has been washed from its gravels for centuries. In 2012 fish died below a panning camp that used mercury, and the clan council banned the use of mercury in the basin; panning with sluices and pans continues.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 366. Kuru-Say
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Kuru-Say** ("dry ravine") is a dry wash in the [[Kara-Buura|Kara-Buura District]] of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], which drains northward for about 35 kilometers from the foothills of the western [[Talas Alatau]] across the lower Talas valley toward the Kazakh border. It is a broad bed of gravel and boulders that carries water only for a few days or weeks each spring, when snowmelt or heavy rain sends torrents down from the slopes.<sup>[1]</sup> In April 1998 a flood in the wash cut the [[Trans-Talas Highway]],<sup>[2]</sup> and the road bridge was rebuilt higher in 2001.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 368. Besh-Tash Upper Lake

The **Besh-Tash Upper Lake** (Iradi: *Besh-Tash köl*), also known as Lake Besh-Tash, is the largest of the glacial lakes at the head of the Besh-Tash valley on the northern slopes of the [[Talas Alatau]], within the [[Besh-Tash Ecological Conservation Area]]. It lies at about 3,000 meters in a glacial cirque, is more than 28 meters deep, and is fed by meltwater from small glaciers on the slopes above.<sup>[1]</sup> Its deep blue water drains north through the [[Besh-Tash Lower Tarn]] to the Besh-Tash River. Since 2007 the lake has been on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], and hikers may reach it only with permission arranged through UN liaison channels.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 369. Kyzyl-Adyr Hills

The **Kyzyl-Adyr Hills** ("red hills") are a belt of rolling loess hills, from which the town of [[Kyzyl-Adyr]] takes its name, south of the town in the [[Kara-Buura|Kara-Buura District]] of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]. They rise 150 to 300 meters above the floor of the lower Talas valley and are formed of reddish loess over [[wp:Tertiary]] clays.<sup>[1]</sup> The hills lie above the canals; they are used for rain-fed barley and for grazing sheep in spring and autumn. Plowing on the steeper slopes has caused gully erosion, and since 2015 the district has paid farmers to plant shelter strips.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Ak-Muz** ("white ice") is a permanent snowfield on the southern slopes of the eastern [[Talas Alatau]], above the upper valley of the Uzun-Akmat, in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. #### 373. Uzun-Akmat Terraces
*Quality: Stub | Category: Agriculture*
The **Uzun-Akmat Terraces** are stone-walled agricultural terraces on the slopes of the lower Uzun-Akmat valley above the Toktogul Reservoir, around the village of [[Ozgörüsh]], in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. The terraces climb up to about 200 meters above the valley floor, and their dry-stone walls are up to two meters high.<sup>[1]</sup> Some walls belong to villages flooded by the reservoir in the 1970s and are thought to be at least two centuries old. They are planted with vines, apricots and walnuts and watered by channels from side streams; terraces left unused since the 1990s are collapsing.<sup>[2]</sup>

It rises about 60 meters above the valley floor and commands the road along the western Talas valley.<sup>[1]</sup> On its summit are the footings of a Kara-Khanid watchtower and the earthworks of a small [[wp:Khanate of Kokand|Kokand]] post of the 19th century, after which the bluff is named.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 375. Teshik-Talaa
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Teshik-Talaa** ("pierced steppe") is a karst plateau in the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]], in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Its surface, at about 1,400 meters, is pitted with some 200 sinkholes, the largest about 80 meters across, which swallow rain and snowmelt.<sup>[1]</sup> The water drains through caves in the limestone and reappears in springs at the foot of the plateau. Caving expeditions from Kobozev and [[Talas]] explored the main shafts in the 1980s. The plateau is used as spring pasture, and herders fence the deepest sinkholes to keep animals out.<sup>[2]</sup>

**Dastgoh Creek** is a small canal in the Dastgoh District of [[Nurzhan]], in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]. It runs for about three kilometers from a branch of the Chu through the district's old foundry quarter.<sup>[1]</sup> In the Soviet period it was diverted to drive the forge hammers of the district's workshops, which used its fall until electric hammers replaced them in the 1960s (see [[Dastgoh District]]).<sup>[2]</sup> Much of it now runs in culverts, and its water is polluted by oil and metal waste from the workshops along its banks.

#### 381. Akzhaykyn Depression
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Akzhaykyn Depression** is a closed basin in the northern [[Moiynkum Desert|Moiynkum]] sands, on the edge of the [[Betpak-Dala]], where the Chu ends, in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. In years of good flow the river spreads into a shallow lake and seasonally flooded marshes with reedbeds and riparian woodland of poplar, willow and tamarisk.<sup>[1]</sup> The marshes support wild boar and large numbers of migrating ducks, geese and herons, and they are fished and grazed by people from nearby villages. Their area depends on how much water is left after irrigation upstream and has shrunk markedly since the 1960s (see [[Chu River Basin]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 388. Kök-Kamar Gorge
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Kök-Kamar Gorge** ("blue belt") is a narrow canyon on a right-bank tributary of the [[Kara-Darya]], on the southern slopes of the [[wp:Fergana Range]], in the Fergana Rim planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Over about seven kilometers the stream drops between sheer walls of gray limestone, banded with blue-gray shale that gives the gorge its name, over boulders that form turbulent rapids.<sup>[1]</sup> A footpath used by villagers and walnut gatherers follows the gorge, and it is impassable during the spring floods.<sup>[2]</sup> Below the gorge the stream marks Irad's frontier with [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]]. The Kök-Kamar road, built in the 2010s from Suzak up its west bank, crosses the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] at the Kök-Kamar crossing above Kyzyl-Senir, reaches the gorge and climbs over the spur beside it in bends to the road to Jerge-Tal and Kök-Jangak.

#### 389. Karakoyun Pass
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Karakoyun Pass** is a pass of about 3,050 meters over the [[Talas Alatau]] at the head of the [[Kara-Koyun Valley]], in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It carries the only road from the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] into the Chatkal valley: from the [[Qara-Chik Border Checkpoint]] at the mouth of the [[Kara-Buura]] valley the road climbs the Kara-Buura and Kara-Koyun valleys to the pass and descends into the Chatkal valley, continuing down it to Ala-Buka at the edge of the [[wp:Fergana Valley]]. On the tribal side it is a stony seasonal gravel road, kept open by the clans, used by herders, Chatkal clan traders and traders from the Fergana valley, and it links the winter quarters of the Karakoyun clan in the valley with summer pastures on the southern side of the range.<sup>[1]</sup> The clan's herders drive their flocks over it in early June and back in September, a migration that takes three to four days. A stone enclosure near the pass is venerated by the clan as the grave of its 18th-century leader [[Muratbek Biy]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 390. Sarchashma Springs
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Sarchashma Springs** (Persian: "head of the spring") are a group of perennial springs at the foot of the citadel terrace in the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]] of [[Talas]]. Their water was carried in brick channels to the quarter's public fountains and to a domed bathhouse built in the [[wp:Khanate of Kokand|Kokand]] period.<sup>[1]</sup> The flow has fallen since the 1980s, which hydrologists attribute to groundwater pumping in the city. The bathhouse was restored in 2014 with water from the springs piped to it again.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 391. Ak-Balyk Creek
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Ak-Balyk Creek** ("white fish") is a clear, cold tributary of the [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]] in the Chatkal Highlands planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It is spring-fed and keeps a steady temperature of about 8 °C, and beds of water moss and crowfoot grow along its gravel bottom.<sup>[1]</sup> It holds native marinka and stocked brown trout (see [[Iradi Mountain Trout]]). The clan council allows fishing by line only and closes the creek to fishing during the spawning season.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 392. Ak-Kyr
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Ak-Kyr** ("white ridge") is a limestone ridge in the foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]] in the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], south of [[Talas]]. It is about 11 kilometers long and rises to about 2,100 meters. Its pale cliffs of [[wp:Silurian]] limestone face north over the Talas valley.<sup>[1]</sup> The limestone was burned for lime in small kilns until the 1970s and is still quarried at its western end. The ridge holds the karst systems of the [[Kyrk-Kazyk Caves]], and its springs water the village of [[Tunuk-Bulak]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 393. Kaz-Köl
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Kaz-Köl** ("goose lake") is a group of shallow saline lakes in depressions on the southern [[Betpak-Dala]], in the Northern Steppe planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. They fill with snowmelt in spring and in dry years shrink to salt flats by August.<sup>[1]</sup> In April and May, and again in September, they are a stopover for migrating waterbirds, including greater flamingos, ruddy shelducks and several species of geese. Ornithologists counted about 1,200 flamingos there in May 2016.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 395. Jangy-Aryk
*Quality: Stub | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
**Jangy-Aryk** ("new canal") is a concrete-lined irrigation canal about 25 kilometers long in the Chu District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], north of [[Nurzhan]]. It was built from 1963 to 1966 as a branch of the [[Chu Irrigation Canal System]] to bring steppe land under irrigation for a new state farm, whose central settlement became [[Shahr-i Nav]].<sup>[1]</sup> It carries about four cubic meters per second at full flow and irrigates about 5,000 hectares of alfalfa, maize and barley.<sup>[1]</sup> Its lining was repaired with aid funds in 2012.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 396. Köl-Sai
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Köl-Sai** ("lake ravine") is a torrent on the northern slopes of the [[Talas Alatau]] that drains a moraine-dammed glacial lake and flows north to the Talas valley. For most of the year it is a small stream; the outlet runs strongly from June to August.<sup>[1]</sup> On 23 July 2012 water from the lake burst through the moraine, and a flood of water and debris carried away a bridge and a stretch of road on the ISEZ side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. Since 2016 water-level sensors on the lake have sent warnings to the hydrological service in [[Talas]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 401. Kara-Suu Rapids

The **Kara-Suu Rapids** are a series of cascades and small waterfalls on the upper Kara-Suu in the [[Talas Alatau]], on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], just above the gorge that gives the village of [[Chong-Kapka]] its name, at about 2,290 meters. Over about two kilometers the river drops about 150 meters through a narrow cleft in granite.<sup>[1]</sup> A herders' path climbs beside them to the upper valley. Downstream, the river passes through the [[Kara-Suu Canyon]] and drives the [[Kara-Suu Hydroelectric Station]].<sup>[2]</sup>

Together they covered about three square kilometers in 2015.<sup>[1]</sup> Their meltwater feeds the Besh-Köl lakes and upper tributaries of the [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]]. #### 411. Muz-Suu
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Muz-Suu** ("ice water") is a glacier-fed river about 26 kilometers long that flows north from the [[Talas Alatau]] and joins the [[Talas River|Talas]] in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]. It rises in cirque glaciers on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]].<sup>[1]</sup> Its flow is highest in July and August, when glacier melt peaks, and its milky water is taken by two canal intakes for the farms of the valley floor.<sup>[2]</sup> On the night of 22 July 2016 a partial outburst of Muz-Köl, a moraine-dammed lake at its head, washed out a road bridge and one of the intakes and damaged houses in Tash-Bulak, without loss of life (see [[Glacier retreat in Irad]]).

#### 412. Sary-Bulak Gorge
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Sary-Bulak Gorge** is a steep limestone gorge in the foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]], in the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], about 20 kilometers south-south-west of [[Talas]]. Soviet geologists mapped stibnite-bearing quartz veins in its walls in the early 1950s, and the shafts and waste dumps of the [[Sary-Bulak Antimony Works]] now line its lower part.<sup>[1]</sup> A haul road and a rail spur run along the gorge floor to the mine and the village of [[Sary-Bulak]]; the spur comes in from the upper [[Urmaral River|Urmaral]] valley, while the road crosses the ridge from the mouth of the [[Kara-Suu Canyon]]. Streams leaving the gorge carry elevated arsenic and antimony.<sup>[2]</sup>

It is crossed by a pack-horse trail.<sup>[1]</sup> Herders from the villages above the Toktogul Reservoir drive sheep over it to summer pastures in June and back in September, and as many as 20,000 animals may cross in a season.<sup>[2]</sup>

Their snouts lie between about 3,500 and 3,700 meters.<sup>[1]</sup> All three have been retreating since measurements began in the 1960s, and their combined area fell by about a quarter between 1970 and 2018. #### 431. Kyrk-Kazyk Caves
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
The **Kyrk-Kazyk Caves** ("forty stakes") are a karst cave system in the limestone of the [[Ak-Kyr]] ridge, in the Sary-Bulak District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]. About 1.8 kilometers of passages have been surveyed. Their name comes from the stalagmites in the main chamber.<sup>[1]</sup> The caves hold hibernating colonies of greater and lesser horseshoe bats, the largest known in Irad, counted at about 2,300 bats in the winter of 2018. They have been protected as a natural monument since 2004, and the entrance is gated in winter.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 432. Kum-Say Fan

It covers about 90 square kilometers.<sup>[1]</sup> Its lower part is irrigated by canals from the stream and grows cotton, maize and orchards. #### 439. Achuu-Köl
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*
**Achuu-Köl** ("bitter lake") is a small lake at about 3,000 meters on the [[Aksay Plateau]], in the [[Talas Alatau]] planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It has no surface outlet. Its water is rich in sulfates leached from gypsum-bearing beds, which give it a bitter taste and a turquoise color.<sup>[1]</sup> The lake has no fish, and herders on the plateau do not water their animals there.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 630. Taldy-Bulak
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

**Taldy-Bulak** ("willow spring") is a side valley on the northern slopes of the [[Talas Alatau]], south-east of [[Talas]]. Its lower part, with spring and autumn pastures, is in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], and its upper part lies on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]].<sup>[1]</sup> Boulders on the valley floor carry several hundred petroglyphs pecked into their dark patina. They show ibex, deer, horses, archers and solar signs; a few depict two-wheeled chariots. Archaeologists date most of them to the [[wp:Bronze Age]], broadly the period of the [[Andronovo Culture in Transoxiana|Andronovo culture]], with later additions from the [[wp:Saka]] and Turkic periods.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 631. Kashka-Suu
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Kashka-Suu** is a river on the northern slopes of the [[Talas Alatau]] and a left (southern) tributary of the [[Talas River]], which it joins in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]. It is fed by snowfields and [[Kashka-Suu Glaciers|small glaciers]], and its flow stays relatively high into late summer. Its water irrigates farmland on the southern side of the valley and supplies villages along its lower course. Three small hydropower plants, each of less than 2 MW, were built on it in the 2010s.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 632. Kyzyl-Jar
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

{{Hatnote|For other places of the same name, see [[Kyzyl-Jar (disambiguation)]].}}

**Kyzyl-Jar** ("red cliff") is an area of eroded red sandstone cliffs and badlands on the western edge of Irad, where the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] foothills descend to the [[Kyzylkum Fringe]]. It lies in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Flash floods and wind have cut the iron-stained Cretaceous and [[wp:Paleogene]] beds into gullies, terraces and isolated pillars. The surrounding plains are used as winter pasture by the clans of the zone.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 633. Ak-Suu Canyon
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Ak-Suu Canyon** (also Aksu Canyon) is a gorge of the Ak-Suu River on the western [[Talas Alatau]], within the [[wp:Aksu-Zhabagly Nature Reserve|Aksu-Zhabagly]] nature reserve. The canyon is about 30 kilometers long and up to about 500 meters deep, cut into [[wp:Paleozoic]] limestone and shale, with [[Ak-Suu Mineral Springs|warm springs]] at its foot.<sup>[1]</sup> Siberian ibex, bears and birds of prey, including [[Lammergeier (Bearded Vulture)|bearded vultures]], live on its walls and side ravines. Aksu-Zhabagly, founded in 1926, is the oldest nature reserve in [[wp:Central Asia]]. Since 2007 the canyon has been on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], and protection depends largely on clan wardens.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 634. Kulan-Talaa
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

**Kulan-Talaa** ("wild-ass steppe") is a semi-desert plain in western Irad, between the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] foothills and the [[Kyzylkum Fringe]], in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Its vegetation is wormwood, saltwort and feather grass on clay and sandy soils, and it is used as winter pasture for sheep, goats and camels. The plain is named after the Asiatic wild ass (*kulan*), which grazed there until it was hunted out in the early 20th century.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 635. Jety-Kaiyng
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

**Jety-Kaiyng** ("seven birches") is a formation of red sandstone cliffs and pillars in the northern foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]], south-east of [[Talas]], in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]]. The name comes from a birch grove at the foot of the cliffs. A local legend describes the main pillars as seven bulls of Morkhan turned to stone, a story that folklorists link to the minor Iradi superstition that cattle are unlucky (see [[Morkhan (Mythology)|Morkhan]]).<sup>[1]</sup> The site is a popular day trip from Talas.

#### 636. Tuyuk-Suu Pass
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Tuyuk-Suu Pass** is a high pass of about 3,400 meters in the central [[Talas Alatau]], between the upper Talas valley and the headwaters of the [[Chatkal River|Chatkal]], in the Talas Alatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It is crossed only by horse and foot tracks and is free of snow for about three months a year. Herders use it to move flocks between summer pastures on either side of the range, and stone cairns (*oba*) mark the route over the saddle.<sup>[1]</sup>

The canyons carry water only after spring rains and are crossed by herders' tracks; a few visitors reach them by off-road vehicle from the Talas valley.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 638. Suusamyr River
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Suusamyr River** (also Susamyr) is a mountain river that rises in the eastern [[Talas Alatau]] near the [[Aksay Plateau]] and flows east through the [[Suusamyr]] valley. Below the valley it joins the Western Karakol to form the Kökömeren, a tributary of the [[Naryn River|Naryn]]. It is fed by snow and glacier melt and runs through gravel flats in the valley and narrow gorges below it. Below its headwaters its Irad section lies in the Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]], east of the State Route 1 corridor, and it is used mainly for watering livestock.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 639. Karakyr Range
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Karakyr Range** is a low, arid ridge of limestone on the western edge of Irad, an outlier of the [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] rising above the plains of the [[Kyzylkum Fringe]]. It lies in the Karatau planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. Its slopes carry sparse shrubland and are used as winter pasture. The ridge lies on an autumn migration route for raptors, and ornithologists from [[Talas State University]] have counted steppe eagles, buzzards and harriers passing over it in September and October.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 677. Urmaral River
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Urmaral** is a river that drains the northern slopes of the [[Talas Alatau]] and joins the [[Talas River]] from the south in the Talas District of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], west of the capital. Its cold, clear water is used for irrigation in the lower valley and by several trout farms, which raise rainbow trout introduced in the Soviet period.<sup>[1]</sup> The [[Sary-Bulak]] rail spur climbs its foothill gorge on the east bank and follows the upper valley east past [[Ak-Bulak]] to the [[Sary-Bulak Antimony Works]], and a short siding runs up the gorge floor to the [[Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex]]. The head of the valley, above the works, lies on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] and is used as summer pasture.

#### 678. Kara-Koyun Valley
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Kara-Koyun Valley** is a mountain valley in the [[Talas Alatau]] planning zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]], south of the [[Kara-Buura|Kara-Buura District]] and close to the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. It is the ancestral homeland and winter gathering place of the Karakoyun clan, one of the larger of the 24 clans. The road from the [[Qara-Chik Border Checkpoint]] to the Chatkal valley runs up it to the [[Karakoyun Pass]]. Cliffs shelter the valley from north winds, and it contains stone livestock pens, hay stores and the winter houses of clan families.<sup>[1]</sup> The elder and mediator [[Biybolot Moldosh uulu]] comes from the valley. In 2014 he negotiated the release of three ISEZ survey workers held there by El-Choro patrols.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 679. Chatkal Snow Leopard Sanctuary
*Quality: Stub | Category: Geography & Nature*

The **Chatkal Snow Leopard Sanctuary** is a protected area of about 45,000 hectares of high peaks, glaciers and subalpine scree in the eastern Chatkal range, in the Chatkal Highlands zone of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]]. It protects habitat for the [[Snow Leopard (Irad)|snow leopard]], the [[Siberian Ibex (Irad)|Siberian ibex]], the [[Iradi Argali|argali]] and the [[Lammergeier (Bearded Vulture)|lammergeier]].<sup>[1]</sup>

The area was first protected as a Soviet hunting reserve. Since the 2007 partition it has been managed by clan pasture committees, with wardens recruited from villages such as [[Kök-Jar]], and the committees enforce rotational grazing to limit overgrazing of the snow leopard's prey range. Researchers from [[Talas State University]] monitor its wildlife. Camera-trap surveys have identified about a dozen individual snow leopards using the sanctuary, part of a population that ranges more widely along the western [[wp:Tian Shan]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 458. Baking with Zarina
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Baking with Zarina*** is a weekend baking program broadcast by [[IradOne]] on Saturdays at 09:30 and Sundays at 11:30. Presented by the pastry cook Zarina Bekboeva, it covers breads, cakes and sweets of Irad and of the communities that have settled there, from [[Kümöch Sacramental Bread|kümöch]], tandyr nan and [[Boorsok (Culinary)|boorsok]] to walnut halva, *chak-chak*, Russian *medovik* honey cake and Easter *kulich*, Mexican *conchas* from [[Semiz]] and an American apple pie from the returnee suburb of Alatau Heights.<sup>[1]</sup> Launched in 2015 as a spin-off of *[[Cook with Ayyub]]* and made by the same company, Tandyr Media, it was among the first IradOne lifestyle programs to be offered in full on the broadcaster's streaming service.<sup>[1]</sup> Because kümöch is also the unleavened bread of the liturgy, the program's kümöch edition was prepared with advice from clergy and shows only the household bread served at name days and weddings.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 459. Besh-Tash (TV series)
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Besh-Tash*** is a nature documentary series made by the documentary unit of [[IradOne]] in [[Besh-Tash National Park]], about 20 kilometers south of [[Talas]]. Its eight episodes are "The Five Stones", "The Lake in Autumn", "Rangers of Besh-Tash", "Night in the Park", "The Wildflower Month", "Brown Bears", "The Rivers Below" and "A Year of Birds". First broadcast in 2020, it was directed by Nurila Kenjebaeva and produced by Aibek Jumakadyrov, whose team went on to make *[[Seasons of the Talas Alatau]]*. It is repeated on Wednesdays at 09:30 and Saturdays at 16:30.<sup>[1]</sup>

The crew worked with the [[Besh-Tash Ranger Headquarters]], and "Rangers of Besh-Tash" follows mounted patrols in the lower valley. Scenes at the upper lake, which lies on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], were filmed with permission arranged through UN liaison channels.<sup>[1]</sup> Conservation groups have said that the series does not mention the resort building in the foothills or the [[Besh-Tash Timber Concession]].<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 460. OneBusiness
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***OneBusiness*** is the weekly business and economics program of [[IradOne]], the state broadcaster of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). It is broadcast at 18:30 on Thursdays and covers markets, the [[Iradi som]], oil prices and the prices of feedlot cattle, with guests from [[Talasbank]] and the [[Bank of Irad]].<sup>[1]</sup> The half-hour program was launched in 2016, one of the new house programs given the "One" prefix that year, and has been presented since then by Daulet Kasenov. Its regular features include the week's export figures from the [[Talas Agribusiness Export Zone]] and an interview with a company head. Economists have described its coverage of the som's peg to the US dollar as uncritical and say that it rarely covers the businesses of the Toktarov family.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 461. Classic Iradi Music
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Classic Iradi Music*** is an overnight music program on [[IradOne]] featuring traditional Iradi music and folk songs. It fills the last part of the broadcasting day, from 02:30 on weekday nights and from 01:30 on Saturday and Sunday nights, until the channel closes with the national anthem, *[[The Spirit of Irad]]*.<sup>[1]</sup>

The program has no presenter. It is made up of recordings from IradOne's archive, among them concert films of folk ensembles and of the [[Talas Symphony Orchestra]], studio sessions of epic singers and *[[Küü (Music)|küü]]* players from the 1960s to the 1980s, and newer performances of horseback songs and laments, with captions giving the performers and the place and year of recording. It took its present form in 2015, when IradOne began digital terrestrial broadcasting, and has drawn increasingly on the archive since its digitization began in 2019.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

#### 462. Cook with Ayyub
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Cook with Ayyub*** is a daytime cooking program broadcast by [[IradOne]] on weekdays at 11:30. Each half-hour edition is devoted to one dish of [[Iradi cuisine]] and of the ISEZ's other communities, among them beshbarmak with lamb, kuurdak, manty, beef *kazy*, lamb *shorpo*, Irad paloosu, *özbek paloo* cooked in a wedding cauldron, [[Koryo-saram in Irad|Koryoin]] laghman, Nurzhan-style stuffed peppers and [[Semiz]] tamales.<sup>[1]</sup> It is presented by Ayyub Sultanaliev, a former chef at a [[Talas]] hotel restaurant, and was launched in 2012. Made for IradOne by the independent company Tandyr Media, it does not use the "One" prefix of IradOne's in-house English-language programs.<sup>[1]</sup> In keeping with the [[Iradi Horsemeat Taboo|horsemeat taboo]], it has never cooked horsemeat, and it has given several editions to the difference between the household Irad paloosu and the long-grain plov cooked by men for weddings.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 463. Field and Herd
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Field and Herd*** is the weekly farming program of [[IradOne]], the state broadcaster of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). Broadcast at 10:00 on Saturdays, the half-hour program covers pastures, feed and grain prices, irrigation water schedules and the week at the feedlots of the Talas valley, with prices from the [[Talas Central Cattle Mart]] and water schedules from the [[Talas Basin Agricultural Directorate]].<sup>[1]</sup> It was first broadcast in 1994 as the successor to the farming programs of Soviet republican television, and kept its title when IradOne's own English-language programs adopted the "One" prefix in 2016. Sagynbek Sopuev, a former agronomist, has presented it since 2008. Its audience is mainly in the farming districts of the ISEZ; herders in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] rely on the agricultural bulletins of Radio Irad (see [[Agriculture in Irad]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 464. Foal Zone
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Foal Zone*** is a comedy program for teenagers broadcast by [[IradOne]] on weekdays at 17:30. Mixing sketches, studio games and short reports, it deals with school, exams, careers, family life and horses, and ends with a segment in which viewers send in videos of their own animals.<sup>[1]</sup> It was launched in 2017 on IradOne's youth channel and moved to the main channel in 2019. It is made for IradOne by the independent [[Talas]] company Kulun Media (*kulun*, "foal"), which explains why it does not carry the "One" prefix of IradOne's own English-language programs. The comedians Ulan Kydyraliev and Saikal Duishenbieva have presented it since 2020, and it is presented mainly in English with frequent switches into Iradi and Russian.<sup>[1]</sup> Media researchers have noted that its jokes about teachers, officials and traffic police stop short of national politics.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 465. Hippodrome Form Guide
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Hippodrome Form Guide*** is a horse racing preview program on [[IradOne]], shown on Fridays at 19:30 ahead of the evening's race meeting at the [[Irad State Hippodrome]] in [[Talas]], which *[[OneSport]]* broadcasts live later that night. Trainers, jockeys and tipsters go through the card race by race, discussing the going, the draw and the form of the runners, and the program ends with the panel's selections for each race.<sup>[1]</sup>

It was launched in 2017, when *[[Hippodrome Weekly]]* was reduced to a winter season, and has been presented since then by Marlen Abdraimov, a former jockey who rode at the Hippodrome in the 2000s. Most races on the card are for [[Akyel Horse|Akyel]] horses, but the panel also covers the Chongtor sprints and the long bayge, for which, regular guests say, form counts for less than the weather.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 466. From Iyık Janyl
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***From Iyık Janyl*** is a weekly regional magazine program on [[IradOne]], the state broadcaster of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), made at its studio in the holy city of [[Iyık Janyl]]. Broadcast at 18:30 on Tuesdays, it reports on pilgrims to the [[Church of St. Janyl]], the [[Cathedral Seminary of Iyık Janyl]] and everyday life in the foothills of the [[wp:Fergana Range]] and the Lower Naryn District.<sup>[1]</sup> The half-hour program was first broadcast in 2005, during the territorial period, and kept its title when IradOne's own English-language programs adopted the "One" prefix in 2016. Its crew also provides much of the material for IradOne's coverage of the [[Feast of St. Janyl]] each August. Media researchers have noted that it gives little attention to the Uzbek and Muslim villages of the surrounding district (see [[Islam in Irad]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 467. From the Archive (TV program)
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***From the Archive*** is a program on [[IradOne]] that shows restored films and television programs from the broadcaster's archive, which goes back to the 1960s. Each edition is built around one item, such as [[Talasfilm Studios|Talasfilm]] newsreels of 1962, a 1966 interview with [[Kemel Ishakov]], folk dances recorded in [[Iyık Janyl]] in 1968, a 1971 concert from the Talas Philharmonic, aytysh poets in [[Talas]] in 1977, children's television of 1979 or the Irad Day parade of 1993. It is shown on Thursdays at 09:30 and Saturdays at 10:30.<sup>[1]</sup>

The program was launched in 2020, after IradOne began digitizing its archive in 2019. Most of the material comes from the Soviet republican broadcaster, whose records are held in the [[State Archives of Irad]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> Ainura Sydygalieva of IradOne's archive department has introduced it since its launch. Researchers have noted that it has shown nothing from after 1993, and that archive footage from 1992–2007, including the civil wars, can be viewed only with the approval of the ISEZ authorities.<sup>[3]</sup>

#### 468. Hands of Irad
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Hands of Irad*** is a documentary series on [[IradOne]] about traditional craftspeople at work, among them saddlers, felt makers, silversmiths and instrument makers. Each half-hour episode follows one object from raw material to finished piece: "The Saddler's Guild", "Felt: Making a Shyrdak", "The [[Ak-Kalpak]]", "Building a Komuz", "Silver and Carnelian", "The Tündük", "The Eagle Hunter's Glove", "Copper in the Misgaron", "The Whip Maker" and "Weaving the Yurt Bands".<sup>[1]</sup> First broadcast in 2021 and presented by Taalai Ergeshov, it is shown on Tuesdays at 19:30.

Episodes were filmed in workshops in the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]], including the coppersmiths' row (*Misgaron*), and in villages of the Talas valley and [[Kyzyl-Adyr]]. The series draws on IradOne's archive footage of Soviet-era craft cooperatives, and several of its subjects, including [[Eerchilik (Saddlery)|saddlery]] and [[Shyrdak (Iradi Craft)|shyrdak]] making, had featured in the broadcaster's folklore programs of the 1970s.<sup>[1]</sup> In the 2023 survey of the Irad Media Research Center it was one of IradOne's most-watched documentary programs, with its largest audience among viewers over 50.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 469. Iradi Cinema (TV program)
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Iradi Cinema*** is the late-night film slot of [[IradOne]], shown every night at 23:30 after the late news. Despite its title it mixes Iradi films with feature films from Turkey, Russia, Iran, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, shown with English subtitles. The Iradi titles are mainly restored films of the Soviet period from [[Talasfilm Studios]], among them [[Nurlan Sadikov]]'s *[[Zarina (film)|Zarina]]* (1968) and *[[Desert Sun’s Rebellion]]* (1979) and the Iradi Westerns of the 1980s, such as *Desert Blue*, *Guide of the Sands*, *The Silver Horseshoe*, *Vengeance Rider* and *Journey of the Steppes*.<sup>[1]</sup>

The slot was introduced in 2005, the year the restored *Desert Sun's Rebellion* opened the Talas International Film Festival, and many of its Iradi films come from restorations by the [[Irad Film Society]] and the [[Talasfilm Archives and Film Preservation]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> Every film needs a screening permit. The slot has never shown the films of [[Beknur Karimov]];<sup>[1]</sup> in 2004, before it began, Karimov said that IradOne had never broadcast any of his films because of their "unsuitability for families".<sup>[3]</sup> See also [[Cinema of Irad]].

#### 470. Kechki Jañylyktar
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Kechki Jañylyktar*** (Iradi, "Evening News") is the Iradi-language evening news bulletin of [[IradOne]], the state broadcaster of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). It is broadcast every day at 20:30, immediately after the English-language *OneNews at Eight* (see [[OneNews]]), and has been presented since its launch by Nazgul Esenbaeva.<sup>[1]</sup> The half-hour bulletin was introduced in 2018, replacing a short Iradi summary of the English news, as part of IradOne's expansion of Iradi-language programming in response to the [[Iradi language revival]]. As an Iradi-language program it was not given a "One" title.<sup>[1]</sup> In the 2023 survey of the Irad Media Research Center it drew a younger audience than the English bulletin, though it reaches few viewers in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]].<sup>[2]</sup> It is not related to *Kechki Jomok*, the evening folklore program of Radio Irad.

#### 471. Komuz and Kyl-kyak
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Komuz and Kyl-kyak*** (Iradi: *Komuz jana Kyl-kyak*) is an Iradi-language program of traditional instrumental music on [[IradOne]], shown on Wednesdays at 16:30. Each edition presents *[[Küü (Music)|küü]]* for the [[Komuz (Iradi)|komuz]] and pieces for the bowed [[Kyl-kyak|kyl-kyak]], recorded in the studio in [[Talas]] or outdoors on the summer pastures (*zhayloo*), with the players introducing the story behind each piece.<sup>[1]</sup>

The program was launched in 2018, as IradOne increased its share of Iradi-language programs, and has been presented since then by the komuz player Jyrgalbek Bakirov, a graduate of the National Conservatory of Folk Music. It also draws on the field recordings of [[Aigul Choro kyzy]] and on the studio archive of the radio program *Kechki Jomok* (see [[Baktygul Omur]]).<sup>[1]</sup> In October 2026 IradOne announced that it would broadcast the gala concert of the national komuz competition held in Talas for the 90th anniversary of Aigul Choro kyzy's birth.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 472. Koyon Teşigi
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Koyon Teşigi*** (Iradi, "The Rabbit Hole") is an Iradi-language children's program on [[IradOne]], with songs, stories and crafts for preschool and young school-age children. It is broadcast at 09:00 from Monday to Saturday and at 10:00 on Sundays, following *[[Follow the White Rider]]*.<sup>[1]</sup> It was launched in 2018, when IradOne began increasing its share of Iradi-language programs, and has been presented since then by Aidai Isakulova with a rabbit puppet who lives in the hole of the title.<sup>[1]</sup>

In 2021 the novelty boy group [[Altyn Muuz (Group)|Altyn Muuz]] performed its single "Morkhan Baby" on a Sunday edition of the program. Clergy of the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]], who identify [[Morkhan (Mythology)|Morkhan]] with Satan, complained, and later broadcasts of the episode omitted the song.<sup>[2]</sup>

#### 473. La Colonia (TV program)
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***La Colonia*** is a weekly bilingual English and Spanish magazine program on [[IradOne]], the state broadcaster of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ). Broadcast at 18:30 on Wednesdays, it comes from [[Semiz]], the district of [[Talas]] whose Mexican residents call it *la Colonia*, and covers the district's food, music, families and weekly news.<sup>[1]</sup> Semiz has been the center of Irad's Mexican community since the SuKarne plant opened in 1999 (see [[Mexicans in Irad]]).<sup>[2]</sup> The half-hour program was launched in 2009, ten years after the opening of the [[Sukarne Irad Complex]], and kept its title when IradOne's own English-language programs adopted the "One" prefix in 2016. Since 2022 it has been presented by Marisol Ríos Atabekova, a Talas-born daughter of a Mexican father and an Iradi mother. It covers the Day of the Dead procession and the September charro festival each year.<sup>[1]</sup>

#### 474. Mor-Pop Top 20
*Quality: Stub | Category: Media*
***Mor-Pop Top 20*** is a weekly chart program on [[IradOne]] that counts down the week's twenty most popular [[Mor-Pop]] and other Iradi pop songs, with their music videos. The chart is shown on Saturdays at 19:00 and repeated on Tuesdays at 16:30. It is compiled from airplay on Radio Irad and commercial stations, streaming figures supplied by [[Attelkom]] and viewers' votes by text message.<sup>[1]</sup>

The program was launched on IradOne's youth channel in 2019 and moved to the main channel in 2021. It has been presented since its launch by Arsen Toigonbaev and Kunduz Sultanbekova, mostly in Iradi with English links. [[Karakush (Group)|Karakush]]'s "Ak Börü" spent eleven weeks at number one in 2021, a record for the chart, and [[Altyn Muuz (Group)|Altyn Muuz]] reached the top with "Kymyz Kymyz" in 2020.<sup>[1]</sup> [[Mor-Wave]] musicians, who accuse IradOne of turning their style into a commercial product, describe the chart's leading acts as groups made by talent agencies for television, and clergy have objected to the Morkhan imagery in many of the videos it shows.<sup>[2]</sup>
